report.summary: This release reorganizes how live collaboration works by moving it out of the editor core with a few small behavior tweaks, so sharing, syncing, and saving scenes need full retesting.
keyChanges: The collaboration runtime (room joining, broadcasting scene changes and pointer positions over encrypted transport, and remote-versus-local element reconciliation) was relocated from the core editor into the app's collaboration code; behavior is meant to be unchanged, but all live-sync paths should be re-verified.

Two pieces of bookkeeping left the broadcast routine in the move: the routine no longer records the last broadcasted/received scene version itself, and opening a room no longer triggers the immediate full-scene broadcast when a new user arrives, so late joiners and mid-session sync now depend on the relocated flow and must be tested with real multi-user sessions.

Scene restore now accepts null or missing data and returns an empty element list with default settings instead of failing, so fresh starts and imports with no content should load an empty, properly positioned canvas rather than erroring.

The live-collaboration dialog (start/stop session, the room link with its copy control, and the name field) moved along with the collaboration code and is still rendered from the editor's canvas-action area and the mobile menu, so its open, close, copy, and session start/stop behavior needs confirmation on both desktop and mobile.

The collaboration-link parser (which matches the strict #room=id,key hash format and now safely ignores an empty link), the per-message random encryption IV, AES-GCM key import, and the backend scene import with its failure alert were moved into the app data layer that creates collaboration links and imports or exports shareable scene data.

The default app state no longer contains the user's name or the collaboration flag, and the collaborators list moved to the end of the defaults; collaboration state is now managed by the collaboration feature rather than the app state.

When a scene is restored from a saved file or browser storage, the user name and collaboration flag are silently dropped even if the saved data still contains them, while the collaborators list is still restored.

Scene reset, which runs when joining a collaboration room and when clearing the canvas, still wipes all local elements and clears undo history so local drawings do not leak into a joined room, and it preserves the light/dark appearance setting.

The scene-update path now applies a collaborators list in addition to background color and elements, so remote collaborator pointers can be synced through scene updates, and applying scene data preserves the viewport width, height, and canvas offsets.

Shareable encrypted links (addresses ending in #json= followed by an id and key), legacy links that carry the id as a ?id= query parameter, and collaboration links (#room=...) are now loaded by the showcase app's own relocated loader: joining a collaboration room still resets the local drawing, fetches the stored room scene from cloud storage first, and otherwise waits for the live session to deliver it.

The confirmation asking whether to replace your current drawing when opening an external link is preserved, and rejoining the same collaboration room within 15 seconds still bypasses it; declining keeps your local drawing and clears the link from the address bar.

Every editor change now flows through a single handler that saves the drawing locally about 300 ms after the last edit (flushed when the window loses focus) and, during live collaboration, broadcasts the changes to other participants.
Changing the URL hash while the editor is open reloads the linked scene in place, but a hash change is ignored while the editor is still initializing.
The step that saved your collaboration display name to browser storage whenever it changed was removed, so display-name persistence now depends on other code and must be verified explicitly.

Collaboration machinery moved from the core editor into the app-level collaboration layer: periodic full-scene rebroadcasting, saving the shared room to the collaboration backend, updating the collaborator list when users join or leave, and the rules for opening a room link, including that reopening the same room within 15 seconds of leaving must reload it without the replace-scene prompt.

Pointer broadcasts no longer tell other collaborators which elements you have selected; remote cursors must keep displaying and moving without errors, and remote selection indication may legitimately disappear.

The in-editor room dialog (username entry, room create/destroy controls) is replaced by a collaboration button with a live collaborator-count badge and an active-session style, shown in both the desktop toolbar and the mobile canvas menu; it renders only when the host app supplies a click handler and delegates the dialog to the host.
A state-update batching helper used by nearly every input handler (drag, wheel, keyboard, copy/cut/paste, gestures, resize) moved to shared code; all interaction behavior should be unchanged.
When the editor is unmounted it no longer detaches the URL-hash and page-leave listeners itself, as cleanup moved to the host collaboration layer, which only matters for embedding scenarios.

Live collaboration plumbing was removed from the main editor component: creating the collaboration link, joining a room, applying other participants' drawing updates, showing their pointers and names, and the tab-close prompt that force-saved unsaved session edits all left the editor and are now expected to run through a dedicated collaboration controller, so share-link sessions must be retested end to end.

Editor state no longer contains the username or an is-collaborating flag, so browser-saved state and the clear-canvas reset no longer carry the username, while collaborator data remains excluded from saved state and exported files.
Re-initializing the scene when the page URL hash changes was removed from the editor, so loading a shared or session link into an already-open editor tab must be verified.

The public embeddable API changed shape: the component ref now delivers a ready promise plus history-clear, scroll-to-center, and scene-element access, width and height are optional, and initial data may be null or a promise.

The shared delay helper used for the local auto-save now safely ignores a flush when nothing is queued (previously it could run the save with no data), and the double-tap (300 ms) and touch-context-menu (500 ms) timers moved into shared constants with identical values.

Scene broadcasts between live collaborators now carry the element list supplied by the caller, and the tracked last-broadcast scene version is updated by the collaboration wrapper (including a throttled periodic whole-scene resync) instead of inside the broadcast sender; the version is no longer refreshed when the full scene is broadcast to a newly joined user.

The reconciliation safeguard that ignores incoming copies of elements the local user is currently editing, resizing, or dragging now reads a stored snapshot of editor state that is refreshed on each local change broadcast, instead of the live editor state, so the protection can behave differently if the snapshot is stale.

Session lifecycle behavior moved with the refactor: warning and saving when leaving a page mid-collaboration, tearing down the connection on unload, and maintaining the participant list should behave as before, but the event listener wiring changed and is regression-prone.

The selection information sent with each participant's pointer updates during live collaboration now comes from the editor's current selection state and falls back to an empty selection when that state is unavailable, so remote collaborators' selection highlighting is the behavior most likely to be affected.

The embeddable editor's public properties changed: the older username-update and reference-based properties were replaced by a scene reference, a collaboration-button handler that does nothing by default when not provided, a live-collaboration flag, and pointer-update handling, so integrations must pass the new properties for collaboration features to work.

Collaboration support code, including the room dialog, collaboration-link and encryption-key generation, and encrypted scene storage, was moved into the application's collaboration and data folders with no intended behavior change, and the embeddable editor package now also shares scene utilities with integrators, so existing live-session flows need only smoke testing.

Starting a live collaboration session puts a shareable collaboration link in the address bar, clears the drawing's undo history first so elements deleted before the session started are not persisted into the shared room, and connects to the collaboration server with a timeout fallback if no initial scene message arrives.

Scene changes sync in both directions: outgoing updates are broadcast only when the drawing's version is newer than the last version sent or received, incoming changes are merged with local elements and their version is recorded before applying so a received scene is not echoed back to others, and applying any remote update clears the local undo/redo stack (the initial load centers the view on the drawing).
Cursor presence is broadcast to other collaborators only while connected and while fewer than two pointers are active, so cursor updates pause during two-pointer gestures such as touch pinch.

The room dialog shows a start-session view until a session exists and, once active, a copy button for the link (copy failures surface an error dialog), a read-only link field that selects all its text when clicked, and a name field whose value is saved locally and shared with other collaborators; closing the dialog returns keyboard focus to the collaboration button.
Stopping the session restores the plain editor address, saves the shared room, and disconnects, after which the dialog shows the start-session view again.
qaChecks: Check that a user joining an in-progress session receives the full current drawing shortly after opening the collaboration link, including elements drawn before they joined, and that the participant count updates for everyone.

Verify that edits made by one participant (drawing, moving, resizing, deleting) appear on the other participants' canvases in both directions, including an element edited at the same moment by two users (one version of it must win deterministically and all screens should settle on it).

Confirm that collaborator pointers and name labels follow remote users live while they drag, and that reloading a participant's browser reattaches to the room with the scene intact rather than showing an error alert.
Test a session with content, close it on one side, and confirm remaining participants keep working and that a rejoining user syncs again.

Validate opening the app with cleared browser storage: the canvas should load empty with the viewport positioned normally (content centered when a scene exists), with no error or blank off-canvas view.

Confirm a shared scene link still loads the intended drawing, and that a link pointing at missing content shows the import-failure alert and leaves a usable empty canvas instead of hanging or crashing.
Verify importing a saved drawing file and dropping a drawing file onto the canvas both restore all elements and settings as before.
Confirm the dialog's two states render correctly: before a session it offers starting one, and during a session it shows the room link with the copy control and the name field.

Check copying the room link puts the correct URL on the clipboard and the input selects it, that typing a name is preserved and closes the dialog on Enter, and that closing the dialog dismisses it and returns focus to the collaboration button.
Ensure stopping the session ends collaboration and the dialog returns to its pre-session state.
Verify a valid collaboration link joins the room and loads its scene, and that a malformed link does not crash the app and simply loads the editor normally.
Ensure a saved file reopened restores both the drawing and the stored settings, since the restore step that feeds this flow now handles empty data differently.
Verify that opening a room link while a local drawing exists replaces the local scene with the room's content instead of merging both.
Confirm that as one participant draws or moves elements, the other participant sees the updates and the remote cursor pointers live.
Test joining a room, reloading the page, and reconnecting; the same scene should load without duplicated elements.
Check that a participant who leaves the room no longer shows a cursor for the remaining participants.
Verify a scene saved before the change, whose stored state still contains the user name and collaboration flag fields, opens without errors and shows all elements.
Test reloading the app after drawing; the previous session's elements, background color, and zoom should reappear.
Validate that restoring a scene that contains collaborator data does not break loading or leave stale collaborator cursors.
Verify clearing the canvas removes all elements and resets tool and selection state.
Confirm the light/dark appearance stays unchanged after the reset.
Check that undo history is cleared so undo does not bring back the cleared elements.
Verify exported PNG and SVG files match the on-canvas view, including the background color and element layout.
Test exporting after zooming in and panning; the exported file should still show the whole scene correctly, not just the current view.
Verify shapes drawn with the pointer appear exactly under the cursor, including near the top-left corner of the canvas.
Test drawing after resizing the browser window; elements should still land under the pointer.
Confirm that zooming and panning (mouse wheel, pinch, space-drag) keeps drawing positions aligned with the pointer.
Verify that a participant joining a collaboration link immediately sees the room's existing drawing, including content drawn before they joined.
Verify that edits made by one participant appear in the other participant's canvas within moments, without reloading.

Test leaving a collaboration room and reopening the same link within 15 seconds: the room should reload directly without the replace-your-drawing confirmation, while reopening the same link after more than 15 seconds with a local drawing on canvas should show that confirmation.
Ensure the display name you set for yourself in the collaboration session still appears after a full page reload and rejoining; report it if it resets to a default.
Verify that opening a #json= shareable link in a fresh tab reproduces the shared drawing exactly, with no import-failure alert.
Test a legacy link that uses the ?id= query parameter: the referenced drawing should still load.

Confirm that opening a shareable link while you already have a local drawing asks whether to replace it: accepting loads the shared drawing, and declining keeps your local drawing and clears the link from the address bar.
Verify that drawings saved before this update still reappear after a full page reload, since the saved-data storage keys were redefined during the move.

Ensure an edit made immediately before switching tabs or closing the window is not lost: the last edit should be present when you return, because pending saves are flushed when the window loses focus and otherwise complete about 300 ms after the last change.
Verify that changing the address-bar hash to another shareable link without reloading swaps the canvas to that linked drawing.
Test changing the hash while the editor is still initializing: the premature change should be ignored and the editor should finish loading normally without breaking.
Verify that with both users in the room, one user draws, moves, and deletes several elements while the other watches, and both canvases end up showing identical content.
Verify a third user joining mid-session receives the full current scene rather than a blank canvas.
Confirm the collaborator count and presence indicators update shortly after a user joins and again after they leave.

Test leaving a room and reopening the same collaboration link within 15 seconds: the room reloads without a replace-scene prompt; then reopen the same link more than 15 seconds after leaving and the prompt should appear before replacing the local scene.

Test moving your pointer around the canvas while one or more elements are selected: the other user still sees your cursor moving smoothly in the correct position, with no errors, missing cursors, or frozen pointer rendering.
Verify the collaboration button renders in the desktop toolbar and inside the mobile canvas menu, and clicking it opens the collaboration or share dialog provided by the host app.
Confirm the badge is hidden with zero collaborators and shows the exact participant count (for example 2 with two users in the room) during a session.
Ensure the button shows its actively-collaborating styling during a session and returns to normal after the session ends.

Test a rapid continuous sequence without pauses: drag an element, pan and zoom with the mouse wheel, double-click to type text, copy and paste it, and undo, confirming every action applies and the UI stays responsive with no stale or frozen panels.
Verify right-click context menu, window resize, dropping a file onto the canvas, and pinch gestures on a touch device all still work.
Verify that after the editor is unmounted, changing the URL hash and closing or refreshing the page produce no console errors and no leave-page warning caused by the removed editor.

Verify that opening the collaboration link in a second browser joins the session and shows the shared drawing, and that the loading overlay clears and the canvas becomes usable within a few seconds even when the first participant is idle (the old 5-second join fallback moved with this code).

Verify that a shape drawn by one participant appears on the other's canvas within seconds and that each participant's pointer and display name are visible and survive that participant reloading and rejoining (the username left editor state, so name persistence is at risk).

Confirm that receiving another participant's changes does not silently discard your own recent edits or break undo, then leave the session and rejoin through the same link and confirm the current scene reloads.

Test closing the tab immediately after making a change while collaborating: leaving may no longer show a confirmation prompt, so reopen the link and confirm the last change is still present in the shared scene.
Verify that navigating an already-open editor tab to a collaboration link joins that room instead of showing a stale or empty canvas.
Test navigating the same tab to a different shared-scene link and confirm the new scene loads and fully replaces the previous one.
Verify that after drawing and waiting briefly, reloading the page restores the drawing and its settings such as background color.

Test making a change and reloading the page immediately, then separately reloading with no changes at all: the drawing must be saved in the first case and no save error should occur in the second (the flush path changed).
Validate exporting the drawing to a file and importing it into a fresh browser: the content matches and no collaborator presence data is included in the file.
Confirm that clearing the canvas empties it, Undo brings the drawing back, and after clearing and reloading the page the canvas stays empty.
Verify the editor mounts and renders the provided scene when embedded without dimensions and with initial data supplied as null or as a promise.
Confirm the host-facing API still applies scene updates, resets the scene, clears history, returns scene elements, and reports readiness through the new ref shape.
Verify that a shape one participant drags appears on the other participants' canvases within a few seconds.

Check concurrent edits of the same shape: while participant A is mid-drag on a shape, have participant B move that same shape; A's drag should continue uninterrupted and, after both release, both canvases should show the same final position with no duplicated or reverted shape.
Validate that rapid consecutive edits from both participants (draw, move, delete) end with identical scenes on every canvas once edits settle.
Test a longer session with continuous editing from both sides and confirm the scenes stay consistent without flicker or sudden full-canvas redraws.
Confirm that a participant joining the shared session link after others have drawn receives the complete existing drawing rather than a blank canvas.
Check two participants joining at nearly the same time both receive the full scene without one overwriting the other's received content.

Ensure that closing the browser tab while collaborating with unsaved changes triggers the browser's leave prompt, and that after choosing to stay the changes are saved so reloading the session link still shows them.
Verify that after one participant closes the tab, that participant's cursor and name disappear from the remaining participants' canvases.
Confirm that when a new participant joins, existing users see that participant's cursor and name appear and follow their edits.

Verify that with one or more elements selected, participant A's pointer movements on participant B's screen still show A's selected elements highlighted and A's username, since selection data now comes from a new state source with an empty-selection fallback.
Ensure that selecting elements and immediately moving the pointer, before any other interaction, still transmits the selection to the other participant.
Verify that moving the pointer with nothing selected still updates the remote cursor normally and does not break the broadcast.
Verify that changing the username in the collaboration dialog still updates the name other participants see next to that participant's pointer, since username handling was rewired in this release.
Verify that starting a session produces a room link (the URL ends with #room=...) and a second browser opening that link joins the same session and shows the same drawing.

Verify that after both participants add changes (for example, a rectangle) and one leaves the session or closes the tab, reloading the room link in a fresh browser restores the latest saved scene, since the storage layer moved in this release.
Verify the editor loads and normal drawing works (create a shape, select and move it, undo) since the component's configuration wiring was renamed in this release.
Verify the collaboration entry point in the editor still opens the collaboration dialog, since its click handler is now a separate property that does nothing by default when not provided.
Check that an embedded editor instance still hands its host a working reference to the scene and drawing controls, since the reference type was renamed.
Verify that starting the session replaces the address bar with a shareable collaboration link and that the second user opening it sees the same drawing, centered on its content.
Check that the element deleted before the session started does not reappear in the joiner's view, since deleted content must not be saved into the shared room.
Confirm that with both users editing at once, each sees the other's changes without duplicated elements and without a received scene being echoed back to collaborators.
Test undo after a remote change arrives: the local undo/redo stack should be cleared, so undoing may not restore your last edit, which is the intended tradeoff.
Verify the copy button puts the collaboration link on the clipboard (paste it into a text editor and compare with the address bar) and that clicking inside the link field selects its full text.
Check that in a browser context where clipboard writing is blocked (for example Firefox on a non-HTTPS page), clicking copy shows an error dialog instead of failing silently.
Verify a name entered in the name field is shown to the other collaborator with their cursor and is still filled in after reloading the page, and that pressing Enter in the field closes the dialog.
Ensure closing the dialog returns keyboard focus to the editor control that opens the collaboration dialog.
Verify that stopping the session removes the room link from the address bar so it returns to the plain editor address.
Confirm the other participant sees that user leave, and reopening the dialog afterwards shows the start-session view so a new session can be created.
Verify that moving the mouse in one browser moves that collaborator's cursor in the other browser, labelled with the name they entered.
Confirm that elements selected by one collaborator appear highlighted as selected in the other user's view.
uncertainty: The moved collaboration code drops the in-broadcast recording of the last broadcasted/received scene version and the immediate full-scene broadcast on new-user arrival; if that bookkeeping was not fully re-homed, the visible symptom would be missed syncs or empty canvases for late joiners, so the multi-user checks above are the primary safety net.

Scenes and browser-stored state saved before this change keep the user name and collaboration flag in the app state, and the new code silently drops those fields on restore; if any remaining feature still reads them from the app state, it would now see them as missing, so watch for empty or missing name labels in collaboration features.

Continued support for legacy shareable links that put their id in the ?id= query parameter is not confirmed: the legacy backend address was removed from the old shared data module together with the loader, and the relocated loader's handling of these links could not be verified from the supplied evidence, so treat the legacy-link check as the watch item.

The receiving side of pointer broadcasts was not part of this group's evidence; since the sender no longer includes its selected elements, any remote selection display may silently stop updating, so watch for stale or incorrect remote selection highlights during pointer movement in a shared room.

This change set shows the collaboration plumbing removed from the main editor but not the replacement implementation, so the removed safety nets (the tab-close force-save and confirmation prompt, the 5-second fallback that cleared a stuck loading state when no initial room update arrived, and the 20-second full-scene resync interval) are the top unverified risk; if the new collaboration controller omits them, last-second edits could be lost on tab close and joining could hang on a loading screen.

Scene-version and editor-state bookkeeping moved out of the broadcast sender into the collaboration wrapper, and the full-scene broadcast to a newly joined user no longer refreshes the tracked scene version; if either lags, likely symptoms are an element snapping back mid-drag or repeated whole-scene re-syncs during normal editing, so report these if observed.

The selection data broadcast with pointer updates now falls back to an empty selection when its new source is not yet populated, and the evidence does not establish when that source becomes available, so a window may exist where remote collaborators see no selection highlights even though elements are selected.

The supplied diffs contain only new code with no removed code, so no specific input was identified that the previous code handled differently; the regression risk therefore sits in message timing and flow, most notably whether joining still completes through the timeout fallback when the initial scene message never arrives (for example when the collaboration server is unreachable after connecting).

testAreas.area: Live collaboration sync
testAreas.howToReach: Open the whiteboard editor, start a live session from the collaboration entry in the canvas controls (desktop) or the mobile menu, copy the collaboration link, and open that link in additional browsers to join.
testAreas.access: Any user; no sign-in or special role is supplied for this flow.
testAreas.setup: Two to three browsers or devices, one used to start the session and the others joining via the copied collaboration link.
checks: Check that a user joining an in-progress session receives the full current drawing shortly after opening the collaboration link, including elements drawn before they joined, and that the participant count updates for everyone.

Verify that edits made by one participant (drawing, moving, resizing, deleting) appear on the other participants' canvases in both directions, including an element edited at the same moment by two users (one version of it must win deterministically and all screens should settle on it).

Confirm that collaborator pointers and name labels follow remote users live while they drag, and that reloading a participant's browser reattaches to the room with the scene intact rather than showing an error alert.
Test a session with content, close it on one side, and confirm remaining participants keep working and that a rejoining user syncs again.

testAreas.area: Scene loading and restore
testAreas.howToReach: Open the application URL directly, then open shared scene links that contain an identifier and key in the address hash; also use the editor's open/import entry and drag a saved drawing file onto the canvas.
testAreas.setup: A saved drawing file to import, a shared scene link, and one browser profile with site data cleared so no previous drawing is stored.
checks: Validate opening the app with cleared browser storage: the canvas should load empty with the viewport positioned normally (content centered when a scene exists), with no error or blank off-canvas view.

Confirm a shared scene link still loads the intended drawing, and that a link pointing at missing content shows the import-failure alert and leaves a usable empty canvas instead of hanging or crashing.
Verify importing a saved drawing file and dropping a drawing file onto the canvas both restore all elements and settings as before.

testAreas.area: Collaboration dialog and link sharing
testAreas.howToReach: In the editor, use the collaboration button in the canvas-action toolbar on desktop, or the equivalent entry in the mobile menu, to open the live-collaboration dialog.
testAreas.setup: A session started so the dialog shows the active room link.
checks: Confirm the dialog's two states render correctly: before a session it offers starting one, and during a session it shows the room link with the copy control and the name field.

Check copying the room link puts the correct URL on the clipboard and the input selects it, that typing a name is preserved and closes the dialog on Enter, and that closing the dialog dismisses it and returns focus to the collaboration button.
Ensure stopping the session ends collaboration and the dialog returns to its pre-session state.

testAreas.area: Collaboration link handling
testAreas.howToReach: Paste collaboration links (hash in the form #room=identifier,key) into the browser address bar, both a valid one and variants with added or altered characters.
testAreas.access: Any user opening a shared link.
testAreas.setup: One valid collaboration link from an active session and one deliberately malformed variant.
checks: Verify a valid collaboration link joins the room and loads its scene, and that a malformed link does not crash the app and simply loads the editor normally.

testAreas.area: Save and export round-trip

report.summary: This release teaches the whiteboard to account for its position on the screen, improving the accuracy of drawing, typing, and the starting view, while keeping that positioning out of saved and exported drawings.
keyChanges: Screen-to-drawing and drawing-to-screen coordinate conversion now factors in the canvas's page offsets and full app state, where before only scroll and zoom were used, so clicks, pasted content, dropped files, and context menus should land exactly under the pointer even when the canvas sits away from the page corner.

The on-canvas text editing box now receives full app state and its positioning transform compensates for the canvas offsets, so at zoom levels other than 100% on an offset canvas the editing box stays aligned over the text instead of drifting by the offset times the zoom difference.
Double-clicking inside a shape to add centered text goes through the corrected conversion, so the snapped text box position follows the same offset correction.
Remote collaborator cursor rendering and local pointer broadcasting now use the corrected conversions, and view centering after loading a scene or joining a session is computed through them as well.

The editor now measures where it sits on the page (top/left offsets) at startup, on mount, and whenever its width/height properties change, and applies those values to the canvas container, which now also carries explicit sizing and position styles; the default editor state no longer contains these offsets, so both embedded and full-page layouts should be visually rechecked.

Loading a drawing now automatically centers the view on the drawing content, whether it loads on page load, via a hash change to a shareable link, or by dropping a .excalidraw file onto the canvas; previously the saved scroll position was applied as-is, so reloading no longer returns to the exact scroll position you left, and the old scroll-to-content option in the restore step was removed in favor of this centering.
Editor actions that return state (undo, redo, clear canvas, zoom) now preserve the current canvas width, height, and measured offsets, so these actions can no longer reset or misplace the canvas.
Scene initialization now waits until the canvas offsets are measured before loading the scene, so the first view is positioned correctly in embedded layouts.

Loading a drawing from a file now uses the current editor state: both the load button in the panel for saving, loading, and exporting drawings and dropping a .json or .excalidraw file onto the canvas pass it to the shared file loader, which centers the imported drawing in the current window instead of the previous automatic scroll-to-content; the loader's file parsing and invalid-file validation behave the same as before.

Scenes fetched from the backend for shareable links are no longer restored with automatic scroll-to-content, on success or on failure; they open with the view position stored in the scene, so a scene saved while scrolled or panned away may open with the drawing off-screen.
Supporting type changes allow editor state without canvas offset values to flow through load results and restored scene data; these have no direct runtime effect on their own.

The editor state gained two new values recording the canvas's top and left offset inside the browser window, and saving to browser storage or exporting to a file now strips them, so drawings no longer persist window-specific offsets and recalculate them when reopened.

Because the standard default state no longer supplies these two values, the server-side canvas export that renders a fixed sample scene (a diamond, an ellipse, and the text 'test') to a PNG now passes both offsets as explicit zero, so its image output should stay unchanged.
No screens or routes were mapped to these changes and no other dependents were found in the dependency graph, so QA focus is on the normal save/reload and export/import round-trips of the editor.
qaChecks: Verify that at 200% zoom double-clicking the existing text element opens the editing box exactly over the text, and after typing one word and committing by clicking away, the saved text occupies exactly the spot where the editing box was.
Verify that double-clicking near the center of the rectangle opens a new editing box centered inside the shape and that committing leaves the text centered in it.
Ensure the editing box stays glued to the text element when zooming to 50% and 200% while editing, with no drift from the canvas offset.
Verify that pasting copied elements while the mouse rests over a distinctive empty spot places the pasted group centered under the cursor.
Check that right-clicking an element opens the context menu anchored at the cursor and that a menu action applies to the element under the cursor.
Ensure dragging an image file from the desktop onto the canvas places it at the release point.
Confirm that dragging an existing element and then resizing it with a corner handle tracks the cursor exactly, with no initial jump.
Verify with both sessions at 200% zoom that each participant's cursor appears on the other's screen over the same element.
Confirm that an element selected by one participant is shown as selected on the other's screen while their cursor rests on it.
Validate that opening the saved drawing file centers the view on its content instead of leaving it off-screen.
Ensure dropping the same saved drawing file onto the canvas loads it with the content centered in view.
Verify drawing a rectangle and a freehand stroke places each shape exactly under the cursor when the canvas is offset from the viewport's top-left.
Verify changing the editor's width/height properties (resizing the embed) keeps click-to-draw alignment and the canvas fills the new size without shifting.
Verify the editor's toolbar and canvas controls still lay out correctly in the standard full-page view, since the canvas container now uses explicit top/left sizing styles.

Verify reloading the page with a saved drawing centers the view on the drawing rather than restoring the exact scroll position you left it at (this replaces the old saved-scroll behavior, so confirm the new centering is intended).
Verify opening a shareable drawing link loads the drawing and centers the view on its content.
Verify dropping a .excalidraw file whose drawing is off-screen loads it and centers the view on the drawing content.
Verify after undo, redo, and clearing the canvas, the canvas container stays correctly sized and positioned and new shapes still appear exactly where drawn.
Verify zooming in and out and panning keeps the pointer-to-canvas mapping accurate afterward.

Verify that opening a shared link whose saved view does not frame the drawing now opens at the saved view position, leaving the drawing possibly off-screen, and that the drawing can still be brought into view by scrolling and zooming; repeat after switching to a second shared link in the same tab.
Ensure that a link to a missing or unloadable scene still shows the import-failure alert and returns to an empty default canvas without crashing.
Verify that opening the valid file centers the imported drawing in the current window without manual scrolling, even though the file was saved with a different view position.
Check that choosing a corrupted or non-Excalidraw file shows the invalid-file error and leaves the currently open drawing unchanged.
Verify that dropping the file onto the canvas loads it and centers the drawing in the current window rather than opening at the file's saved scroll position.

Verify that after panning the canvas so the drawing sits away from the window's top-left corner (non-zero canvas offsets), saving and reloading the page reopens the drawing with every element at the same position and still selectable.

Ensure that saving a drawing and reopening it in a differently sized browser window (or after resizing the window) keeps the scene at the correct position and that clicking an element still selects that element rather than a neighbor.

Validate that exporting a drawing to a file and importing it back reproduces the scene identically, including in a fresh session or a window of a different size, since the file must not depend on the exporting window's offsets.
Confirm the generated PNG still shows the diamond, the ellipse, and the text 'test' complete, unshifted, and on a white background, matching the output produced before this change.
uncertainty: The old and new code behave identically while the canvas sits at the page's top-left corner; the difference only appears when the canvas has a non-zero page offset (for example when embedded below other content), which the supplied context does not confirm for the standalone build, so run the checks on an offset or embedded placement or they will pass trivially.

Scene loading now overrides any saved scroll position with a computed center on the drawing; the context supplies no affected areas or navigation details, so this behavior change could not be traced to a documented page or rule, and the team should confirm that dropping the exact saved scroll position on reload is intended.

The main page entry point also calls the updated file loader, but the context does not establish which user action triggers it; if the page offers any file-opening flow outside the editor, verify whether it now opens the drawing at the file's saved view position instead of centering it.

The supplied evidence does not show where the browser editor sets or refreshes the new window-offset values, for example on load or when the window is resized; if a stale or missing value were used, pointer actions could land slightly off the intended element, so any mismatch seen during the save/reload checks should be reported together with the window size and scroll position.

report.summary: This release rebuilds how the canvas decides what you are clicking and makes arrows connect to shapes, staying attached as shapes are moved, resized, copied, or undone.
keyChanges: Arrows can now attach to shapes: rectangles, diamonds, ellipses, and text are valid connection targets, and a shape highlights while an arrow is drawn or edited near it; only arrows bind, while lines and free-draw strokes do not.

Finishing an arrow on a shape, or moving a shape so a loose arrow endpoint lands within its border, attaches the connection, and moving or resizing the bound shape afterward keeps attached arrows connected with a recalculated gap, including when several elements are resized together.

Clicking, hovering, double-clicking, and right-clicking now resolve through new geometric hit-testing math that accounts for rotated shapes, ellipses, and diamonds, so selection, text editing entry, arrow point editing, and the context menu should behave exactly as before.

Core geometry calculations, resize-handle math, and element-type checks were retyped or centralized (arrows are the only element type treated as a binding element); these are intended as no-behavior-change refactors but sit underneath rendering, selection, resizing, and export, so those flows deserve a regression pass.

Canvas hit detection was rewritten as a single geometric test with a tolerance of about 10 pixels at 100% zoom: filled or currently selected shapes are clickable anywhere inside, outline-only items (arrows, lines, background-free shapes) within the tolerance of their outline, and text elements, which previously matched only clicks strictly inside their bounding box, can now also respond to clicks up to that tolerance outside it.

Arrows can bind to rectangle, text, diamond, and ellipse shapes: the shape shows a translucent highlight while an arrow endpoint is near, the arrow endpoint shows a highlight circle for point bindings, the binding zone is a quarter of the shape's smaller side clamped between 15 and 80 pixels with diamonds scaled to their slanted edge, and bound arrows follow shapes that are moved or resized.

Selection overlays were refactored into shared drawing helpers with two visible changes: the rotation handle of a single selection is now drawn as a filled circle, and the white/red point handles shown while editing a line or arrow are now filled dots centered on each point.

The scene renderer now paints suggested binding highlights on the canvas whenever binding is active, and because image export and copy-to-clipboard run through the same renderer, exported output must remain free of these editor-only overlays.

This change group introduces a brand-new 2D geometry math library (operations on points, lines, directions, and transforms) and the editor canvas geometry now runs through it; because it is entirely new, there is no previous behavior to compare against.

Shape hit-testing - deciding which shape a click or cursor lands on for rectangles, diamonds, ellipses, and line segments, including rotated shapes - now uses these new primitives, so selection and hover behavior depends on the new math.

Arrow binding - where arrows attach to shapes and how attachment points and gaps are recomputed when shapes move or resize - now uses the new math, so binding suggestions and arrow endpoints depend on it.

Dragging, resizing single and multiple elements, and arrow/line point editing (including the action that finalizes an edit when you click away) also flow through the new library, so their geometry must be re-verified on the canvas.

Arrows and lines now bind to shapes (rectangle, diamond, ellipse, text): while drawing or hovering with the arrow or line tool the shape under the cursor highlights, and finishing the arrow attaches it so it follows the shape when the shape is moved.

Holding Ctrl or Cmd while drawing now disables binding, releasing the key or the app regaining focus re-enables it, and a multi-point arrow finished by switching to another tool now attaches at its last point.

Copying and pasting elements, and dragging library items onto the canvas, now remap connections so pasted arrows attach to the pasted shapes; clearing a text element's content deletes it and cleanly detaches any arrow attached to it; editing a line's points keeps its existing bindings.

Element picking was reworked: double-click text editing, right-click menus, and hover cursors now use a shared new hit-test, and the underlying geometry helpers were replaced, including removal of the old point-to-segment distance routine, so click precision near straight or curved outlines may differ subtly.
Switching to a tool other than arrow, line, or freehand clears hover highlights, and the surrounding interface skips re-renders while binding hover state changes to stay responsive.

The engine that connects arrows and lines to shapes was moved into its own dedicated module, and the diff contains only added code with nothing removed, so no behavior change is established and this release should be treated as a regression test of the existing connection behavior.

The rules to regression-test are that a simple two-point arrow or line will not attach one end to a shape its other end is already attached to, that newly created connections keep a minimum gap of one pixel between the arrow tip and the shape edge, and that older zero-gap connections still point the arrow tip straight at the shape when the shape moves.

When a shape with attached arrows is resized, each arrow's gap is recalculated from the new size and clamped between one pixel and the shape's connection boundary, so connections stay attached without overlapping the shape.

Diamond shapes are drawn from four corner points with the left point at the shape's left edge at half height and one-pixel offsets applied to some coordinates to avoid a drawing-library error on zero values, and this geometry feeds both the on-canvas rendering and exported images.

Shapes keep their arrow connections while being transformed: dragging a shape, resizing one or many selected shapes, and rotating a shape now update the arrows attached to them, which previously were not updated during the drag or resize.

Connection bookkeeping was added around copying and deleting: duplicating elements via copy-paste, the duplicate action, library drops, or Alt-drag now remaps arrows to the copies, and deleting shapes strips dangling connections, including when replayed through undo and redo history.

New arrows bind as you draw: starting an arrow on a shape records that shape as the start connection, releasing over a shape attaches the end, and shapes eligible for connection are highlighted at the cursor while drawing or dragging elements.

In the arrow/line point editor, dragging the first or last point records the shape hovered at release and applies or removes that connection on the next click elsewhere; deleting the first or last point clears that end's connection, and trailing-point bookkeeping is now cleared so repeated Alt-clicks keep adding fresh points.
Scrollbar dragging was extracted into a shared handler and some coordinate helpers were added, with no intended behavior change.

Arrows and lines can now end attached to shapes: completing a new multi-point arrow or line that ends on a shape connects the two, and completing an edit of an existing arrow can move or remove that connection; binding is enabled by default, and a line drawn as a closed loop is deliberately not bound.
Duplicating a selection (for example with Ctrl/Cmd+D) now remaps attachments onto the copies, so a duplicated arrow follows the duplicated shape rather than the original one.
Undo and redo now repair attachments during every history restore, so restoring a snapshot in which a bound shape is absent leaves the arrow cleanly unattached instead of holding a stale connection.

Opening older saved drawings keeps any existing attachment data and supplies empty defaults where the new fields are missing; saving and reopening a drawing preserves attachments, while transient binding session state is kept out of saved files and browser storage.

Pointer hit-testing and the math that attaches arrows to shapes were rewritten on top of a new geometric algebra calculation library, replacing the previous segment-distance and diamond-points calculations.

The rewrite affects how accurately clicks register on and near element borders (including diamonds and rotated elements) and where bound arrow endpoints attach to rectangles, diamonds, ellipses, and text, and it reruns on every drag or resize of a shape with an arrow attached.

New edge-case rules were added: a connection line tangent to a shape corner's standoff circle, or a zero-radius corner circle, now yields no boundary intersection, in which case the arrow endpoint falls back to the shape's focus point instead of the gap-offset border point.

Ellipse border distance is now found with an iterative closest-point method, and the ellipse focus-point calculation substitutes a tiny vertical offset when the approach point lies exactly on the ellipse's horizontal center axis.
qaChecks: Verify that drawing an arrow with the arrow tool and finishing it exactly on a rectangle highlights the rectangle while hovering and, after release, dragging the rectangle keeps the arrow's end attached with the same connection gap.

Test dragging a shape so that the free end of an unattached arrow lands inside its border: the endpoint should attach on release, including to a text element, which is now also a valid connection target.

Ensure resizing a shape that has arrows bound at both its start and end keeps both connections on the shape's edges, and that resizing several elements together with bound arrows included in the selection preserves the connections.

Check that a plain line or free-draw stroke finished on a shape does not create a connection (moving the shape leaves it behind), and that double-clicking an arrow to edit its points and dragging an endpoint onto another shape rebinds it on release.

Verify that clicking overlapping shapes selects the topmost one, that right-clicking a shape opens the element context menu with copy and paste actions, and that right-clicking empty canvas shows the canvas-only menu.

Confirm double-clicking a rotated rectangle or ellipse starts text editing, double-clicking a text element opens it for editing, and double-clicking an arrow or line with the selection tool enters point-by-point editing.
Test clicking near the edge of a rotated shape: the rotated shape itself should be selected rather than the element behind it.
Verify the corner, edge, and rotation handles of a selected rectangle appear at the correct positions at different zoom levels, grabbing a corner resizes, and the rotation handle rotates.
Confirm text elements still show the reduced handle set and that handle positions stay correct on a rotated selection.
Ensure a two-point arrow still resizes by moving its endpoints rather than scaling it like a box.
Verify that copying or exporting a drawing with bound arrows as PNG and SVG produces an image matching the canvas, with connections intact and no leftover binding highlights.
Ensure deleting a shape that has bound arrows cleans up the connections, and that undo afterward restores the shape and arrows without dangling or broken ends.

Verify that a click inside a text element's bounding box still selects it, that a click just outside the box but within about 10 pixels of its edge now also selects it, and that a click farther out in empty space selects nothing.

Verify that clicking the center of the filled rectangle, diamond, and ellipse selects and drags each shape, and that clicking within the tolerance of the outline of the background-free rectangle or the arrow selects it rather than an element behind it.
Verify that clicking the interior of the background-free rectangle behaves as before (it should not grab the shape from its empty middle unless it is already selected).
Verify that double-clicking a filled shape opens text editing on it and right-clicking a shape opens its context menu.

Verify that drawing an arrow so its end lands on or within the translucent highlight around a shape connects them, confirmed by the arrow staying attached when the shape is then moved, and repeat for the rectangle, diamond, ellipse, and text shapes.

Verify the binding highlight zone scales with the shape: at least 15 pixels around the small shape and no more than 80 around the large one, with the diamond's zone hugging its slanted edge rather than its bounding box.
Verify that hovering the loose end of an arrow near a bindable shape shows a translucent circle at that endpoint and releasing completes the connection.
Verify that resizing a shape with arrows attached keeps the arrows connected with a proportionate gap instead of detaching them.
Check that drawing an arrow whose endpoint ends on or inside a nearby shape binds the endpoint to that shape with a visible binding indication.
Verify that dragging a bound shape across the canvas keeps the arrow endpoint attached and the arrow reroutes smoothly.
Verify that resizing a bound shape keeps the arrow endpoint on the shape's boundary, neither detached nor buried inside it.
Verify a single selected shape shows its corner resize handles and a rotation handle drawn as a filled circle in the correct spot, and dragging that handle still rotates the shape.

Verify multi-selecting several elements shows the dashed bounding box with handles when not rotating, and that dashed selection borders still render, including a collaborator's colored dashes on shared elements.
Verify that entering point editing shows a filled dot centered exactly on each point and that dragging the first, a middle, and the last dot moves the corresponding point.

Verify that exporting the scene as PNG and copying the image to the clipboard produce output with the arrow still connected and no selection borders, resize or rotation handles, or translucent binding highlights included.
Verify that clicking directly on each shape type (rectangle, diamond, ellipse, line, arrow) selects exactly that shape and that clicking empty canvas clears the selection.
Verify that hovering over a shape highlights it and that right-clicking a shape opens its context menu for that shape.
Test a shape rotated about 45 degrees: clicking its visible corners and edges selects it while clicking the empty corners of its unrotated bounding box does not.
Verify that resizing a single shape with a corner handle down to a very small size keeps its outline correct and the shape still selectable.
Check that selecting two shapes together and resizing from a corner handle scales both correctly while any bound arrows follow.
Verify that double-clicking an arrow enters point-edit mode, dragging a point reshapes it, and clicking empty canvas finishes editing without losing the change.
Check that while editing a bound arrow, dragging its free endpoint onto another shape binds it to that shape.
Verify that double-clicking empty canvas creates a text box at that position and typed text appears there.
Confirm that double-clicking directly on a shape opens its text for editing and does not target a neighboring shape.

Verify that with the arrow tool hovering over a shape highlights it and hovering empty canvas shows no highlight, and that an arrow finished on a shape attaches so that moving the shape afterwards drags the arrow's endpoint along.

Test drawing an arrow onto a shape while holding Ctrl or Cmd: it must not attach; after releasing the key a new arrow onto the same shape must attach, including after clicking outside the window with the key held so the app loses and regains focus.
Test a multi-point arrow created by clicking point by point that ends near a shape, then switching to the selection tool before finalizing: the arrow should attach to the shape under its last point.

Confirm the toolbar and menus stay responsive while moving the pointer across shapes with the arrow tool, and that switching from the arrow tool to a shape tool such as rectangle clears any hover highlight.

Verify selecting a shape together with its attached arrow, copying, and pasting yields a duplicate where the pasted arrow is attached to the pasted shape: moving the pasted shape moves the pasted arrow's endpoint and the original pair is untouched.
Test dragging a library item containing connected shapes onto the canvas and confirm the dropped copy keeps its internal arrow connections and they move with the shapes.
Verify clicking inside a closed hand-drawn shape selects it, while clicking empty canvas inside its bounding area but outside the drawn outline does not.
Test double-clicking a text element that overlaps another shape: the text editor must open for that text element, and hovering it with the text tool must show the text cursor.
Confirm right-clicking a specific element where several overlap opens the context menu for that element so Copy and Paste act on it.
Verify clearing a text element's content and submitting so the text is deleted leaves the attached arrow cleanly detached, with no error and no arrow pointing at a removed element.
Test double-clicking an attached arrow to edit its points, moving a middle point, and finishing: the arrow must stay attached to the shapes it was bound to.

Verify that drawing an arrow and releasing its endpoint on or near a shape attaches the arrow to that shape with a small visible gap between the arrow tip and the shape edge rather than touching it exactly.

Test drawing a simple two-point arrow whose start is already attached to a shape and dragging its endpoint to the same shape; confirm the endpoint is not attached to the same shape and the arrow keeps only its original connection.
Check that moving a shape with attached arrows drags the arrow endpoints along with it and the connections remain attached.

Ensure a drawing where an arrow tip touches a shape edge exactly, a zero-gap connection from an older drawing, still points the arrow tip straight at the shape when the shape is moved, rather than detaching or drifting.

Verify that while dragging an arrow endpoint across a shape, the shape is highlighted as a connection suggestion only when the endpoint is eligible, and that no suggestion appears for a simple two-point arrow whose other end is already attached to that shape.
Confirm that after releasing an arrow endpoint onto a shape, the connection persists and the shape is highlighted again when the endpoint is dragged nearby.
Test resizing a bound shape larger and smaller and confirm attached arrows follow the shape edge, keeping a gap of at least one pixel and never overlapping into the shape.
Ensure extreme resizing, both very small and very large, keeps the connections attached and the arrow tips on the shape's boundary.
Verify that a diamond renders as a symmetric four-point shape with its left point at the shape's left edge at half height, both on the canvas and in exported images.
Confirm that exported PNG and SVG images of a drawing containing diamonds match the on-canvas rendering.
Verify that dragging the rectangle across the canvas makes both attached arrows' endpoints follow and stay connected to it, which previously did not happen during the drag.
Check that resizing the rectangle from a corner handle and then rotating it keeps the arrow endpoints attached to the moved edges and redrawn cleanly.
Verify that selecting the rectangle together with the second shape and resizing the selection keeps the shared arrow attached to both without stray displacement.
Check that copy-pasting or duplicating a shape with an attached arrow produces a pasted arrow connected to the pasted shape while the original pair keeps its own connection.
Verify that holding Alt and dragging a connected shape creates a duplicate where both the original and the duplicate keep correct arrow connections.
Confirm that deleting a shape with an attached arrow cleanly drops only that arrow's connection, and that undoing the delete restores the connection while redo removes it again.
Test that starting an arrow on a shape and releasing it over another shape attaches the arrow at both ends, while releasing over empty canvas leaves it unattached.
Verify that shapes eligible for connection are highlighted while dragging a new arrow's end or while dragging selected elements, and that the highlights disappear when the interaction ends.
Check that finishing a new shape over an existing arrow's loose endpoint attaches that arrow to the newly drawn shape.

Check that dragging the arrow's first or last point onto a shape, releasing, then clicking elsewhere connects the arrow to that shape, and clicking away with nothing under the cursor removes the connection.
Verify that deleting the first point of a bound arrow clears the start connection while the end connection survives, and deleting the last point clears the end connection.
Ensure that Alt-clicking adds a new point and that, after moving the mouse without Alt, another Alt-click still adds a fresh point; dragging a closed loop's endpoint should still snap it closed.
Verify that dragging the horizontal scrollbar pans the canvas horizontally and the vertical scrollbar pans vertically, with no element distortion.
Check that after a scrollbar drag, selecting, dragging, and resizing elements still behave as before.

Verify that an arrow drawn so it ends directly on a shape becomes attached: draw a multi-point arrow ending on the rectangle, complete the drawing, then move the rectangle and confirm the arrow's end stays connected to it.

Check that re-editing an existing arrow can move or remove its attachment: enter the arrow's point-editing mode and confirm the round point handles render, drag the end point onto a different shape and complete editing so it attaches there, then repeat with the end point on empty canvas to confirm the arrow detaches and moves independently.

Confirm that a line drawn as a closed loop still closes: with the line tool, place points that return to the starting point and complete it; the last point should snap to the first, the loop should stay closed at different zoom levels, and it should not attach to shapes.

Verify duplicating a bound pair keeps the copies paired: select the rectangle together with its attached arrow and press Ctrl/Cmd+D; expect duplicates offset 10 px down and right with the duplicated arrow attached to the duplicated rectangle, while both originals remain attached to each other.
Check that duplicating several bound shapes and arrows at once pairs every copy with its own copy instead of pointing copies at the original shapes.

Verify deleting the bound shape and pressing Ctrl/Cmd+Z restores both the shape and the attachment (moving the restored shape keeps the arrow connected), and that redo with Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+Z removes the shape again while the arrow stays intact, selectable, and movable with no stale attachment.
Check that ordinary undo and redo of drawing, moving, and deleting elements without attachments still restores the exact previous state, since the attachment repair now runs on every undo and redo.
Verify that a drawing saved by the previous version, which contains no attachment data, opens without errors and its shapes, arrows, and text render as before.

Confirm that saving a drawing with an arrow attached to a shape and reopening it preserves the attachment (moving the shape keeps the arrow connected), and that reloading the page restores the scene from browser storage the same way.

Verify that dragging each bound shape (rectangle, ellipse, diamond, and text label) across the canvas keeps every attached arrow endpoint on that shape's border at the same small standoff distance, with no endpoint floating in empty space, sinking inside the shape, or snapping to the shape's center.

Test resizing a bound rectangle and a bound ellipse to very small (a few pixels) and very large sizes and confirm each arrow re-anchors smoothly to the new border, without the endpoint jumping to the center, flying off the shape, or the canvas becoming unresponsive.

Verify that an arrow drawn starting exactly level with an ellipse's center height binds to the ellipse's side edge and, when the ellipse is then dragged, the endpoint keeps tracking the ellipse boundary rather than landing at the center or an arbitrary point.

Check that at 100% zoom a click inside a filled rectangle selects it, a click on an unfilled rectangle's border selects it, a click on each extreme left, right, top, and bottom point of an ellipse selects it, and a click clearly away from all shapes (more than about 10 pixels) selects nothing.
Verify that clicks along a diamond's four edges and just outside its corners select the diamond according to its visible diamond outline rather than its rectangular bounding box.
Confirm that after rotating a rectangle, clicking near its rotated edges and corners selects it according to the rotated outline.

Test starting an arrow drag just outside (not touching) a rectangle, an ellipse, and a diamond and confirm the hovered shape still highlights as bindable and the finished arrow binds to it, including drags started just outside an ellipse's edge or a diamond's corner.
uncertainty: Almost all changed code here is newly added (binding and geometric hit testing) or type-only, so no input could be identified that the old code provably handled differently; the one rewritten check delegates the old direct arrow/line/draw comparison to a type list that was not visible, so confirm arrow, line, and free-draw strokes still count as line-like elements for bounds, resizing, rotation, and undo history.

The tolerance-based hit test changes text selection: the previous build required a click strictly inside a text element's bounding box, while the new code can register a click up to about 10 pixels outside it at 100% zoom; confirm this is intended, because in dense diagrams a click in the narrow gap beside text may now grab the text instead of the empty canvas or a neighboring element.

The geometry library is newly added with no prior implementation, so the diff provides no old-versus-new input to target; verification must judge correct canvas geometry against expected behavior, and the app context supplied no specific screens, routes, or navigation steps.

The reworked point-in-shape geometry uses an exact collinearity test with a bounding-box approximation in place of the previous on-segment check, and the old point-to-segment distance helper was removed in favor of the new hit-test pipeline; whether clicks exactly on straight or curved outlines register slightly differently than before is not fully determinable from the change, so any report of shapes selecting from slightly farther off their outlines, or outline clicks missing, should be triaged against the previous build.

The supplied diff consists entirely of added code with nothing removed, so the behavior before this change could not be compared directly; if any connection rule was adjusted during the reorganization, QA has no reference for the old behavior and must rely on the rules described above.

In point-editing mode the new connection appears to be recorded when the dragged point is released but only applied or removed on the next click that is not on a point; the supplied context does not describe this interaction, so confirm the intended timing with the team before treating a delay as a defect.

A small circle-drawing helper used for point handles in the renderer was removed in this change while the graph still lists the point-handle renderer as calling it; if round point handles fail to render or the canvas misbehaves while editing a line's or arrow's points, this removal is the first suspect, and the point-editing check in the first test area covers it.

The supplied diffs present these functions as newly added code without the previous implementations alongside, so exact differences from the old math could not be pinned to a specific input; the likeliest visible differences are for exact-tangent or axis-aligned geometry, such as an arrow connection line grazing a shape corner's standoff circle (now treated as no intersection, with the endpoint falling back to the shape's focus point) and clicks landing exactly at the selection tolerance distance.
