report.summary: This release lets text live inside shapes in the drawing editor, so attached text now behaves as part of the shape when editing, selecting, copying, resizing, rotating, saving, and rendering.
keyChanges: Text inside shapes is now wrap-aware: typing long text in a shape wraps it to the shape's width, the shape grows taller line by line while typing and shrinks back toward its original height when lines are deleted, and the text stays vertically centered.

Committing text inside a shape now also links that text to the shape (and unlinks it when every character is deleted), and starting text over a shape now ignores text elements when finding the shape under the cursor, so existing text in a shape is edited in place rather than shadowed by a new text element.

Changing font family, font size, or alignment, or pasting copied styles, on text inside a shape now recomputes the text box from the original text re-wrapped to the shape's width, instead of re-measuring the already-wrapped text with no width limit.

Text measurement internally gained wrap-aware sizing and an approximate line-height helper, and newly created text elements record the shape they belong to and their original text; standalone (unbound) text should behave as before.

Double-clicking a shape with attached text (or double-tapping on touch) now opens the inline editor at the shape's center and edits the bound text; previously editing started at the exact double-click position with no binding, so off-center double-clicks now behave differently.

Text added to a shape is now attached to it: containers smaller than one line of the current font are grown to fit, submitting via keyboard selects the shape rather than the text, and submitting empty text deletes the attached text and unbinds the shape.

Pointer hit-testing and rubber-band selection now ignore text bound to a shape by default: clicking on that text selects and drags the shape, and a selection rectangle picks up the shape without separately selecting its text; explicit text lookup (text tool, editing) still finds attached text.
Duplicating or copy/pasting a shape with attached text now rebinds the copied text to the copied shape, and deleting a selected shape also deletes its attached text.

The inline text editor is now positioned without subtracting canvas offsets (it should sit exactly over the text), and while typing, attached text no longer resizes per keystroke because the shape's width caps it; dimensions update only on submit.

Text attached to a shape now takes the shape's angle when the shape is rotated, whether rotated alone or together with other selected elements (where it also moves along); before, the text kept its original angle while the shape turned.

Resizing a shape that contains text now rewraps the text to the new width and grows the shape taller when the text needs another line (shifting the shape when resizing from a top handle), and this reflow now also runs when several elements are resized in one selection; previously the text kept its old line breaks.

Resizing gained new limits: shapes with attached text can no longer be sized to negative dimensions (dragging a handle past the opposite edge is ignored instead of inverting the shape) and cannot be narrowed below roughly the width of one character of their font plus padding; shapes without attached text now also require a positive width, so over-dragging an east/west handle no longer flips them horizontally while a north/south over-drag still can.
When a multi-element selection is scaled, the font of attached text is now measured against the wrapped width so the scaled text stays correctly positioned inside its shape.

Text committed from the in-canvas editor is now word-wrapped to the container width, including breaking a single word longer than the shape, and small shapes grow to fit at least one line when you start typing in them.
Copying or cutting a shape that has attached text now includes that text in the clipboard; previously only the shape was copied, so pasting dropped the attached text.

Clicking inside a shape now behaves differently: a fully transparent shape with attached text can be grabbed and moved from inside its outline (before, dragging only worked from the edge), while shapes with a semi-transparent hex background such as #ff000000, which were draggable from anywhere inside before, are now only draggable when grabbing near their edges.

When you edit text attached to a shape, the text is now measured against the shape's width and wraps inside it, and if the text becomes taller or wider than the shape, the shape automatically grows to fit it plus a 30-pixel padding; before, the shape stayed its original size and text could overflow.

The text measurement routine was replaced and now accepts a width limit, which feeds font family, font size, and alignment changes, paste-styles, pasted spreadsheet charts, and text resizing; the editor's text-update flow also now passes an original text and a flag controlling whether dimensions are recalculated.

Selecting exactly one rectangle, diamond, ellipse, or image now shows a hint about binding text to that element, where the previous version showed no hint for those single selections, while the existing arrow, line, and text-selection hints are unchanged.

Text that sits inside a shape is no longer treated as a connectable target, so arrows now attach to the surrounding shape rather than to its inner text, while free-standing text on the canvas remains connectable as before.

Text wrapped inside shapes is now measured through a new per-font character-width cache with calculate, update, read, and reset helpers, so line-break positions in bound text may shift slightly, most visibly for long words without spaces, and resizing or flipping such shapes re-wraps text through the same path.

Text attached to a shape (bound text) now stays attached when the shape is duplicated: pasting, dropping a library item onto the canvas, and duplicate-dragging a selection with Alt held rebind the copied text to the copied shape; previously the duplicated text lost its attachment and floated separately, and duplicate-dragging did not copy the attached text at all.
Dragging a shape that is not part of a group now carries its attached text along with it; previously the text did not follow the shape.

Selection-based output now includes attached text: the image export dialog's export-only-selected option (preview, PNG, SVG, and copy-to-clipboard image) and adding selected elements to the library now pick up text attached to the selected shapes, which was previously left out.

Attached text now survives restoring scene data: opening saved files, shareable links, and collaboration scenes keeps each text's link to its shape and its original text, so bindings no longer disappear on load; this same restore step is what makes the paste fix work.

Text editing entry points changed: pressing Enter on a selected shape (not a line or arrow) now starts editing with text binding enabled, and clicking with the text tool on a shape that already has attached text opens the editor centered on the shape for the existing text instead of at the click point.

When text is drawn on canvas, lines of text attached to a shape (bound text) are now spaced using the font's approximate line height; before this change the drawing code divided the text element's height by the number of lines, stretching or squeezing the lines to fill that height. Text not attached to a shape keeps the old height-based spacing.

Because editor rendering and all canvas-based outputs share this drawing code, multi-line attached text can look different in the main editor canvas, the image export dialog's preview, clipboard copies made as PNG or SVG, saving into a currently opened file, library publish previews, and the embeddable package's canvas and blob exports — for example, a tall shape with two short attached lines will no longer have its lines spread across the whole shape height; they keep font-based spacing.

The remaining edits are plumbing for attached text: the text element model gains fields recording the attached shape and the original typed text, and helper imports were added in the text editor, renderer, and selection code; none of them changes behavior on its own.
Automated tests already cover the embeddable package export helpers on this path.
Text placed inside a shape (bound text) is now treated as part of that shape in all selection-based actions: delete, duplicate, copy as PNG, copy as SVG, group, select all, and add to library.

Deleting a selected shape now also deletes the text bound to it, so text-filled shapes no longer leave orphaned text on the canvas; select all no longer selects bound text separately, and select all followed by delete still clears the whole canvas.
Duplicating a selection now copies each shape's bound text with it and rebinds the copy's text to the copied shape; the duplicated text is not left as a separately selected object afterwards.
Copy as PNG and Copy as SVG of a selection now include the text inside the selected shapes, which the exported image previously omitted.

Grouping now counts bound text as part of the selection, so the group action becomes available for a single text-filled shape (previously it did nothing) and grouping shapes also groups their texts; adding a selection to the library now includes bound text.
qaChecks: Verify that double-clicking a rectangle and typing a sentence much wider than the shape wraps the text onto multiple lines inside the shape instead of staying on one line running past its edges.

Check that the shape grows taller as each wrapped line is added while you keep typing, and shrinks back toward its original height as you delete lines, with the text staying vertically centered the whole time.

Confirm that finishing with Escape or a click outside commits the text: the canvas shows the same wrapped text inside the shape, and reopening the editor shows the wording exactly as you typed it, without extra hard line breaks inserted by the wrapping.
Test deleting every character of a shape's text and committing: the shape should end up with no text, and double-clicking it again should start a fresh text that binds to the shape.

Validate changing the font size of text inside a shape (for example from small to twice the size): the text re-wraps within the shape's width instead of overflowing horizontally, and the shape grows to hold the larger text.

Confirm switching the font family or the text alignment of text inside a shape keeps all wrapped lines inside the shape's bounds in the expected position; the same should hold after copying style from another element and pasting it onto the text inside the shape.

Verify that normal text on empty canvas (double-click on empty space or the text tool) still behaves as before: it stays on one line while you type, breaks only where you press Enter, and committing with Escape or an outside click keeps it on the canvas.
Test typing many lines of standalone text near the bottom edge of the window: the on-canvas editor should not extend past the visible screen area and should remain fully editable and committable.
Confirm double-clicking the text inside a shape that already has text reopens that same text for editing, still bound to the same shape, instead of creating a second overlapping text element.
Ensure copying a shape that contains text and pasting it produces a duplicate whose text sits inside the duplicate shape, not as a separate floating text.
Validate opening an older saved drawing, selecting one of its text elements and changing its font size or family: the text should reflow without errors and stay positioned as before.

Check: double-click (or double-tap on touch) the center of a shape, type Hello, and press Enter — the text is created inside and attached to the shape, a too-small shape grows to fit at least one text line, and the shape (not the text alone) stays selected after submit.
Check: double-click a shape that already has attached text — the existing text opens for editing with no duplicate text created; edit and submit, and the shape shows the updated text once.
Check: open editing on attached text, clear it to empty, and submit — the attached text is removed, the shape remains, and no orphan text is left on the canvas.
Check: with the text tool selected, click a shape's center — editing starts and the resulting text is attached to that shape rather than left as free text.
Verify: click directly on the text inside a shape (including a transparent shape with text) — the whole shape is selected, and dragging moves the shape and its text together.

Check: drag a selection rectangle that fully covers a shape and its text — only the shape is selected (the attached text is not added as a separate item), and moving the selection keeps the text attached and centered.
Check: right-click over a shape's attached text — the element context menu opens for the shape, and the shape gets selected if it was not already.
Check: select a shape with attached text and duplicate it — the duplicate carries its own copy of the text attached to the duplicated shape while the original keeps its text.

Check: copy the shape with attached text and paste it, and separately drop it in from the library — the pasted copy shows the text bound to the copy, positioned with the copy rather than the original.
Check: select the shape with attached text and delete it — both the shape and its text are removed with no orphan text remaining.
Ensure: with the page scrolled or the canvas not at the top-left, start editing text on a shape and on free text — the editor overlay appears exactly over the text's on-screen position.

Check: type long, multi-line text into a shape's attached text — while typing, the text wraps within the shape's width without the text resizing per keystroke; on submit the shape grows to fit the text (with padding) and the text stays centered.
Verify: double-click empty canvas and then click a standalone text element — plain text is still created at the click point and remains separately selectable and movable, unchanged from before.

Confirm: with a shape that has attached text selected, run an action such as align, flip, or group — the action applies to the shape only and the text follows the shape rather than being treated as a second selected element.

Verify dragging a corner or side resize handle past the opposite edge of the text-containing shape stops the resize instead of inverting it: the shape keeps a positive size and the text stays inside the outline (this input previously flipped the shape inside out).
Verify narrowing the shape wraps the text onto more lines and the shape grows taller to keep the text inside with padding, and widening it lets the text flow back onto fewer lines.
Verify the shape cannot be narrowed below about the width of its widest text character plus padding: the resize stops at that minimum instead of collapsing the text.
Verify resizing from a top corner (top-left or top-right) while the text needs an extra line grows the shape upward so the bottom edge stays put and the text remains inside.
Test Flip horizontal and then Flip vertical on a freedraw scribble and on an image: each should mirror in place, keeping its position and size.
Confirm flipping a shape that has attached text still mirrors the shape and leaves the text readable and inside it.

Verify that on a plain shape without text, dragging an east or west resize handle past the opposite edge stops the resize (no horizontal mirror), while dragging a north or south handle past the opposite edge still mirrors vertically.
Verify rotating a shape containing text to about 45 degrees makes the text rotate with the shape and stay inside it.
Verify selecting several elements including a shape with attached text and rotating the group moves and rotates every attached text together with its shape.
Verify dragging a corner handle to make the selection narrower and then wider rewraps the text inside to the new width and keeps it inside its shape (it previously kept the old wrapping).
Verify scaling that selection down and back up keeps the text wrapped inside its shape and vertically positioned, without overflowing or drifting outside.
Verify double-clicking a very small shape and typing makes the shape grow to at least fit one line of the current font so the text is not clipped.

Verify typing a normal sentence plus one word longer than the shape's width, then clicking outside, commits text wrapped within the shape's width with the long word broken across lines, and reopening the editor shows the same wrapped text.
Verify that copying a shape with attached text and pasting it elsewhere produces the shape together with its attached text, not the shape alone.
Verify that cutting a shape with attached text and pasting it moves both the shape and its text, and the text is not left behind on the canvas.
Verify that clicking well inside the transparent shape that has attached text now grabs and moves the whole shape, instead of only working when grabbing near its edge.

Verify that clicking well inside the shape with background #ff000000 no longer moves it from the inside, and it only moves when grabbing near its border; confirm a solid-filled shape is still draggable from inside as before.
Verify that typing a long unbroken line of text into a shape's attached text makes the shape grow to fit the text with visible padding, instead of the text overflowing a fixed-size shape.
Verify that text longer than the shape's width now wraps inside the shape rather than extending past it.
Verify that after finishing editing (click away), the shape's position and size are correct and the text stays centered as configured.
Verify that pasting spreadsheet data produces correctly positioned chart previews (bar and line) with axis labels placed as before, and inserting one yields a readable chart.
Verify that changing font family and font size on attached text keeps the text inside its shape and adjusts the shape accordingly, and that changing them on standalone text resizes it consistently.
Verify that resizing a text element using its corner handles still updates its rendered size and font without visual glitches.

Verify that drawing an arrow toward a shape with text typed inside it (create a rectangle, double-click it, type text, click away, then draw the arrow at its border) attaches the arrow to the shape's border rather than to the inner text, and that the arrow stays attached when the shape is dragged around the canvas.
Ensure an arrow can still attach to a free-standing text element placed directly on the canvas and not inside any shape.
Confirm deleting a shape that has both a connected arrow and text inside it removes them cleanly, and pressing undo restores the drawing with the arrow reconnected.

Test a single long word with no spaces, such as a roughly 40-character URL, typed into a narrow rectangle and confirm it breaks onto multiple lines and stays within the shape's edges instead of overflowing.
Confirm multi-word text inside a shape re-wraps immediately when the shape is dragged narrower and wider with its side handle, with no characters cut off or spilling outside.
Verify that the line breaks shown while editing text inside a shape match the final result after clicking away to save it.
Verify that resizing a shape containing several lines of text with a corner handle re-wraps the text and keeps it fully visible at each size.
Check that flipping a shape containing text horizontally and vertically keeps the text inside the shape in the correct position afterwards.
Verify that selecting exactly one rectangle, then one diamond, then one ellipse, then one image shows a hint about binding text to the element in each case, which previously showed no hint at all.
Confirm a single selected arrow or line still shows its line-editing hint and a single selected text element still shows its text hint.
Check the same hints appear correctly in the mobile layout's toolbar area when a single shape is selected.
Verify dragging the shape with attached text moves the text together with the shape, keeping the same relative position during and after the drag.
Verify duplicate-dragging the selected shape with Alt held produces a copy that carries its own attached text inside it, not a textless copy or a floating copy of the text.
Verify copying a shape with attached text and pasting it: the pasted text stays attached to the pasted shape and moves with it afterwards.
Verify that immediately after pasting a plain shape, pressing Delete removes the pasted copy and not the original drawing content, and that the pasted shape can still be clicked and moved normally.
Verify opening the saved drawing or link: every attached text is still bound to its shape, so dragging the shape moves the text and no text floats separately.
Verify refreshing the browser during a live collaboration session: after the scene is restored, attached text is still bound to its shape.

Verify the export preview with the export-only-selected-elements option enabled shows the attached text, and the exported PNG and SVG files contain that text; previously it was missing from selection-only exports.
Verify copying the selected image to the clipboard from the dialog also includes the attached text.

Verify with the text tool active, clicking on the shape that already has attached text (including near its edge rather than its center) opens the editor for the existing attached text centered in the shape, without creating a second overlapping text.
Verify selecting a shape, pressing Enter, typing text, and finishing: the typed text becomes attached to the shape, so dragging the shape afterwards moves the text with it.

Verify adding the selection to the library stores an item that includes the attached text, and inserting that item back onto the canvas produces the shape with its text still attached; previously the text was dropped.

Test the discriminating case first: a shape taller than its text needs holding two or three short lines of attached text — the lines should keep the font's natural line spacing instead of being stretched to fill the shape, and the result should match what the on-canvas text editor shows.
Verify the same drawing's standalone multi-line text (not attached to any shape) still renders exactly as before, with its lines distributed across the text box.
Check the attached text while zooming in and out and confirm spacing and placement stay consistent and the text neither overlaps the shape's border nor gets clipped.
Verify the dialog's export preview shows the attached multi-line text with the same line spacing as the editor canvas.
Confirm the downloaded PNG (and the SVG, for comparison) shows the attached text with placement and spacing consistent with the canvas.
Verify a pasted PNG copy of the drawing shows the attached multi-line text with the same line spacing as the editor canvas.
Confirm a copy made as SVG renders the attached text legibly and consistently with the canvas when pasted or opened in another application.
Verify that after saving to the currently opened file and reopening it, the attached multi-line text's spacing and placement match what the canvas showed before saving.
Verify the generated preview image shows the attached multi-line text with the same line spacing as the editor canvas before the item is submitted.
Verify selecting one text-filled rectangle and deleting it removes both the rectangle and its text, leaving no orphaned text on the canvas (previously the text was left behind).
Verify selecting two text-filled shapes and deleting them removes both shapes and both texts, while the nearby standalone text element that is not selected remains.
Verify select all on this canvas followed by delete clears the entire canvas, including the text inside the shapes and the standalone text.
Verify duplicating a selected text-filled shape creates an offset copy that includes its own text, with the original shape and text unchanged.
Verify duplicating two text-filled shapes at once, grouped or ungrouped, copies each text with its shape and leaves no extra orphaned text on the canvas.
Verify that after duplicating a text-filled shape, dragging the duplicated shape moves its text along with it and the text stays inside the shape.

Verify selecting the text-filled shape, copying it as PNG to the clipboard, and pasting into an image editor or back onto the canvas shows the text inside the shape in the pasted image (previously the text was missing from the export).
Verify copying the same selection as SVG to the clipboard produces SVG content that renders the text inside the shape.
Verify the exported output contains only the selected shapes and their text, with nothing extra added.
Verify selecting the two text-filled shapes and grouping them pulls their texts into the group, so moving the group afterwards moves the shapes and their texts together.
Verify selecting the single text-filled shape and using group: the action now runs where it previously did nothing, and the shape and its text end up grouped without errors or odd selection behavior.
Verify adding the selected text-filled shape to the library and then placing the saved library item onto a canvas shows the item with its text included (previously the text was missing).
uncertainty: Text elements created before this change do not carry the newly stored original text value, and restyling them now reads that value; the supplied context does not establish whether older saved drawings are handled, so loading and restyling text from pre-existing files (last test area) should be treated as the open risk.

The selection helper used by roughly 34 callers is a traversal hub and the blast radius was truncated, so selection-based actions beyond duplication (align, distribute, flip, group, zoom-to-fit, copy as image/SVG) were not fully expanded; they default to the old behavior, but if any path starts including attached text, shapes with text could be processed twice in those actions.

The flip actions internally resize with the handle pulled past the opposite side to create the mirror, and the new rule that a resized width must be greater than the minimum (zero for shapes without attached text) may block that internal step; the flip checks above decide this, and if Flip horizontal or Flip vertical stops mirroring elements, report it as the regression from this change.

The old text measurement routine was removed and replaced with a new one whose code is not in the evidence, so exact match of text sizes, wrapping, and baselines with the previous version cannot be confirmed; chart label placement and font changes are the most sensitive checks. Also, the exported text-update routine now requires new parameters (an original text and a dimensions flag), and only the editor's own caller is evidenced as updated, so external embedders calling it directly could be affected.

Drawings made with the previous version could attach an arrow to text sitting inside a shape, and this change no longer treats that text as a connectable target; the evidence does not show what happens to such existing arrow connections, for example after the inner text is deleted, so spot-check one older drawing file if one is available.

The paste and library-insert flow now auto-selects only standalone text elements, so pasted shapes and shape-with-text pairs no longer appear selected after pasting, whereas previously everything pasted was selected; confirm whether this narrowing is intended, because a user who pastes and immediately presses Delete may find that nothing is deleted.

No documented rule states what the correct line spacing for text attached to a shape should be, so judge it against the on-canvas text editing view and keep canvas and export outputs consistent; the attached-text feature spans changes reviewed outside this group, so full behavior may depend on those too.

The supplied context does not document whether grouping a single shape with its own bound text is intended; the new code enables the group action for that selection where it previously did nothing, so flag any unexpected grouping or selection behavior there.

report.summary: This release adds hyperlinks to drawing elements in the editor and changes how generated packages load their interface library and behave offline.
keyChanges: Selecting exactly one element now shows a link action button in the selected-shape properties panel, placed after the group and ungroup actions; previously the panel offered no link action, and two or more selected elements still hide it. The same panel is rendered by the desktop side panel and the mobile menu.

The link tooltip display code was added or updated in this group: hovering an element that has a link shows the URL in a tooltip near the link icon at the element's top-right corner after a brief hover delay, and it hides when the pointer moves away; the tooltip shares one on-screen tooltip element with the app's control tooltips and is clamped to the window with a 5px margin.
The help dialog now lists the link tool with the Ctrl+K shortcut, shown as Cmd+K on Mac.
Linked elements now render a small link icon (14 px baseline size) on the drawing canvas, shown only while that element is not selected, rebuilt per zoom level, and rotated together with the element.
This icon is deliberately skipped in every export path, so PNG and SVG exports, clipboard image copies, images saved with scene data, and library publish previews must not contain it.

The element right-click menu gains a link entry for setting or editing a URL, the link popup closes automatically whenever the context menu opens or the active tool changes away from selection, and the internal menu-open marker resets after each action so popup behavior recovers normally.

A new internal editor flag tracking whether the link popup is visible defaults to off at startup and is deliberately stripped from browser storage, server saves, and file exports, so drawings saved before this release keep loading normally and new saves stay clean.

When drawing content is loaded from files, pastes, drops, library items, or shared collaboration storage, each element now keeps its stored link value, and older content without any link data is filled in with an empty value instead of losing or corrupting anything.
A new link keyboard shortcut, Ctrl or Cmd plus K, is now registered in the editor's shortcut map, so selecting an element and pressing that combination should invoke the link action.
The link interface gained supporting pieces in this group: a new edit icon for editor controls and a setting that makes the link tooltip appear after roughly a third of a second of hovering.

A selected element can now be given a hyperlink: Ctrl/Cmd+K, the link entry in the right-click menu, or the link button in the selected-element panel opens a link editor popup on that element; pressing the shortcut again while the editor is already open does nothing.

The right-click link entry appears only when exactly one element is selected, and its label switches between creating a link and editing one depending on whether that element already has a link; the panel button shows as active only when a single selected element has a link.

Every newly created element (drawn shapes, text, lines and freehand strokes, dropped or pasted images, pasted spreadsheet charts) now stores a link field that starts empty, so scenes now persist this field and creation flows should otherwise behave exactly as before.

The link popup stays visible while the pointer is over the element, in the gap between the element and the popup, or over the popup itself, and hides shortly after the pointer moves elsewhere; the element bounding-box hit test behind this is unchanged apart from now being shared with the popup logic.

Selecting a single canvas element and hovering its link icon shows a link popup centered above the element: it shows the saved link with edit and remove buttons, or an input with the placeholder 'Type or paste your link here' when no link is set, and the edit button switches it to the input.

Pressing Enter or Escape in the input saves the link — the value is trimmed and prefixed with https:// unless it already contains :// or starts with / or [ — and closing the popup while editing also saves what was typed.

The popup auto-hides after a short delay once the pointer moves away from the element, the gap between the element and the popup, and the popup itself, but stays open while the input is open and is hidden while dragging, resizing, or rotating the element.

Clicking the link icon at the element's top-right corner (press and release both on it) opens the link in the same tab when it points to the current site (contains the site's own address or starts with /) and in a new tab otherwise; the link text shown in the popup opens the same way.
The remove button clears the link from the element and closes the popup.

Hovering the pointer over the small link icon of an element that has a link now shows a pointer cursor and a link tooltip, and the click listener is attached only while hovering that icon; moving off the icon hides the tooltip and detaches the listener.

A full click (pointer press and release both on the link icon) on a non-selected linked element now opens its link: links pointing to the app's own origin or starting with a slash open in the same tab, other links open in a new tab with the opener reference cleared, and bare domains without a protocol get https:// added automatically.
Pressing on the link icon of an already selected element now stops the press from changing the selection (an early return was added), so the click opens the link instead of starting a drag or resize.

Selecting exactly one element that has a link, or dragging a selection box that ends up containing exactly one linked element, now shows an 'info' hyperlink popup; a selection containing more than one element does not show it, and the popup renders as a Hyperlink panel only when exactly one element is selected.

Supporting plumbing: pointer-down now records the down event and clears the context-menu-open flag, and pointer-up records the up event; the cursor logic during hover was restructured but should behave the same outside link icons.

Only one changed function in this group affects runtime behavior: version pinning for libraries now embeds the chosen version directly in the generated package's HTML import map instead of writing a version.json file, and generates a framework entry file that imports the pinned library entry point and mounts the app.

The generated HTML previously resolved library versions at runtime from version.json plus import-map overrides; it now ships with the pinned version and framework entry pre-rendered, so the dev server and the distributed page use the same fixed versions.

A separate service-worker-related fix keeps a previously cached package-configuration response when a fresh network fetch fails, so offline users keep working with the last known versions instead of losing them.

Verify: with the dev server running, choose a library and a non-latest version in the wizard (for example an older major version), generate the package, open the preview in the browser, and confirm the page loads using exactly that version, with no browser console errors about a missing versions file.

uncertainty: Before/after code was supplied only for the panel action, the help dialog shortcut, and the tooltip helper's export; the remaining changed tooltip functions (tooltip update and positioning, link icon coordinates, tooltip show and hide) have no before/after code in the evidence, so their exact old-versus-new behavior is unknown, and the link action's own editor behavior is not described in the supplied context — the checks verify the feature end to end rather than specific changes.

The application context supplied no navigation paths, screen names, or verbatim UI labels for these areas, and the exact conditions under which the new context-menu link entry appears are not documented; the hover or pointer wiring that first shows the link popup belongs to other parts of this release, so testers should explore the editor canvas and may need to discover the menu entry's visibility rules themselves.

The underlying link editing behavior is delivered by companion changes outside this group, so if the new shortcut or tooltip does nothing, the cause may lie in those companion changes rather than in the pieces reviewed here.

Drawings saved from this version now include an empty link field on every element; compatibility of that element format with older app versions or third-party embedders was not established by the supplied evidence, so cross-version save and reopen behavior is unverified.

No removed code was supplied for any of these changes, so no old-versus-new input divergence could be identified; the link flow should be verified functionally end to end, and note that links without :// (for example mailto:user@example.com) receive an https:// prefix because only :// counts as fully qualified — confirm that is intended.

The link-open path assumes a pointer-move already happened (it stores the hovered link element and both the down and up events); on a touch device where a tap produces little or no pointer movement, tapping the link icon may not open the link or could fail, so a tap test on touch hardware or device emulation is recommended but the expected behavior is not established by the evidence.

The exact user-visible labeling for picking a non-latest library version in the wizard is not described in the supplied context, so locate the version control by its current on-screen label; if the version list is hidden behind an advanced option, that step of the checks may need adjusting.

report.summary: Text attached to shapes can now be vertically aligned top, middle, or bottom, and it keeps that alignment when the shape is resized, flipped, or edited.
keyChanges: When a shape containing bound text is resized, the text is now repositioned according to its vertical alignment: top-aligned text stays pinned to the top edge and bottom-aligned text to the bottom edge, each with the standard small padding, where previously resizing always re-centered the text vertically.

The on-canvas text editor now opens and rests at the position matching the bound text's vertical alignment; bottom alignment is newly supported, and a top-aligned text's editor is no longer forced to the vertical center of its container.

A shared vertical-alignment constant (top, middle, bottom) was introduced and adopted across element creation, text handling, and chart defaults; the chart default value is unchanged (middle), so chart creation, pasted-spreadsheet previews, and SVG export are expected to behave exactly as before.
The editor's action registry now recognizes a vertical-alignment change action, enabling the new alignment option for bound text.

Selecting elements now shows a vertical alignment control for text attached to shapes in the desktop shape actions panel and the mobile menu, and it appears only when every selected element has attached text or is a shape bound to text.

Re-editing text that is attached to a shape no longer resets its vertical alignment to the default middle when the text is not centered in the shape, so an alignment the user picked now survives later edits.

Bottom-aligned text attached to a shape is now drawn a small fixed padding above the shape's bottom edge instead of at the old baseline-based offset, changing the live canvas and every image produced through the shared export pipeline, including copy as PNG or SVG, the image export dialog, saving to an image file, and library publish previews.

Text attached to a shape (bound text) gains a new vertical alignment control with three options — align top, center vertically, align bottom — shown as three new button icons in the text properties area; the action is registered app-wide and each change is recorded in undo history.

Bound text inside a shape is no longer always vertically centered: the repositioning routine now pins it near the top edge, the bottom edge, or keeps it centered per the chosen alignment; only centered text keeps the old behavior where an oversized shape grows to fit the text — top- or bottom-aligned text no longer grows the shape and can extend past its edge.

Because font-size changes (increase, decrease, set), font-family changes, horizontal text-alignment changes, and paste-styles all reuse that repositioning routine, they now preserve a chosen top/bottom alignment instead of re-centering the text; centered text behaves exactly as before.
The horizontal text-alignment picker (Left/Center/Right) was restructured with no intended behavior change; it still reads the current alignment from the bound text when a shape is selected.
The new vertical picker and the horizontal picker share the same underlying selection group, so their highlighted states can interact.
qaChecks: Verify with vertical alignment set to top, dragging a resize handle to make the shape taller leaves the text pinned just below the top edge, where the previous version re-centered it.
Check bottom alignment by making the shape taller and then shorter: the text must stay attached to the bottom edge with its small padding at both sizes.
Confirm middle-aligned text still ends up vertically centered after resizing, and that resizing several shapes together in one multi-selection keeps each bound text at its own aligned position.
Confirm double-clicking a shape with bottom-aligned text opens the on-canvas editor over the text at the bottom of the shape, not vertically centered as before.
Check top-aligned text: the editor opens at the top of the shape, aligned with the rendered text.
Ensure that deleting lines until the container shrinks back to its original height leaves a bottom-aligned editor pinned at the bottom instead of snapping back to the center.

Test the flip vertical and flip horizontal actions on the selected shape: after each flip the text must remain attached to the shape and hold its aligned position rather than re-centering or detaching.
Verify text attached to a shape and set to bottom alignment sits a small fixed padding above the shape's bottom edge on the canvas, not at the old baseline-based position.
Test copying the same bottom-aligned attached text to the clipboard as PNG and as SVG and Confirm both outputs anchor the text at the shape's bottom edge, matching the canvas.
Confirm the PNG and SVG previews in the image export dialog also show the bottom-aligned text at the bottom of the shape.
Test saving the drawing to an image file and Confirm the saved image shows the bottom-aligned text anchored at the shape's bottom edge.
Verify that after setting attached text to bottom alignment, double-clicking the shape to edit the text and adding a line keeps the text anchored at the bottom instead of jumping back to the middle.
Check the case the previous version reset by re-editing attached text that is left-aligned instead of centered, and Ensure it keeps the bottom alignment rather than resetting to the default middle.
Confirm the vertical alignment control appears in the shape actions panel when a single shape containing attached text is selected.

Verify the control disappears when that shape is selected together with a plain shape that has no attached text, since it should show only when every selected element has attached text or is a shape bound to text.
Ensure the same vertical alignment control appears in the mobile menu when the shape with attached text is selected on a mobile-sized viewport.

Verify the three new alignment buttons (top, vertical center, bottom) appear next to the horizontal text alignment buttons and each one moves the attached text to the top edge, vertical middle, or bottom edge of the shape with a small gap from the edge.
Test selecting only the shape (not the text) and clicking a vertical option: the attached text should still reposition, and the change should be reversible with undo.

Ensure with text taller than the shape, Align top keeps the text pinned at the top (it may extend past the shape's bottom edge) and the shape keeps its size, while vertically centered text still grows the shape to fit as before.
Confirm picking a vertical option does not clear the highlighted horizontal alignment button, since both pickers share one selection group.

Verify that after choosing Align top, increasing and then decreasing the font size keeps the text pinned at the top of the shape rather than re-centering it (the old behavior re-centered on every font change).
Verify changing the font family and switching the horizontal alignment on top- or bottom-aligned text also keeps the text at its chosen edge.
Verify vertically centered text still re-centers and the shape still grows when the font size makes the text taller than the shape, matching the previous behavior.
Verify Left, Center, and Right still highlight the current alignment for both standalone text and text attached to a shape, and switching between them re-aligns the text as before.
Verify that opening it and changing the font size of its attached text leaves the text vertically centered where it was before, with no jump to the top or bottom edge.
uncertainty: The supplied context does not show where users change vertical alignment (the new action was registered but no control was identified), and drawings saved before this change may hold top-aligned bound text positioned under the old always-center rule, so the first resize or edit after updating can visibly re-pin such text; treat that shift as intended realignment rather than data loss unless the text detaches from or overflows its shape.

This group's evidence only special-cases bottom-aligned attached text in canvas drawing; no equivalent handling for top-aligned text appears here, so if the new control also offers top alignment, its on-canvas and exported position is not covered by this group and may be implemented elsewhere in the release.

The evidence does not establish what vertical alignment value attached text carries by default or in drawings saved before this change; the new positioning only preserves the old centered behavior when that value is the centered one, so if existing text stores a different value its position could shift on the next font or alignment change — cover this with the saved-drawing check.

report.summary: This release overhauls how the app handles files, so opening, importing, sharing, and saving them all now work through one unified system.
keyChanges: Opening .excalidraw scenes, .excalidrawlib libraries, and images from the file picker or drag-and-drop now goes through a reworked loading pipeline that re-creates files with a detected type; behavior should be unchanged for normal files, but a blob whose type claims PNG/SVG yet lacks an embedded scene, or an empty/zero-byte file, now surfaces a clear invalid-file error instead of a broken state.

The file-type detection now checks image bytes by magic number, so images with a mismatched extension (e.g. a JPEG named .png) are re-labeled on import and pasted/dropped images should render correctly instead of failing.

Live collaboration and Excalidraw+ export now convert data with the new helper before encryption; if this path fails, broadcasts or cloud saves would be blank, so verify a shared session still syncs and an Excalidraw+ export still returns a valid link.
A new save/load round-trip path was added for restoring shared scenes; opening a share link or a saved scene should load with the same theme and elements as before.

Opening a scene file now runs it through a type-normalization step: files with no MIME type (.excalidraw or .excalidrawlib files) are re-typed by extension, and image files are re-typed by their leading bytes when the extension does not match the content, so a scene PNG renamed with a wrong image extension now loads instead of failing with an invalid-file error.

The helper that reads a file's raw bytes for PNG scene metadata was moved from the image module to the shared data module and is now also imported by the encryption module (where it converts Blob data to a buffer before encrypting); every flow that embeds or reads a scene inside an image — save with embedded scene, copy as PNG or SVG, open and drag-and-drop import, library imports, and shared-link restore — now uses the shared copy, so these paths need smoke tests even though no behavior change is expected.

The example app for the embeddable package gains a 'Load Scene or Library' button that opens a file picker and loads the chosen scene or library into the editor, and the package's public entry now exports the file-loading helper so integrating developers can use it directly.

Files dropped on the canvas, opened when the app launches, and received through the share target are now loaded by a single routine that first normalizes the file, detects from the file content whether it is a scene or a library, then loads the drawing or imports the library items, and shows an error message for anything it cannot parse.

When a file is dropped, the file and its operating-system file handle are now captured first, in the same event frame, and passed along so an opened drawing stays linked to its on-disk file for later saves; the old browser-capability branching was removed.

Library files are now detected by content instead of the .excalidrawlib extension or MIME type, so a misnamed library file imports correctly and a misnamed scene file loads as a scene; however, the old code explicitly opened the library panel when a library file was dropped, and the unified loader no longer does this.
The embeddable package's utility exports now also expose the unified loader and the MIME type constants; this has no visible effect in the app itself.

report.summary: Selecting a line or arrow now puts it into a point-editing state right on the canvas, letting you drag its points directly instead of using a separate edit mode.
keyChanges: Selecting a single arrow or line no longer shows any corner, side, or rotation handles — straight two-point arrows previously showed two corner handles plus rotation, and multi-point arrows showed the full handle set — and instead the line's own points render as circular handles meant to be dragged directly.

When one of the selected line's points is under the cursor, a faint translucent purple circle highlights that point (except when the point is already selected in point-editing mode), and while dragging a single arrow or line its rectangular selection border is no longer drawn.

In point-editing mode the point handles are now twice their previous size and change from red and salmon coloring to indigo, while freehand strokes keep their previous direction-dependent handle behavior.

A new internal state tracking the selected line is added with a null default: it is kept in browser storage but stripped from saved files, exports, and collaboration sync, so exports and other collaborators should never carry or show your line-selection state.

Because arrows and lines no longer expose any resize handle, the flip actions can no longer find a handle to pull and now exit without changing the shape, so flipping a selected arrow or line silently does nothing where it previously mirrored it.

Lines and arrows now stay in a selected state that displays their points as draggable handles: pressing and dragging a point reshapes the element without entering the old editing mode, and releasing an endpoint now re-evaluates its connection to nearby shapes, attaching or detaching it.

While a line or arrow is selected, pointer targeting for it drops the whole-bounding-box shortcut and uses the exact drawn shape, so clicks in empty areas inside its bounding box pass through instead of grabbing it.
Right-clicking an unselected line or arrow now also selects it and shows its point handles behind the context menu, and on touch devices the same applies via long-press, which shares the same path.

Point handles appear only when exactly one line or arrow is selected: box-selecting or shift-clicking further elements clears them, shrinking the selection back to a single line or arrow brings them back, and a new cleanup removes stale handles when the selected element leaves the selection.

Hovering a selected line or arrow now shows a pointer cursor over its points and a move cursor over its body (previously only in the old editing mode), and a helper that tracks the trailing point while drawing or extending lines was renamed with no intended behavior change.

After finishing a multi-point line or arrow with Escape or the checkmark button, and after Select all when exactly one line or arrow is selectable, the shape now stays selected in point-editing mode with its point handles visible instead of dropping back to plain selection.
Selecting multiple elements at once or locking the selection now exits point-editing mode, where previously the point-editing state could linger on a multi-selected or newly locked line.

The point handles drawn on selected lines and arrows shrink from 20 to 10 pixels, while the click tolerance for grabbing a point stays at about 11 pixels, so a point can still be grabbed slightly outside its smaller visible handle.

Clicking and dragging the points of a line that is merely selected, without double-clicking into full point editing, now follows the same handling as full editing, so point interactions must be regression-tested in both states.
qaChecks: Verify selecting a single bent multi-point arrow shows only its own points as circular handles with no corner, side, or rotation handles on the bounding box, where previously the full handle set including rotation appeared.
Verify selecting a straight two-point arrow likewise shows no corner or rotation handles, where previously two corner handles and a rotation handle appeared.

Confirm hovering near one of the selected arrow's points shows a faint translucent purple circle at that point, and that the circle is absent for a point that is already selected in point-editing mode.
Ensure no rectangular selection border is drawn around the selected arrow or line, whether hovering or dragging it, while a selected rectangle keeps its usual selection border.

Test flip horizontal and flip vertical on a selected diagonal arrow and on a straight line; the expected outcome after this change is that nothing visibly changes, so if mirroring is expected behavior, log it as a regression.
Verify flip horizontal and flip vertical still mirror a selected rectangle as before.

Verify a PNG or SVG export taken while an arrow is selected contains no selection border, point handles, or faint purple highlight circle — selection rendering is switched off for exports but the new hover highlight is not covered by that switch, so explicitly confirm the image is clean.
Verify a saved file reopened later, and a collaborator's view of the same scene, show the line unselected with no carried-over selection state.
Ensure reloading the page while an arrow is selected and a point was hovered restores the scene cleanly with no leftover highlight circle or error.

Verify the point handles in point-editing mode are noticeably larger than before (double the previous size), that the currently selected point is filled indigo where it was previously salmon red, and that all points are outlined in indigo where they were previously outlined in red.
Verify a selected straight freehand stroke still shows the same corner handles as before, two corners for a diagonal stroke and four for a horizontal or vertical stroke.
Verify selecting an arrow together with other elements still shows the shared bounding box with corner handles, so arrows can still be resized and moved as part of a multi-selection.
Check: click a line or arrow once - its points should appear as small draggable handles, and clicking on empty canvas afterwards should clear them.
Verify: press and drag a middle point of the selected line to a new position - the point should follow the pointer and the line should keep its new shape after release.

Ensure: drag the endpoint of the selected arrow onto the rectangle and release - the arrow should attach and move with the rectangle afterwards; then drag the endpoint off the shape and release - it should detach cleanly.
Confirm: with the arrow selected, hovering over one of its points shows a pointer cursor and hovering over the arrow's body shows a move cursor.

Test: with the bent line selected, click inside its bounding box but on empty space away from the drawn stroke (for example inside the open corner of the L) - the click should pass through instead of dragging the line.
Validate: with the bent line still selected, click on the shape sitting behind that empty bounding-box area - that shape behind should be picked up rather than the line being dragged.
Verify: right-click an unselected arrow - the context menu opens and the arrow is selected with its point handles shown.
Ensure: right-click the rectangle - no line point handles appear for it.
Check: on a touch device, long-press an unselected arrow - the arrow should end up selected with its point handles shown.
Check: drag a selection box around exactly one arrow - its point handles appear; repeat including the arrow plus a rectangle - no handles are shown.
Confirm: select the arrow, then shift-click a rectangle to add it - the handles clear; shift-click the rectangle again to remove it - the handles reappear for the lone arrow.

Validate: draw an arrow by dragging and keep the pointer moving before release - the trailing point should follow the cursor and the arrow should finalize correctly on release; then with a drawn line selected, hold Alt or Option and move the pointer to extend it - a new trailing point should follow the cursor and be committed on the next click, working as before.
Verify that finishing a multi-point line or arrow with Escape or the checkmark button leaves the shape selected in point-editing mode with its point handles visible.
Check that clicking a point on a merely selected line selects it and that dragging moves the point with the connected segments following, without entering full edit mode first.

Confirm that Alt+click while fully editing a line's points still adds a point at the cursor, and that Alt+click on a merely selected line now behaves like a normal point click rather than doing nothing.
Ensure hovering along a selected line shows the move cursor over the body and the pointer cursor within about 11 pixels of a point even though the drawn handle is smaller.
Verify that Select all on a canvas whose only selectable element is a line or arrow puts that shape into point-editing mode with point handles visible.
Check that Select all with several selectable elements exits any active point-editing mode and yields a plain multi-selection without point handles.
Ensure locked elements and text bound inside shapes are still excluded from Select all.
Check that locking the selection while a line is in point-editing mode exits point-editing mode so the point handles disappear while the element stays selected and locked.
Ensure unlocking preserves the existing point-editing state instead of clearing it.
Confirm the locked line shows no point handles and its points can no longer be grabbed or dragged.
Verify the drawn point handles are about 10 pixels at default zoom, roughly half their previous size.

Check that clicking just outside the smaller visible handle still grabs the point because the grab tolerance remains about 11 pixels, and that when two points overlap the rightmost point takes precedence.
uncertainty: Flipping arrows and lines previously worked through the resize handles that this change removes, so the flip actions now exit without modifying arrows and lines; confirm with the team whether dropping flip support for arrows and lines is intended or a regression that must be fixed before release.

The pass-through of clicks in empty bounding-box areas while a line or arrow is selected removes a grab area users may have relied on; the code change looks intentional, so confirm this stricter targeting is accepted before release.
The grab tolerance around a point stays about 11 pixels while the drawn handle shrinks to 10 pixels, so confirm whether the handle is intentionally allowed to look smaller than its clickable area.

checks: Verify the drawn point handles are about 10 pixels at default zoom, roughly half their previous size.

Check that clicking just outside the smaller visible handle still grabs the point because the grab tolerance remains about 11 pixels, and that when two points overlap the rightmost point takes precedence.

report.summary: Editing points on lines and arrows is improved, so every segment can now be grabbed and adjusted directly instead of only the middle of the whole line.
keyChanges: While editing a multi-point line or arrow, every segment now shows its own midpoint handle; previously at most a single midpoint was offered, effectively only for two-point lines.

For round-curve lines the midpoint is computed on the curve, and clicking any midpoint now inserts the new point into the segment that was clicked at its correct position, instead of always right after the first point.

Very short segments — shorter than about four handle widths on screen at the current zoom — no longer offer a midpoint handle, and hover detection stays locked to a midpoint until the pointer moves beyond roughly one handle-size distance.

In live collaboration the point handles of the line being edited are now drawn from the on-screen element list, fixing a case where the handles rendered blank because the looked-up element was one version ahead of its cached shape.
Simple two-point lines keep their previous behavior: one center midpoint that highlights on hover and splits the line into three points when clicked.

Mid-point handles on curved multi-point lines and arrows are now placed using an exact length-measured point on the curve instead of the plain centre between the two end points, so when hovering a selected line the hover highlight and the clickable middle handle should sit exactly on the curve.

The midpoint position is computed via a new binary search over sampled curve points, so an interval of 0.5 should land at 50% of the curve's length, which changes where the handle appears on non-symmetric curves and how precisely you can grab it.

Whether a segment is too short to show its middle handle now uses the actual curve length for curved lines (rather than the straight-line distance), so very short curved segments should correctly hide their midpoint handle.
Point-equality checks are stricter: a null point no longer equals any point, so empty or removed points on lines should be handled without the editor confusing them with real coordinates.

Curve sampling now explicitly appends the curve's end point when missing and returns an empty point list when no curve shape exists, so edge cases like very short curves, deleted points, or unbuilt shapes should not crash the editor or misplace handles.

While editing a line or arrow, hovering or clicking a segment midpoint now highlights and adds a point on any segment, replacing the old behavior where only a two-point line had a single clickable center midpoint; for curved segments the midpoint is computed along the curve, and midpoint results are cached by element version and zoom.

Adding points by dragging inside point-edit mode now reads the editor state directly and reports that no line is being edited once the session has ended, with the canvas pointer handler made null-safe, so moving the pointer after leaving edit mode should be error-free.
Every path that enters point-edit mode (double-clicking a selected line, right-click selection, finalize with Escape, select all) now starts the session with no segment midpoint marked as hovered.
qaChecks: Verify that in edit mode each segment shows its own midpoint handle and clicking the midpoint of the second or last segment inserts the new point into that segment at its middle, with the line's shape and selection box staying correct.
Test a curved round-style segment: the midpoint handle sits on the curved stroke rather than the straight line between its endpoints, and clicking adds the point on the curve.

Confirm a very short segment (a tiny zig-zag, well under four handle widths at the current zoom) shows no midpoint handle and clicking along it adds no stray point while the segment still moves normally.
Ensure dragging points and zooming in and out during editing keeps every midpoint centered on its segment with no stale or misplaced handles.
Verify hovering the middle of the line highlights the midpoint and shows the pointer cursor, and clicking inserts a point exactly in the center so the line ends up with three points.
Confirm the highlight clears and the cursor returns to normal once the pointer moves away from the midpoint.
Ensure a multi-point line that is selected but not in edit mode offers no midpoint handles, and the per-segment midpoints appear only after entering edit mode.
Ensure that while editing a line's points the endpoint and midpoint handles render immediately and keep updating as edits and remote changes arrive, instead of coming out blank.

Verify that after drawing a curved multi-point line and selecting it with the selection tool, hovering near the middle of any segment shows the midpoint handle exactly on the curve, and clicking it splits the segment at that on-curve position rather than at an offset.
Test dragging an existing midpoint handle along a curved segment: the handle should follow the cursor and stay attached to the curve without jumping or detaching.
Confirm that on a very short curved segment (zoomed out or with two nearly touching points), the midpoint handle is hidden (segment treated as too short), while longer curved segments still show it.
Ensure that deleting a middle point from a curved multi-point line reflows the curve smoothly and the remaining midpoint handles still sit on the new curve without error or displaced handles.
Verify that rapid delete and undo of points on a curved line never produces a crash or a handle rendered at an impossible position (for example far outside the canvas).

Confirm that as the pointer moves along a selected curved line, only the segment under the cursor is highlighted and its handles update at the correct on-curve positions, with no flicker or stale highlights on other segments.
Verify hovering exactly over an existing endpoint or corner point does not incorrectly trigger the midpoint cursor or highlight the wrong segment.

Validate that exporting a drawing containing curved multi-point lines to PNG or via the export dialog produces an image where the curves render identically to the on-screen canvas, with no missing or distorted curve segments.
Confirm that ordinary straight lines and arrows still render, select, and drag normally, with their point handles appearing in the usual positions (no regression from the curve-handling changes).
Verify hovering the midpoint of each segment of the three-plus-point line highlights that segment's midpoint and shows the pointer cursor, which previously only worked on two-point lines.

Verify clicking a segment midpoint on the multi-segment line inserts a point exactly at that midpoint while the rest of the line keeps its shape, and the two-point line still shows a single midpoint at its center.
Verify on the curved line the highlighted midpoint sits on the drawn curve rather than on the straight line between the endpoints.
Verify after editing one line and switching to edit a different one, each line shows its own segment midpoints, and undoing a point insertion restores midpoints matching the reverted shape.

Verify holding Alt and dragging across the canvas adds points along the cursor path; releasing Alt removes the trailing uncommitted point, and clicking commits the points so they persist after leaving edit mode.
Verify adding points to an arrow that is attached to shapes keeps both ends attached after committing and leaving edit mode.
Verify double-clicking a selected line enters point-edit mode with point handles visible and no midpoint highlighted as hovered.
Verify right-clicking an unselected line selects it and opens the context menu, and point editing still works on that line afterwards.
Verify pressing Escape exits point-edit mode cleanly and, after using select all, the drawing is left in a normal selectable state with no line stuck in editing.
Verify moving the pointer freely over the canvas without editing any line, including immediately after leaving a point-edit session, causes no error, freeze, or stuck cursor.
Verify exporting or copying the drawing as PNG and SVG renders the lines and arrows as they appear on the canvas, with no editing handles included.
uncertainty: The exact previous midpoint behavior for lines with three or more points is not fully visible in the before-and-after evidence, so per-segment midpoints are treated as new behavior; verify that clicking the midpoints of two adjacent segments in one editing session inserts each point into its own segment and never duplicates or reorders points.

Whether the stricter midpoint placement changes the expected position of the middle handle on symmetric versus asymmetric curves compared to the previous release is not documented here, so QA should compare handle placement against the prior version on a representative curved drawing to confirm the new position is intended.

The change graph reaches the shared scene-rendering path used by image export, clipboard copy, and library publishing previews, but the removed logic only applied to editing-mode handles, so the evidence does not demonstrate a user-visible export change and the export checks above are smoke tests only.

report.summary: The drawing editor's customizable bottom bar now takes custom content placed directly inside it instead of through a callback, and its upgrade link only appears for signed-in users.
keyChanges: Custom footer content is now supplied as children of the editor and rendered through a Footer component instead of a footer-render prop; the app's footer child shows a link to Excalidraw+ (previously labelled Go to Excalidraw+ and only shown to signed-in users) plus the encrypted shield icon.

The old footer builder's small-screen branch that listed languages under a Language label was removed entirely, so the same footer content now shows at every screen size and no language picker appears in the footer.
The encrypted shield icon (tooltip plus link to the end-to-end encryption page) and the footer component moved to new locations with named exports; their visible content should be unchanged.
Sign-in detection moved to a shared constant that also gates the welcome screen's switch-to-Excalidraw+ prompt, so sign-in behavior should be unchanged.

Custom footer content is now passed as children into the editor and renders in the centered region of the bottom footer on desktop; the old custom-footer render prop is no longer read anywhere, so integrations still passing it show nothing, and the mobile menu no longer renders any custom footer content.
Children are matched by component name, so only a recognized named footer child is rendered; plain text, plain HTML-tag children, or unnamed components passed to the editor are silently ignored.
In the showcase app, a new "Go to Excalidraw+" link (opens the Plus app in a new tab) appears only for signed-in Excalidraw+ users, while the encryption shield icon and link behave as before.

Custom bottom-bar content must now be placed directly inside the drawing editor component instead of being supplied through the old footer-rendering callback property, so any existing integration that relied on that callback no longer shows its custom content until it migrates.

Content supplied the new way renders in a new centered region of the bottom bar between the zoom and undo-redo controls and the right-side controls, and it animates along with those controls when zen mode is toggled.
The Go to Excalidraw+ button now appears only when the browser holds a cookie indicating an Excalidraw+ signed-in session.
The encrypted-link shield icon keeps its tooltip, accessible label, and blog link after its relocation, while the remaining edits are import-path and naming cleanups with no visible behavior change.

The editor component no longer renders a footer via the old footer rendering API, so any host application still supplying one will show nothing; custom footer content is now passed as React children instead.

The public editor component renders this changed component directly, so every embedded editor surface shares the same behaviour change and any consumer relying on the old API needs migrating to children.

A new central footer component is now exported from the package entry point for reuse by host applications, with no graph-traced dependents inside this package, so it needs no separate QA path beyond the migration above.
qaChecks: Verify a signed-in user sees the Excalidraw+ link in the footer while a signed-out visitor does not see it.
Check the encrypted shield icon still appears in the footer and still opens the end-to-end encryption page with its tooltip text.
Ensure zoom and undo/redo controls in the footer still render and respond after the footer restructuring.

Check the footer on a small screen now shows the same content as desktop (plus link and shield icon) with no Language list, and confirm the app still offers a language setting somewhere in its interface.
Verify the welcome screen still shows the switch-to-Excalidraw+ prompt for a signed-in user and omits it for a signed-out visitor.

Test a host page that passes a Footer child into the editor and confirm the child content renders in the editor's bottom footer; content supplied through the removed footer-render prop no longer appears and must be migrated to children.
Verify the custom footer content appears in the centered region of the bottom footer, rendered once and aligned correctly (not duplicated or shifted).
Test an editor with no footer children, and one given plain text or unnamed children instead: no custom content should render and the editor should load without errors.
Check the editor's distraction-free (zen) mode: turn it on and confirm the centered footer content slides away, then returns when zen mode is turned off.
Confirm that changing only the custom footer children while the drawing stays unchanged still refreshes the displayed footer content.
Verify the canvas actions and collaborators list still render in the mobile menu panel with no layout gap where the old custom footer slot used to sit.
Confirm no custom footer content appears in the mobile menu anymore, since that slot was intentionally removed.
Check that a signed-in Excalidraw+ user sees a "Go to Excalidraw+" link that opens the Plus app in a new tab, and that a signed-out user does not see the link.
Verify the encryption shield icon still renders, shows its tooltip on hover, and opens its end-to-end-encryption blog link in a new tab.
Verify the footer's standard controls still render and work: the zoom actions, undo and redo (hidden in view-only mode), and the shortcuts help control on the footer's right side.

Verify both example buttons appear in the centered bottom area: clicking the icon button activates the comment tool and changes the cursor, and clicking the button labeled custom footer shows the This is dummy footer alert.

Verify the existing left-side controls (zoom, undo/redo, and finalize on touch screens) and the right-side controls still render and work around the new centered area, including their animation when zen mode is toggled on and off.

Verify the migration case: content supplied through the old footer-rendering callback is no longer rendered anywhere in the bottom bar, and only content placed directly inside the editor component is displayed.
Verify that with the signed-in cookie present the Go to Excalidraw+ button appears and opens the Excalidraw+ app link in a new tab.
Verify that after clearing cookies the button does not render at all, leaving no empty clickable area.
Verify hovering the shield icon still shows the encrypted tooltip and that clicking it opens the end-to-end-encryption blog post in a new tab.
Verify the plain editor embed loads and all canvas interactions still work as before.
Test an embed still using the old footer API and confirm the footer no longer appears rather than duplicating or erroring.
Ensure an embed migrated to the children-based footer displays the custom footer content below the editor as before the change.
Confirm no child content renders outside the intended footer area or is cropped in view mode and light/dark themes.
uncertainty: The old small-screen footer language list was invoked from code that passed the desktop flag, so whether mobile users actually saw it before this change is not established by the evidence; the new footer has no language list at any size, so if the app offers no other language control, the footer rework is where it was lost.

The editor UI's memoized re-render check dropped the old custom-footer prop comparison but does not compare the new children, so a host that changes only the footer children may see stale content until app state or drawing elements change; whether live children updates must work was not established by the supplied context.

The signed-in check matches the cookie name as plain text anywhere in the browser cookie string, so an unrelated cookie merely containing that name could falsely show the Go to Excalidraw+ button; test with a realistic cookie set containing unrelated cookies, and note no navigation routes or page labels were supplied so all surfaces must be located manually.

The supplied context provides no concrete pages, routes, or labels where the editor is embedded, so the tester must locate a host page or example themselves; no consumer was graph-traced, so whether any caller still uses the old footer API is unverified.
