report.summary: This release is an internal cleanup that changes how the editor determines which items are selected, with no intended user-visible change, so selection-driven actions across the app need regression testing.
keyChanges: All main canvas interaction paths (pointer down, move, and up, resizing, rotating, context menu, double-click, text editing, color eyedropper, touch context menu) now read the current selection through a new cached method instead of recomputing it from the element list each time; intended behavior is identical, so any regression would appear as stale or wrong selections.

Updating frame contents after moving, aligning, distributing, or flipping elements now resolves the selection through the same cached API, and the shared frame-membership helper now requires the app instance, making framed and grouped selections the risk area.

Group selection bookkeeping (grouping, ungrouping, select-all, duplicate, paste and library drop, double-click into a group) now passes the app instance to use the cached path, while the ungroup path passes null and keeps the old behavior.

A few paths that previously counted deleted-but-selected elements (the color-picking target check, the selected frames computed on pointer release, and the element loop during Ctrl/Cmd drag-duplication) now operate on non-deleted elements only.

Selection lookups across the editor now go through a new per-scene cache, used by copy and clipboard exports, duplicate, group and ungroup, lock, align, distribute, zoom-to-fit-selection, frame selection commands, text binding, context menus, keyboard shortcuts, and the hint tips, so a cache that fails to refresh would make a command act on the previous selection.

Add to Library now reads the selection through that cache with the same inclusions as before (text bound to shapes and everything inside selected frames), still refuses images with the existing not-supported message, and still confirms a successful add.

Flip horizontal and vertical, and Select All, now pass the app instance when updating frame membership and group selection so those updates use the cached selection, while Duplicate explicitly bypasses the cache when regrouping its copies.

Destroying the editor scene, which runs when the editor component unmounts as in embedded integrations, now clears all element lists and the new selection cache so a remount cannot see stale elements or selections.

The action framework's contracts were widened so action predicates, labels, and keyboard tests can receive the app instance, a code-level contract change flagged for the flip actions that has no user-visible effect of its own.

The two zoom-to-fit-selection commands (the fill-the-viewport variant and the fit-within-viewport variant) now determine the selected shapes from the app's live scene through a new cache instead of from the snapshot passed to the action, and when nothing is selected they must still zoom to the entire drawing.

The context-sensitive hint text in the desktop toolbar and the mobile toolbar no longer receives the drawing's element list and instead reads the selection through the app instance, so incorrect wiring would show wrong or missing hints.

Every action panel rendered by the action manager now receives the app instance, which enables the changes above and touches panels in the selected-shape actions menu, the file and link export dialog, the editor footer, and the mobile app toolbar.
No new user-facing behavior is intended in this group, so the QA risk is a stale cached selection or broken prop plumbing rather than a new feature.

The editor now resolves the current selection through one cached scene query in keyboard handling, the line and arrow multi-point editing action, group selection after pasting or inserting elements, and the hyperlink popup check, keeping the same selection rules including attached shape text and frame members where previously requested.

The line and arrow multi-point editing action now reads its selection through the cached path for its context-menu availability, its start and exit toggle, and its menu wording, so the context-menu entry and the Ctrl or Cmd plus Enter shortcut should behave exactly as before.

The app instance is now passed into keyboard shortcut matching and context-menu label lookups, and grouped elements added via paste, drag-and-drop of library items, or programmatic insertion are grouped for selection with the app supplied.
Frame and group typing imports and two new type-only utilities have no runtime effect and need no separate testing.

The lock/unlock action — its right-click context-menu entry, its Ctrl or Cmd plus Shift plus L shortcut, and the lock operation itself — now reads the selection through the editor's scene, while the rules stay the same: locking still includes attached text and frame contents, the action is still withheld when a selected element is locked and inside a frame, and single versus multi selections still show the lock/unlock versus lock-all/unlock-all labels depending on whether every selected element is unlocked.

The six alignment controls (align top, bottom, left, right, center horizontally, center vertically) now compute their visibility the same scene-based way, keeping the rule that they appear only when more than one element is selected and stay hidden when any frame is in the selection.

All six align commands (left edge, right edge, top edge, bottom edge, center horizontally, center vertically) now pick the selected elements from the scene's live selection instead of filtering the passed element list, and the frame-membership update that runs after aligning now goes through the editor instance; alignment results are expected to be unchanged.

Copy and cut now build the copied set of elements from the scene with the same inclusion rules as before (text attached to shapes and frame contents included); these copy and cut commands apply on mobile devices, and cut still copies the selection before deleting it.
Copy as PNG and copy as SVG use the same scene-based selection and keep the fallback that copies the whole drawing when nothing is selected.

The copy-text command's availability rule and action now use the scene selection; it should still appear only when the selection contains text (including text attached to shapes) and copy the selected texts joined by a blank line.

Group and Ungroup now resolve the selected elements through the drawing scene's cached selection instead of filtering the element list handed to the action; the rule that text attached to a selected shape still counts for grouping is preserved, and after ungrouping the follow-up selection recompute deliberately runs without that cache.

Distribute horizontally and vertically use the same new selection lookup and now pass the app instance into the frame-membership update, which should keep removing selected elements that end up outside their frame after being spaced.

Button visibility and availability rules are unchanged in intent but are now evaluated from the scene-backed selection: Group requires at least two selected elements that are not already all in one group, and Distribute requires more than one selected element with no frame among them.
No new user-facing behavior is intended; the risk is a silent change in which elements each action treats as selected.

All six text-binding behaviors (binding text to a container or arrow, freeing attached text, and wrapping text in a container, each in both its menu-visibility check and its actual action) now read the current selection from the scene's shared selection lookup, which caches results, instead of from the element list handed to the command.

The two frame behaviors, selecting all elements inside a frame and removing all elements from a frame, plus their shared visibility rule that exactly one selected element exists and it must be a frame, made the same switch.

The stated selection rules are unchanged (bind requires exactly two elements with one text and one bindable container without attached text; unbind requires at least one element with attached text; wrap requires only text elements), so the release effect should be invisible to users and the real risk is a subtle stale-selection regression from the new caching path.
qaChecks: Verify that marquee-selecting several shapes and dragging moves them together, dragging a corner handle resizes the whole selection, and the rotation handle rotates it, with no leftover handles or stale selection outline afterwards.
Verify that Ctrl/Cmd-dragging a selection leaves the originals in place and creates an offset duplicate that becomes the new selection, while a normal drag moves the originals.
Verify that clicking one shape of a group highlights the whole group, double-clicking a group edits only that shape, and Escape returns selection to the whole group.
Verify that selecting a single arrow or line shows its point-editing handles and that selecting an additional element switches back to the normal bounding box with those handles hidden.

Verify right-click on empty canvas shows canvas options, right-click on an element shows element actions such as copy and delete, and right-clicking the edge of a multi-selection's bounding box still shows element actions.
Verify double-clicking a text element opens inline editing with the existing text and font, and Ctrl/Cmd+double-click on an arrow or line enters point-editing mode.
Verify on a touch device that press-and-hold on an element opens the context menu and that a second finger or a drag cancels it.
Verify dragging a shape into a frame attaches it to the frame and dragging it out detaches it cleanly.
Verify selecting a frame and resizing keeps contained shapes at their relative positions, and align or distribute actions are not offered when a frame is part of the selection.
Verify flipping a selection that includes framed elements leaves the frame contents positioned consistently.
Verify that ungrouping leaves both former members selected as individuals and that select-all afterwards behaves consistently with groups.
Verify duplicating a grouped selection creates a second independent group where clicking one member selects only the copy's group.
Verify pasting elements or dropping them from the library selects the new elements with group highlighting intact.
Verify picking a stroke color with a shape selected applies it only to selected shapes, and picking with nothing selected sets the default for newly drawn shapes.
Verify the context-sensitive hint text near the top of the editor changes appropriately between single-element and multi-selection states.
Verify that after copying one selection, selecting different elements, and copying again, pasting the second copy contains only the newly selected elements and none from the earlier selection.

Verify duplicating a selection containing a group, a shape with bound text, and a frame duplicates them together as before (groups preserved, copies offset slightly), then change the selection and duplicate again so the second duplicate covers only the new selection.
Verify that after deselecting everything by clicking empty canvas, group, lock, align, distribute, and zoom-to-fit-selection are unavailable or do nothing rather than acting on the earlier selection.
Verify that after deleting a selected element and undoing the deletion, copy and group still see the restored element and no deleted ones.
Verify adding a selection that includes bound text and frame contents stores all of those elements in the new library item and shows the added-to-library confirmation.
Verify adding a selection containing an image still shows the not-supported message and does not create a library item.
Verify flipping selected elements inside a frame horizontally and vertically keeps them members of the frame and that undo restores the pre-flip state.
Verify flipping a selection that spans frame and non-frame elements never attaches an outside element to the frame or detaches a frame element incorrectly.

Verify select all selects complete groups with no partial groups while skipping locked elements, container-bound text, and frame contents, and that group and ungroup commands work correctly immediately afterwards.

Verify that after unmounting and remounting, selection commands such as copy and duplicate operate only on elements of the new session and no stale elements or selection from the previous mount reappear.
Verify selecting three separated shapes and running zoom to fit selection frames exactly those shapes, and repeating with nothing selected zooms to the entire drawing instead.
Test the fit-within-viewport variant with the same selection and confirm the canvas centers and fits the selection without error.
Check the sequence of selecting one shape, deleting it, then running zoom to fit selection: it should zoom to the remaining drawing, not fail on the cleared selection.

Verify the hint updates per state: with nothing selected it shows the canvas panning hint, selecting one text element shows the text hint, and resizing a single shape with the mouse shows the resize hint.
Confirm rapidly selecting and deselecting shapes several times in a row always shows the hint matching the current selection, which exercises the new cached selection lookup.
Verify the mobile toolbar hint updates when selecting and deselecting shapes, matching the desktop behavior.
Confirm the mobile app toolbar buttons for menu, undo, redo, duplicate, and delete still appear and perform their actions.
Verify the save-to-disk card still shows the project name input and that saving exports the scene file.
Confirm the link export button still triggers the link export when clicked.
Verify that selecting one shape opens the selected-shape actions panel and that its style controls, for example stroke color, still apply.
Confirm the footer controls at the bottom of the editor, such as the zoom buttons, still render and work.

Verify that selecting exactly one line or arrow, opening the canvas context menu, and choosing the multi-point editing entry starts editing that element's points, and that reopening the context menu during editing shows the exit wording and returns to normal selection when chosen.

Test the keyboard path with exactly one arrow selected by pressing Ctrl or Cmd plus Enter to start multi-point editing and pressing the same combination again to exit, confirming each toggle targets the arrow selected at that moment.
Verify that after double-clicking into a group to edit inside it and selecting a single arrow within that group, pressing Ctrl or Cmd plus Enter starts multi-point editing for that arrow.
Check that when a single arrow with an attached text label is selected, the context-menu editing entry appears and starts editing the arrow itself rather than its label.

Verify that pressing the arrow keys with a connected shape inside a frame selected moves the shape, its connected arrow, and any attached text together, and that after releasing the arrow key the arrow remains attached to the shape.

Test that when quickly switching selection between two different lines and pressing Ctrl or Cmd plus Enter right after each selection, each press starts editing the line selected at that moment rather than the previously selected one.

Verify that pasting the copied group with Ctrl or Cmd plus V and separately dragging a library item onto the canvas places the elements at the expected drop point or canvas center, and that selecting one element of the inserted group selects the whole group.
Confirm that the hyperlink popup appears on a linked element when exactly one element is selected and disappears when a second element is added to the selection.
Check that selecting one unlocked shape and right-clicking it offers the single-element lock menu entry, and that after locking it the same menu offers unlock instead.
Verify that selecting two unlocked shapes offers the lock-all menu entry, and that after locking just one of them and selecting both again the menu offers the unlock-all entry.

Ensure that selecting a shape with attached text together with elements inside a frame and pressing Ctrl or Cmd plus Shift plus L locks the attached text and the frame's elements along with the selection so none of them can be dragged, and that pressing the shortcut again unlocks everything.
Confirm that when exactly one locked element sitting inside a frame is selected, the lock entry is absent from the context menu and the Ctrl or Cmd plus Shift plus L shortcut does nothing.
Verify that all six alignment buttons are hidden when exactly one element is selected and that all six appear when a second element is selected.

Confirm that selecting a frame together with a normal shape keeps the alignment buttons hidden and that the Ctrl or Cmd plus Shift plus arrow-key shortcuts move nothing while the frame is part of the selection.
Ensure that with two shapes selected the align-left button lines up their left edges and that pressing Ctrl or Cmd plus Shift plus Up lines up their top edges.

Verify each align command (left edge, right edge, top edge, bottom edge, center horizontally, center vertically) lines up exactly the selected shapes as before the update, leaves unselected elements untouched, and undo restores the previous positions.

Confirm aligning elements inside a frame keeps them as frame contents while they stay within the frame's bounds, and an element aligned to outside the frame bounds is no longer treated as part of that frame.
Check aligning a selection made by clicking a group: every member of the group moves together and no unselected elements move.
Verify copying a selection that includes a frame and a shape with bound text, then pasting it back onto the canvas, reproduces the frame with all of its contents and the bound text.
Confirm cutting removes the selected elements from the canvas and pasting them back restores them unchanged.
Test copying a multi-element selection as PNG and as SVG and pasting into a suitable target: the clipboard must contain exactly the selected elements, including frame contents and bound text.

Verify that with nothing selected, copy as PNG copies the entire drawing and shows a confirmation message referring to the canvas rather than the selection, and copy as SVG likewise copies the whole drawing.
Verify that copying two selected text elements through the copy-text command and pasting into a plain-text editor produces both texts in selection order separated by a blank line.
Confirm the copy-text command is offered when the selection includes text or a shape with bound text, and not offered when the selection contains only shapes, lines, or images without text.
Verify grouping two separately selected shapes combines them so they move, resize, and delete as one unit.
Verify grouping a shape with attached text together with another shape keeps the attached text with its shape inside the new group.
Verify the Group action is not offered when every selected element already belongs to the same single group.
Verify ungrouping a selected group returns its elements to individually selectable items and leaves the selection state consistent afterwards.
Verify three shapes placed with clearly uneven gaps end up evenly spaced after distributing horizontally, and after rearranging them unevenly vertically, evenly spaced after distributing vertically.
Verify the distribute actions are not offered when only one element is selected or when the selection includes a frame.
Verify an element inside a frame that ends up outside the frame's area after distributing is no longer treated as part of that frame.

Verify that after a group or distribute action, and again after undoing one, selecting different elements and running the same action applies it only to the newly selected elements at their current positions, for example spacing a different pair of shapes rather than the earlier one.

Verify the bind-text-to-container command appears only when exactly two elements are selected, one text and one bindable shape or arrow with no text already attached, and that running it attaches and centers the text inside the shape; check it stays hidden for one element, three elements, two text elements, or two shapes with no text.

Verify the free-attached-text command appears when the selection includes a shape or arrow with text attached, and running it detaches the text onto the canvas and restores the container's original size; check it stays hidden when nothing in the selection has attached text.

Verify the wrap-text-in-container command appears when at least one text element is selected and every selected element is text, and running it places each text into a new container; check it stays hidden when the selection mixes text with a non-text element.
Confirm both frame commands appear only when exactly one frame is selected, and stay hidden when a frame is selected together with any other element or when two frames are selected.
Confirm the select-all-elements-in-frame command selects the contents inside the frame so they can be moved or edited together.
Confirm the remove-all-elements-from-frame command empties the frame while keeping every element visible on the canvas, and that undo puts the elements back into the frame.

Test alternating the selection between a single frame, a text-and-container pair, and a shape with attached text several times in one session, confirming the offered commands toggle correctly each time and always act on the current selection rather than a previous one.
uncertainty: The new selection lookup caches results and now ignores deleted-but-selected elements in a few paths (color picking, selected frames on release, drag-duplication); no input a user can reliably produce was identified where the old and new selections differ, so the practical residual risk is a stale cached selection after rapid select, delete, and undo sequences, and separately the exported frame-membership and group-selection helpers gained an extra required argument, which only affects external embedding code rather than UI testing.

The blast radius was truncated at the shared selection-lookup hub (47 direct callers, 101 entities reached), and the cache's correctness depends on invalidation triggers not visible in this evidence; if any editing step changes elements without producing a new selection-ids reference, later commands could act on stale results, so interleave moves, resizes, deletions, and undo and redo between selection-based commands while testing.

No specific input was identified that the old and new selection lookups provably handle differently, because both exclude deleted elements, bound text, and frame children; the unproven risk is a stale cached selection after very rapid select, edit, or undo sequences, which the zoom and hint checks cover.

The new selection lookup passes only which elements are selected, where the old lookups passed the full editor state, and it reuses cached results while the selection is unchanged, so equivalence while editing inside groups and during rapid selection changes is not proven by the evidence.

No input was found that the previous code handled differently: every changed call keeps its selection thresholds and include options, so this group is a refactor of where the selection is read from (now a cached scene lookup). The residual risk is a selection-dependent control showing information computed from a stale selection, so re-check align-button visibility and lock menu labels immediately after changing the selection.

No concrete input was identified where the old and new selection resolution provably produce different results, since both keep the same inclusion rules and exclude deleted elements; the deepest logic change is the frame-membership update that runs after aligning, which now goes through the editor instance and is the most likely place for a subtle regression.

The old code derived each selection from the element list passed into the action while the new code reads the live scene's cached selection; they should agree in normal editing, but no concrete user input that the two treat differently could be identified from the supplied evidence, so checks while editing inside an existing group or immediately after undo are exploratory.

No concrete input was identified where the old way of gathering the selection (from the element list passed to the command) and the new way (from the scene's cached selection) should produce different results, so the residual risk is stale or shifted selection in edge cases; the alternating-selection test above is aimed at exposing it.

testAreas.access: Any diagram creator or editor; no role restrictions are shown.
testAreas.setup: Copy a group of several connected shapes to the clipboard and have a library item containing grouped elements available.
checks: Verify that pasting the copied group with Ctrl or Cmd plus V and separately dragging a library item onto the canvas places the elements at the expected drop point or canvas center, and that selecting one element of the inserted group selects the whole group.

testAreas.area: Hyperlink popup on single selection
testAreas.howToReach: No navigation details were supplied for this area; open the Excalidraw editor and select elements on the canvas.
testAreas.access: Any diagram creator or editor; no role restrictions are shown.
testAreas.setup: Give one element a hyperlink.
checks: Confirm that the hyperlink popup appears on a linked element when exactly one element is selected and disappears when a second element is added to the selection.

testAreas.area: Lock and unlock elements
testAreas.howToReach: Navigation was not found in the supplied context; open the drawing editor, select elements on the canvas, and use the right-click context menu lock entry or press Ctrl or Cmd plus Shift plus L.
testAreas.setup: A drawing with a few standalone shapes, one frame containing elements, and one shape with text attached to it.
checks: Check that selecting one unlocked shape and right-clicking it offers the single-element lock menu entry, and that after locking it the same menu offers unlock instead.
Verify that selecting two unlocked shapes offers the lock-all menu entry, and that after locking just one of them and selecting both again the menu offers the unlock-all entry.

Ensure that selecting a shape with attached text together with elements inside a frame and pressing Ctrl or Cmd plus Shift plus L locks the attached text and the frame's elements along with the selection so none of them can be dragged, and that pressing the shortcut again unlocks everything.
Confirm that when exactly one locked element sitting inside a frame is selected, the lock entry is absent from the context menu and the Ctrl or Cmd plus Shift plus L shortcut does nothing.

testAreas.area: Align elements
testAreas.howToReach: Navigation was not found in the supplied context; open the drawing editor, select elements on the canvas, and use the alignment buttons in the editor's action panel or the Ctrl or Cmd plus Shift plus arrow-key shortcuts.
testAreas.setup: A drawing with several separate shapes and one frame with contents.
checks: Verify that all six alignment buttons are hidden when exactly one element is selected and that all six appear when a second element is selected.

Confirm that selecting a frame together with a normal shape keeps the alignment buttons hidden and that the Ctrl or Cmd plus Shift plus arrow-key shortcuts move nothing while the frame is part of the selection.
Ensure that with two shapes selected the align-left button lines up their left edges and that pressing Ctrl or Cmd plus Shift plus Up lines up their top edges.

testAreas.area: Aligning selected elements
testAreas.howToReach: Navigation steps were not supplied in the application context; open a drawing in the editor, select several elements, and run the align commands available for the selection.
testAreas.setup: A drawing with at least three shapes of different sizes, a frame containing elements, and a shape with text attached to it; access to undo.
checks: Verify each align command (left edge, right edge, top edge, bottom edge, center horizontally, center vertically) lines up exactly the selected shapes as before the update, leaves unselected elements untouched, and undo restores the previous positions.

Confirm aligning elements inside a frame keeps them as frame contents while they stay within the frame's bounds, and an element aligned to outside the frame bounds is no longer treated as part of that frame.
Check aligning a selection made by clicking a group: every member of the group moves together and no unselected elements move.

testAreas.area: Copy and cut selections
testAreas.howToReach: Navigation steps were not supplied in the application context; open a drawing on a mobile device or a session the app treats as mobile and use the copy and cut commands for a selection.
testAreas.setup: A mobile device or mobile-emulated session with a drawing containing a frame with elements inside and a shape with bound text.
checks: Verify copying a selection that includes a frame and a shape with bound text, then pasting it back onto the canvas, reproduces the frame with all of its contents and the bound text.
Confirm cutting removes the selected elements from the canvas and pasting them back restores them unchanged.

testAreas.area: Copy selection as PNG or SVG image
testAreas.howToReach: Navigation steps were not supplied in the application context; open a drawing in the editor and use the copy-as-PNG and copy-as-SVG commands for a selection.
testAreas.setup: A drawing with several elements including a frame with contents and a shape with bound text, plus a document or image editor to paste into.
checks: Test copying a multi-element selection as PNG and as SVG and pasting into a suitable target: the clipboard must contain exactly the selected elements, including frame contents and bound text.

Verify that with nothing selected, copy as PNG copies the entire drawing and shows a confirmation message referring to the canvas rather than the selection, and copy as SVG likewise copies the whole drawing.

testAreas.area: Copy text of a selection
testAreas.howToReach: Navigation steps were not supplied in the application context; open a drawing in the editor and use the copy-text command with text selected.
testAreas.setup: A drawing with at least two text elements and a shape with bound text, plus a plain-text target to paste into.
checks: Verify that copying two selected text elements through the copy-text command and pasting into a plain-text editor produces both texts in selection order separated by a blank line.
Confirm the copy-text command is offered when the selection includes text or a shape with bound text, and not offered when the selection contains only shapes, lines, or images without text.

testAreas.area: Group and ungroup actions on the current selection
testAreas.howToReach: No navigation path for this area was supplied with the release; in the Excalidraw drawing editor the Group and Ungroup actions act on whatever elements are currently selected on the whiteboard.
testAreas.setup: A drawing with at least two separate shapes, one shape that has text attached to it, and one existing group of two or more elements.
checks: Verify grouping two separately selected shapes combines them so they move, resize, and delete as one unit.
Verify grouping a shape with attached text together with another shape keeps the attached text with its shape inside the new group.
Verify the Group action is not offered when every selected element already belongs to the same single group.
Verify ungrouping a selected group returns its elements to individually selectable items and leaves the selection state consistent afterwards.

testAreas.area: Distribute actions for even element spacing
testAreas.howToReach: No navigation path for this area was supplied with the release; in the Excalidraw drawing editor the horizontal and vertical distribute actions act on the elements currently selected on the whiteboard.
testAreas.setup: A drawing with three or more shapes placed with clearly uneven gaps, plus a frame containing at least one element.
checks: Verify three shapes placed with clearly uneven gaps end up evenly spaced after distributing horizontally, and after rearranging them unevenly vertically, evenly spaced after distributing vertically.
Verify the distribute actions are not offered when only one element is selected or when the selection includes a frame.
Verify an element inside a frame that ends up outside the frame's area after distributing is no longer treated as part of that frame.

testAreas.area: Repeated selection-driven actions in one session
testAreas.howToReach: No navigation path was supplied with the release; perform these actions on selections in the Excalidraw drawing editor.
testAreas.setup: Reuse the drawing prepared for the group and distribute checks.
checks: Verify that after a group or distribute action, and again after undoing one, selecting different elements and running the same action applies it only to the newly selected elements at their current positions, for example spacing a different pair of shapes rather than the earlier one.

testAreas.area: Text binding, unbinding, and wrapping commands on the drawing canvas
testAreas.howToReach: Navigation was not found in the supplied context; the area is the main Excalidraw drawing canvas for a diagram creator, where selected elements offer their element commands.
testAreas.setup: A drawing containing a text element, a container shape such as a rectangle, ellipse, or diamond, an arrow, and one container that already has text attached to it.
checks: Verify the bind-text-to-container command appears only when exactly two elements are selected, one text and one bindable shape or arrow with no text already attached, and that running it attaches and centers the text inside the shape; check it stays hidden for one element, three elements, two text elements, or two shapes with no text.

Verify the free-attached-text command appears when the selection includes a shape or arrow with text attached, and running it detaches the text onto the canvas and restores the container's original size; check it stays hidden when nothing in the selection has attached text.

Verify the wrap-text-in-container command appears when at least one text element is selected and every selected element is text, and running it places each text into a new container; check it stays hidden when the selection mixes text with a non-text element.

testAreas.area: Frame content selection and removal commands
testAreas.howToReach: Navigation was not found in the supplied context; in the drawing canvas, create or load a frame and open the commands offered for a selected frame.
testAreas.setup: A frame containing several elements, including a shape with text attached, plus loose items outside the frame.
checks: Confirm both frame commands appear only when exactly one frame is selected, and stay hidden when a frame is selected together with any other element or when two frames are selected.
Confirm the select-all-elements-in-frame command selects the contents inside the frame so they can be moved or edited together.
Confirm the remove-all-elements-from-frame command empties the frame while keeping every element visible on the canvas, and that undo puts the elements back into the frame.

testAreas.area: Selection switching regression for the new cached selection path
testAreas.howToReach: Navigation was not found in the supplied context; repeat selections on the main drawing canvas within one editor session.
testAreas.setup: A drawing containing a frame, a text-plus-container pair, and a shape with text attached.
checks: Test alternating the selection between a single frame, a text-and-container pair, and a shape with attached text several times in one session, confirming the offered commands toggle correctly each time and always act on the current selection rather than a previous one.

report.summary: This release adds a hand tool for panning the drawing canvas and improves how the editor handles switching between tools.
keyChanges: A new hand tool button appears in the drawing toolbar on desktop and mobile; activating it shows a grab-style cursor so dragging pans the canvas without drawing or selecting, and the H key toggles it on and off.
While the hand tool is active with nothing selected, the floating shape/edit actions panel is now hidden; it still appears whenever elements are selected or a drawing tool is active.

The editor's remembered previous tool was renamed and is no longer eraser-specific: after an eraser stroke finishes, the tool that was active before the eraser is restored, now including the hand tool, and loading any saved scene or reloading the page resets that memory so the session starts on the selection tool.
Toolbar shape buttons now show the capitalized letter as the on-button shortcut badge for tools that have no number shortcut, where previously no badge appeared; number badges are unchanged.

A hand (pan) tool button is added to the desktop top toolbar after the lock control, separated by a divider, and to the mobile tool row after the lock button; it shows as active while the hand tool is selected and its tooltip advertises the H shortcut.
On mobile, the library button moved from the end of the tool row to the front, before the pen mode button, so the row now reads library, pen mode, lock, hand.
The help dialog's tools section now lists the Hand tool with the H shortcut.

All single-letter shortcut key badges in the help dialog now render uppercase (previously lowercase, for example h becomes H); digits and multi-character keys such as Enter, Esc, and Ctrl/Cmd combinations are unchanged.

On mobile the hand button is rendered in view-only mode as well, while the library button stays limited to edit mode, and the desktop lock control no longer receives the zen-mode state it used to get.
A new hand tool button with a hand icon and an H keyboard shortcut appears in the shape toolbar and toggles panning mode through the editor's action system.

With the hand tool active, left-button dragging on the canvas now pans the view — previously panning required holding space, using the middle mouse button, or being in view mode — and pressing on the canvas no longer starts creating an element or applies per-shape hover cursors.

Supporting changes add the hand icon used by the new button and apply small type-level cleanups, such as allowing tool buttons to receive a null shortcut label and dropping an unused prop on the lock button, with no observable runtime effect.

A new hand tool for panning the canvas was added and toggles with the H keyboard shortcut; activating it shows a grab cursor over the canvas, clears the current selection, remembers the previously active tool, and pressing H again restores that tool or falls back to the selection tool.

The eraser keeps its E keyboard shortcut but the toolbar button it previously rendered, an eraser icon with a tooltip naming the eraser and the E shortcut, was removed, so button access to the eraser may have moved elsewhere.

The eraser and the hand tool now share a single remembered previous-tool slot, so toggling eraser and then hand, or the reverse, overwrites that memory and the eventual fallback is the selection tool.
Switching to the hand tool or the eraser deselects all selected shapes and groups, and each switch is recorded in the drawing history.
The remaining edits are internal type and bookkeeping changes with no runtime effect beyond the behaviors above.

When drawing data is restored (opening or importing a saved scene, or data loaded programmatically), the saved active tool is checked against an allowlist; the pan tool was previously missing from that allowlist, so a scene saved while panning was treated as not allowed and was not kept in pan mode after restore.

The pan tool is now allowed, so such a scene reopens with the pan tool active; all other tool entries are unchanged and the dependency graph shows no affected dependents, so the only expected behavior change is the active tool after a restore.
qaChecks: Verify clicking the hand tool button activates it: the canvas cursor becomes a grab-style hand and dragging the canvas pans the view without creating, selecting, or moving any elements.
Test pressing H to switch to the hand tool and pressing H again to return to the tool that was active before.
Confirm switching from the hand tool to a drawing tool restores the normal tool cursor and drawing still works.
Check on a mobile viewport that the hand button appears in the mobile toolbar and pans the canvas there too.
Verify with the hand tool active that switching to the eraser, erasing an element, and releasing the pointer automatically returns the hand tool instead of staying on the eraser.
Confirm the same round-trip with the selection tool active before the eraser: after erasing, the selection tool comes back.
Verify the saved drawing loads without errors and the active tool starts as selection, with the tool lock state kept as saved.
Confirm that right after loading, the eraser round-trip still returns to the selection tool.
Verify with the hand tool active and nothing selected that no shape/edit actions panel appears above the toolbar.
Confirm the panel still appears when elements are selected, and that an active drawing tool with nothing selected still shows its own actions.

Verify each shape tool button shows its shortcut badge: a number where one exists (unchanged behavior) and the capitalized letter for tools that only have a letter shortcut, which previously showed no badge.

Verify a hand tool button appears in the top toolbar after the lock control, separated by a divider, and clicking it activates pan mode: dragging the canvas moves the view instead of drawing and the button shows as selected.
Test selecting the hand button and then a shape tool, for example selection, and confirm the hand button deactivates and normal drawing resumes.
Confirm the hand button's tooltip shows the tool name together with the H keyboard shortcut.
Verify the lock button still toggles the locked state as before, including with zen mode enabled.
Verify a hand tool button appears at the end of the mobile tool row after the lock button, and tapping it activates pan mode with the button shown as active.
Confirm the library button now appears first in that row, before the pen mode button, instead of last after the lock button.
Verify the hand button is now also present in view-only mode on mobile, where tapping it pans the canvas without altering the drawing.
Verify the tools section of the shortcuts list now includes a Hand entry whose key badge shows an uppercase H.

Verify single-letter key badges across the list now display uppercase letters, for example selection, rectangle, diamond, ellipse, arrow, line, draw, text, and eraser, while digits such as the image tool's 9 and multi-character keys such as Enter, Esc, and Ctrl/Cmd combinations are unchanged.

Verify that with the hand tool active, pressing the left mouse button on empty canvas and dragging pans the canvas view without creating any shape, line, or selection rectangle and without modifying existing elements.
Check that after pressing H to activate the hand tool, pressing H again or clicking another shape tool restores the previous tool and dragging with that tool still creates elements exactly as before.

Ensure the older panning paths still work without the hand tool: selection tool plus space-bar drag and middle-mouse-button drag both pan the canvas (on Linux a middle-button drag must not trigger a paste), and a two-pointer pinch still zooms rather than pans.

Confirm that with the hand tool active, moving the pointer over existing shapes produces no shape hover cursors or hover interactions, and that panning stops cleanly on pointer release with the view staying where it was left.
Verify the new hand button shows a hand icon, its tooltip ends with '— H', and selecting it deselects the previously selected shape tool so only one shape tool appears selected at a time.
Ensure the H shortcut hint is hidden on the hand button in the mobile layout and shown on desktop.

Test pressing H while a shape tool such as rectangle is active: the canvas should enter pan mode with a grab cursor and dragging should move the view instead of drawing, and pressing H again should restore the rectangle tool.
Verify pressing H twice in a fresh session with no remembered tool returns to the selection tool after the second press.
Verify that selecting a shape and pressing H deselects it while entering pan mode.
Ensure drawn elements are preserved after toggling the hand tool on and off.
Verify the eraser still activates with the E keyboard shortcut and erases elements as before.
Check whether an eraser button is still shown wherever drawing tools are listed, because the button this feature previously rendered was removed.

Test this exact sequence: activate the rectangle tool, press E, press H, press H, then press E; you should end on the selection tool rather than the rectangle tool because eraser and hand share one remembered previous-tool slot.

Check that opening or importing the scene saved with the pan tool active reopens with the pan tool active rather than the selection tool (the previous behavior), and that dragging the canvas pans and selecting another tool afterwards still works.
Verify that loading data with the pan tool saved as active initializes the embedded editor in pan mode without an error, and that the other drawing tools remain selectable.
uncertainty: The previous-tool memory change appears to be a rename with equivalent behavior, and no concrete input was identified where the old and new code produce different results; treat the eraser and hand round-trip checks as regression sweeps, and report any case where the editor stays on the eraser or forgets the previously used tool.

The desktop lock button no longer receives the zen-mode state it previously received; whether that changes its visibility or behavior while zen mode is on is not established by the evidence, so compare the lock button's zen-mode appearance and toggling against the previous release.

The tool's on-screen display name and exact toolbar position are not established by the supplied evidence, and the toggle action plus H-key handling behind the new button come from related changes outside this group, so if pressing H or clicking the button does nothing, report it as a defect rather than expected behavior.

The application context does not document where the eraser can be reached in the interface now that its toolbar button was removed, so if mouse-only access to the eraser is required, confirm with the team where the replacement entry point lives.

No callers of this allowlist appear in the dependency graph, so the restore-time treatment of previously disallowed tools is inferred from the file's restore role; if a scene saved with the pan tool still reopens on the selection tool, report it rather than assuming the allowlist entry alone fixes the flow.

report.summary: This release rebuilds the editor's sidebar, changing how the library panel and its buttons open, close, dock, and remember their state across desktop and mobile.
keyChanges: The docked-sidebar preference is renamed in the editor's saved and exported state with the same true and false behavior per context, and the open sidebar is now recorded as a named sidebar with an optional tab instead of the plain 'library' label, so saves from this version store the new keys while restoring still maps the old docked key.

Restoring a saved scene that recorded the library sidebar as open now reopens it unconditionally, where previously it stayed closed unless the sidebar was docked; very old saved keys for library-open and an older docked flag are no longer migrated at all.

When library data is imported, the library now opens as a named sidebar on its library tab, and the canvas is refocused only after an import that showed a confirmation prompt is confirmed; plain imports such as dropping a library file no longer force focus afterwards.

For integrators, the public API's old menu-toggle call is replaced by a sidebar toggle that takes a sidebar name, an optional tab, and a force option and reports whether the sidebar ended up open; the editor now only grabs keyboard focus on load when the auto-focus option is turned on, while the focus routine itself no longer checks that option, so picking a tool or confirming a library prompt still returns focus to the canvas even when auto-focus is off.

The editor now shares its live instance and configuration with the interface through shared application context instead of passing several one-way inputs down, so inserting from the library, custom sidebars, library return links, and canvas focusing from the interface must still work through the new path.

The library panel is reworked to render inside the default sidebar: it now exposes a shared library-open state and a combined control bar with a browse-libraries link and a dropdown menu, so hosts embedding the editor with their own sidebars are affected too.

Pressing Escape no longer closes the library panel from within it, because the handler that closed the library on Escape when it was undocked or the viewport could not fit the docked sidebar was removed.

Remove-from-library and reset-library moved into the library dropdown menu: remove still filters out exactly the selected items, clears the selection, and shows an error alert if saving fails, while reset no longer returns focus to the editor container afterward.

The empty-library view now shows the new control bar instead of the standalone browse button, with full-width styling, 16px vertical padding, an always-applied no-items label, and a variant without a bottom border.
The shared editor button now accepts a selected flag for an active state and its click handling was reworked, and the welcome-screen center and hint components were also reworked.
The library now opens as a tab inside a newly assembled default sidebar instead of rendering its own sidebar shell, and docking it now stores a default-sidebar docked preference.
The library panel's automatic close on outside click and its document-level keyboard handling were removed, so an undocked panel may stay open in situations where it previously closed.

Library actions were reorganized: the browse-button area now also hosts the actions menu for import, export, removal, and reset, and that menu only appears when the library has items or elements are selected for adding, so it may be unreachable with a completely empty library; removing selected items now clears the selection afterwards.

The internal wrapper that keeps the main menu and default sidebar trigger from rendering twice now counts mounted instances differently and resets its preference when the last instance unmounts, risking duplicate or missing menu buttons if the count goes wrong.

App actions, app properties, UI state, and UI tunnels are now supplied via new context hooks consumed by the library, paste-as-chart dialog, main menu, mobile menu, footer, and welcome screen, so any wiring gap would blank those surfaces.

After pasting, dropping, or inserting elements, the editor now decides whether to keep the library sidebar open using the default docked preference instead of the sidebar's current docked state, so an open but undocked (floating) library sidebar now stays open after a paste or drop when the default preference is docked, where it used to close.

The old toggle for the library and custom sidebars was removed and replaced by a sidebar toggle keyed by sidebar name; the library panel's open/close control now runs through this new mechanism, and the old refusal to open a custom sidebar without a host-provided renderer is gone.

Confirmation dialogs, including the clear-canvas and the remove-items/reset-library confirmations, now move keyboard focus back to the drawing canvas after clicking the confirm or cancel button, which matters for keyboard users.
A new public API on the embedded editor inserts supplied elements at the center of the canvas without any attached files, sharing the same paste/insert flow and sidebar rule.

Internal plumbing was renamed with no intended behavior change: the library open-state flag now lives in one shared location, dropdown menus use a renamed outside-click hook, and the centered footer content renders through a renamed tunnel, so menus and footer content should behave exactly as before.

The side panel was rewritten: it now closes on a pointer press outside it or on Escape while the panel is undocked or the screen is too small to fit a docked panel, it stays open while an editor dialog is open, it ignores outside presses on the panel's own trigger button, and it emits a development-only warning when docking is enabled without a docked state.

The old panel tracked how many host-rendered sidebars were shown and docked to survive host apps mounting several sidebars at once, whereas the new code keeps a single docked flag that assumes only one sidebar is rendered at a time, and the old options for an explicit close callback, an initial docked state, a dockability switch, and a flag marking a sidebar as internal to a host app are no longer accepted, which is a contract change for embedded integrations.

The shared button's click handling changed: a surrounding click handler now runs before the button's own action instead of after, and the button's own action is skipped when that handler has already prevented the click's default behavior, where the old code always ran the action; a new selected option also adds a selected style class, which the panel's dock button now uses to look selected while docked.

The panel's building blocks were reorganized into dedicated components: a checkbox-style trigger that opens and closes the panel and clears a UI animation state on toggle, plus tab components that keep the active tab in app state, render nothing when no panel is open, and expose the same tab-button markup as before.
The live-collaboration button, the panel's dock and close buttons, and the example page's footer button all render through the changed shared button, so each must still fire exactly once per click.

The dedicated library button is replaced by a library trigger for the new default sidebar: on desktop it hides while the sidebar is open and docked and returns when the sidebar is closed or undocked, and the drawing canvas now narrows whenever any sidebar is open and docked rather than only the library sidebar.

On mobile, the toolbar's library button is replaced by the same sidebar trigger, and the scroll-back-to-content button is now hidden while any sidebar is open; before, it stayed visible when a non-library sidebar was open.

The paste-chart dialog now reads its insert action from app context instead of receiving it as a prop, so pasting spreadsheet data and choosing the bar or line preview must still insert the chart and close the dialog.

Re-render skipping for the editor chrome now compares selected element and group id maps by contents, and the shared shallow-compare helper now flags objects whose key sets differ, so selection-driven panels should always refresh; this also applies to the embeddable editor component.

Internal insertion points feeding the main menu, footer, and welcome-screen hints were renamed and new sidebar ones added, so that menu, footer, and welcome-screen content should render exactly as before.

Editing hints, the context-sensitive tips such as eraser and text-tool guidance, are now hidden whenever any sidebar is open on a screen too narrow to fit it, whereas before they were hidden only while the library sidebar was open, so hints that used to show beside an open custom sidebar will now be suppressed on narrow screens.

Saved drawings store their sidebar preferences in a changed format: the old saved library-open and library-menu-docked preferences are no longer carried over, and a saved sidebar-docked preference now loads into the new default-sidebar docked preference, so previously saved sidebar state may not restore exactly as it was saved.

For integrating developers, the embeddable editor no longer accepts a custom sidebar through a render prop and the old imperative sidebar toggle is replaced by a new sidebar toggle; custom sidebars must now be declared as child components together with a dedicated trigger button, and the package now exports a new default sidebar component.

Internal UI insertion points for the main menu, welcome-screen hints, and footer were renamed and expanded with new insertion points for the default sidebar trigger and its tab triggers, so all menu and welcome-screen content must still render in place on desktop and mobile.

The example integration app now demonstrates the new pattern with a floating 'Toggle Custom Sidebar' button that opens a sidebar containing a header and two tabs whose triggers are labeled 'One' and 'Two', replacing the previous custom-sidebar button.

The dedicated Library toolbar button was removed from both the desktop toolbar and the mobile menu, so the Library panel must now be opened through the new shared sidebar trigger and any leftover or duplicate Library entry would be a regression.
Sidebar panels now support multiple tabs, where selecting a tab shows only that tab's content and keeps the panel open, and a panel can be opened directly onto a specific tab.

The close and dock controls in the sidebar header are now driven by the panel's own configuration instead of separate dockability and close settings, so on which screens the dock toggle appears may differ from before, especially on small windows.

A new shared trigger toggles named panels open and closed, reports those changes through a single callback, and built-in panels now defer to host-provided panels in embedded uses so the same panel never renders twice.

The old panel-override helper that previously prevented duplicate rendering was removed along with the old Library button code, so repeated triggering should never produce doubled panels, orphaned buttons, or dead controls.

uncertainty: Saved data from much older versions loses two sidebar migrations that were removed: a file that recorded only the old library-menu docked flag will restore as undocked, and one that recorded only the old library-open flag will no longer auto-open the library; confirm dropping these legacy mappings is intended and such files otherwise load cleanly.

The welcome-screen center and hint components are listed as changed, but their before-and-after behavior was not supplied, so the exact change is unknown and the welcome-screen checks are generic regression checks.

Whether closing an undocked library panel via outside click or Escape is now handled by the surrounding sidebar is not established by the evidence, so the expected new behavior for those inputs is unconfirmed and should be recorded during testing.

The removed sidebar toggle refused to open a custom sidebar when the host integration supplied no sidebar renderer, while its replacement toggles any sidebar by name without that refusal, so a host integration toggling a custom sidebar without content may now open an empty panel; custom sidebars come from host integrations and no in-app surface could be mapped, so spot-check any integration that uses them.

The shared button now skips its own action when the click's default behavior has already been prevented by an outer click handler, whereas the old code always ran the action; none of the buttons the application context reaches pass both their own click handler and the button's built-in action, so this could not be turned into a manual check.

The sidebar area of the editor now always shows the default sidebar; the previous path that rendered a custom sidebar and its related settings was removed, and context shows no page or flow that opened one, so confirm with the team that no supported flow or host integration still expects a custom sidebar.

Scenes saved before this change that recorded a custom sidebar as open, or that stored the removed library preferences, now fall outside the recognized saved-state shape; whether the app silently migrates them or resets them to defaults is not established by the evidence, so the legacy-scene load check is the main way to catch a regression.

The supplied context does not establish which embedded screens exercise the fallback precedence between built-in and host-provided sidebar panels, so that scenario may need manual confirmation in an embedded build.

report.summary: The release rewires how the editor internally records changes for undo, redo and live collaboration, so nothing should look different but those behaviors need careful retesting.
keyChanges: The editor now detects 'nothing changed' before recording, so capture and update passes with no element or app-state difference, including calls that omit either input, leave the previously recorded baseline untouched instead of producing a new baseline or an empty change.
App-state projections are now tagged once and reused when already projected, changing how every edit, undo/redo step, and remote collaboration update is compared against the last recorded state.

A new safeguard asserts that no more than three recording actions are scheduled at once: development and test builds now throw an error past that limit while production only logs to the console, a failure mode that did not exist before.

Importing a drawing via open, drag-and-drop, or share-link restore now flows through the reworked baseline update that is meant to prevent duplicated element ordering when undoing right after an import.
Reconciling remote updates against in-progress local edits now reads the current recorded baseline, affecting how an unfinished local stroke is preserved when another participant's change arrives.
Undo and redo recording was rebuilt: edits are now queued and written to the history after the screen refreshes instead of immediately, which can change how repeated edits group into undo steps.

Finishing a draw, drag, or resize gesture, and discarding an accidental short touch stroke made when a second finger touches the canvas while drawing, now explicitly declare how they are recorded instead of relying on internal flags.
Applying an eyedropper-picked color to selected elements is now recorded as an explicit undoable step through the new mechanism.
Opening or dropping a saved drawing onto a scene that already has content now refreshes the undo baseline through a new path intended to prevent duplicated element ordering when undoing the load.

Scene updates made through the public embedding API and by remote collaborators must now state how they are recorded; updates that do not may stop being captured for undo, because recording no longer runs automatically on every scene update.

Scene updates now pass an explicit store action instead of the old boolean flag: automatic updates (image save-status changes, marking images whose files failed to load, and syncing data between browser tabs) use UPDATE, while loading a scene after the URL hash changes uses CAPTURE, matching the old flag's intent, so visible behavior should be unchanged but undo/redo around these automatic updates is the main risk.

Scene loading no longer attaches an explicit do-not-commit flag, so the initial scene load (app opened with a saved local drawing) and shareable-link loads now rely on the store's default action; the drawing should still load fully and immediate undo should behave as before.

The line and arrow point editor's pointer-down handler now receives the concrete store type instead of an interface, a type-only change with no expected runtime effect, but it sits on the line and arrow selection input path.

In live collaboration, the scene refreshes that apply a collaborator's incoming changes, initialize a newly created shared session, restore the canvas when leaving a session, and mark uploaded images as saved now explicitly flag their canvas update as a sync-driven update rather than a user-made change.

These steps previously relied on the default handling, which treated them like ordinary user edits; the main visible difference to watch is how these sync-driven updates interact with undo/redo, alongside confirming the collaboration sync itself still works exactly as before.
The accompanying import adjustments only enable this flag and have no behavior of their own.

On the public scene-update API for embedders, the single yes-or-no flag that forced an update to be recorded was replaced by a three-way choice of recording the change, refreshing the internal baseline without recording, or doing neither, so a host still passing the old flag can no longer rely on it to record the update.

The labels used for that recording choice changed from all-uppercase words to their lowercase forms and are now exported from the embeddable editor's public entry point, so hosts reading or comparing these labels will see "capture", "update", and "none" instead of the old uppercase words.

Recording is now scheduled and applied in a single pass that gives full recording priority over baseline-only refreshes and clears the schedule afterward, and clearing the store now also discards pending scheduled work so a scene reset cannot leave stale work behind.

The baseline comparison behind opening or dropping a file, restoring a shared file, initial scene load, and scene reset was reorganized to clone only when a change is actually detected, with no behavior change expected for ordinary use.

Two internal routines were renamed, the recorded app-state baseline now carries a hidden marker so the recording step can recognize it, and the remaining edits are type-only or cosmetic with no expected runtime effect.
qaChecks: Verify a sequence of edits (draw a shape, move it, recolor it, delete it) can be undone one step at a time back to the starting state and redone forward, with each step restored exactly once and no dead or merged undo steps.

Confirm an app-state-only change such as the canvas background color, and selection-only changes such as selecting and deselecting shapes, are each undone and redone correctly without altering or duplicating the drawn shapes.
Ensure no unexpected console errors appear during normal editing, since a silently failing capture would thin out the undo history.

Verify opening a saved drawing over an existing one replaces the canvas and that undoing immediately afterwards restores the previous drawing intact with no duplicated shapes or corrupted element ordering.
Confirm dragging a drawing file onto the canvas loads it and the same clean undo behavior applies.
Ensure restoring from a share link opens the drawing and supports the same clean undo.
Verify edits made by one participant (drawing, moving, resizing) appear for the other participant, including during a continuous remote drag, with matching final positions after release.
Check that while one participant is mid-stroke drawing, an edit arriving from the other participant neither deletes nor reverts the in-progress stroke, and both changes persist for everyone.

Test programmatic updates that change only elements, only app state (for example the view background color), and neither, each in capture and update modes; confirm the canvas reflects every intended change, nothing throws, and no empty or duplicate undo entries appear.
Confirm a programmatic update that supplies only collaborator information does not create a stray undo step.

Test fast back-to-back interactions (drawing, erasing, pasting, double-click text editing, multi-touch pan and zoom) without pausing; confirm the development build does not crash, since exceeding three concurrently scheduled actions now throws there.
Ensure the same rapid interactions in the production build cause at most console errors and no user-visible failure.

Verify that drawing a shape, then dragging and resizing it, yields clean undo steps: one undo after drawing removes the shape, one undo after resizing restores the pre-resize size, and redo reapplies each.

Verify that rapid consecutive operations (draw several shapes, erase one, paste elements, change a style property of an element) produce no errors or half-updated scenes and each undo step matches one deliberate edit.

Verify on a touch device that drawing a very short stroke with one finger and then touching the canvas with a second finger still discards that short stroke, and undo afterwards does not restore a broken or duplicated stroke.
Verify that picking a color with the eyedropper onto selected elements applies it to all of them and a single undo restores the previous colors.

Verify that applying an eyedropper color and immediately making another edit (such as dragging a shape) can be undone twice in sequence, reverting the later edit and then the color change in the right order.

Verify that opening a saved drawing onto a scene that already has elements loads it correctly and that undo afterwards returns to the previous scene without duplicate, missing, or wrongly stacked elements.
Verify that undo after the load steps back in a single action to the prior scene and redo restores the loaded drawing.
Verify that while one collaborator repeatedly drags one of their elements, the other client's undo steps revert only that client's own local changes and never the remote changes in progress.
Verify that after the remote drag settles, undo and redo on both clients produce consistent scenes without duplicated or missing elements.
Verify that opening the app with a saved drawing renders it completely and that pressing Undo immediately afterwards does not clear the canvas or step through load-related changes.
Test drawing an image, waiting for it to finish saving, then pressing Undo: undo should revert your last manual edit, not an automatic image-status update.
Confirm that opening a shareable scene link in the same tab loads the full scene including images, and that Undo and Redo still step through edits sensibly afterwards.
Verify that images that load normally render correctly and remain usable after saving.
Ensure that when an image file fails to load, only that image is marked as errored, the rest of the scene stays intact, and pressing Undo afterwards is not consumed by this automatic status change.
Verify that after editing in tab A and switching to tab B, tab B shows the updated scene without a reload, and that Undo in tab B is not filled with sync-related steps.

Verify that an image inserted by one participant appears for the other, that the scene stays editable for both, and that leaving the session still saves the room so reopening the link shows the latest content.
Confirm that selecting a line or arrow and dragging its points, adding a point while holding Alt, and clicking segment midpoints still work exactly as before.
Verify that a shape one participant draws or edits appears on the other participant's canvas within a few seconds without reloading.
Verify that after a collaborator's shape appears on your canvas, pressing undo reverts only your own most recent edit and leaves the collaborator's shape on the canvas.
Verify that several rounds of back-and-forth edits by both participants leave both canvases showing identical content.
Confirm that starting the session keeps the current drawing intact on the canvas and that the share link opens the same scene for the second participant, including the image.
Confirm that starting the session itself does not disturb your undo history: undo right after starting still reverts your last drawing action normally.
Verify that an image inserted during the session finishes uploading and stays fully visible on both participants' canvases, with no blank or missing image after the upload completes.
Verify that after leaving the session and confirming the prompt, the full drawing including images remains on the canvas and can still be edited and saved normally, without reloading.

Test a scene update sent by the host that still sets the previously supported yes-or-no flag to force recording; confirm the updated elements still appear on the canvas and that undo can still revert them, since the flag is no longer read and recording now requires one of the new choices.

Verify that scene updates passing each of the three new choices, "capture" to record, "update" to refresh without recording, and "none" to skip, still render their elements on the canvas and that only "capture" updates can be undone.
Confirm that the recording labels now exposed by the editor are the lowercase words "capture", "update", and "none" and that the old all-uppercase words no longer occur.
Verify that undo (Ctrl/Cmd+Z or the undo toolbar button) reverses a drawn or moved shape and that redo re-applies it, and that the undo button becomes disabled again once the history is empty.
Confirm that after aligning selected elements, for example align left or center, undo restores their previous positions.
Verify that binding text into a container still works and that undo after binding cleanly removes the binding.
Verify that opening or dropping a drawing file renders all of its elements correctly and that undo after loading does not replay changes from before the load.
Verify that resetting the scene clears the canvas and that undo does not resurrect elements cleared by the reset, since clearing now also drops pending scheduled recording work.
uncertainty: No real interaction was identified that schedules more than three recording actions at once, so the new development-build crash guard may either never fire in normal use or surface on an untested fast-paced flow.

The new recording option for scene updates is documented to default to capturing an undoable step, but the new code only records when the option is explicitly provided, so scene updates made through the public embedding API or other paths that do not pass it may silently stop being undoable; verifying this needs an embedding host, which the supplied context does not describe.

The diff does not reveal what the new store action defaults to when a scene update does not specify one, including the initial scene load where the explicit do-not-commit flag was removed; if the new default records updates in undo history, previously invisible automatic updates (image status changes, tab sync) could appear as undo steps, which the undo checks above are designed to catch.

The supplied context does not document how these sync-driven scene updates were recorded before this change, so the exact before/after undo behavior is inferred; if a pre-change build is available, compare undo/redo during a live session to confirm collaborator changes no longer enter your undo history while your own edits still undo correctly.

Whether any host applications or external consumers still rely on the old all-uppercase recording labels or the old yes-or-no recording flag could not be confirmed from the supplied evidence; if they do, their scene updates would silently stop being recorded.
