testAreas.setup: A drawing with a multi-point line or arrow.
checks: Confirm that selecting a line or arrow and dragging its points, adding a point while holding Alt, and clicking segment midpoints still work exactly as before.

testAreas.area: Live collaboration sync and undo
testAreas.howToReach: Start a live collaboration session on a drawing and open the generated shareable room link in a second browser; no specific navigation labels were supplied in the context.
testAreas.access: Any diagram creator or live collaborator; no account requirement is indicated.
testAreas.setup: Two browsers (two participants) in the same live session, each with a few shapes drawn.
checks: Verify that a shape one participant draws or edits appears on the other participant's canvas within a few seconds without reloading.
Verify that after a collaborator's shape appears on your canvas, pressing undo reverts only your own most recent edit and leaves the collaborator's shape on the canvas.
Verify that several rounds of back-and-forth edits by both participants leave both canvases showing identical content.

testAreas.area: Starting and joining a new shared session
testAreas.howToReach: From a drawing in the app, start a live collaboration session to generate a shareable room link, then open that link in a second browser; no specific navigation labels were supplied in the context.
testAreas.access: Any diagram creator or live collaborator; no account requirement is indicated.
testAreas.setup: A canvas with several drawings including one inserted image, plus a second browser for the joining participant.
checks: Confirm that starting the session keeps the current drawing intact on the canvas and that the share link opens the same scene for the second participant, including the image.
Confirm that starting the session itself does not disturb your undo history: undo right after starting still reverts your last drawing action normally.

testAreas.area: Image upload during a live session
testAreas.howToReach: Join a live collaboration session via the shared room link and insert an image while the session is active; no specific navigation labels were supplied in the context.
testAreas.access: Any live collaborator; no account requirement is indicated.
testAreas.setup: An active shared session with two participants and an image file ready to insert.
checks: Verify that an image inserted during the session finishes uploading and stays fully visible on both participants' canvases, with no blank or missing image after the upload completes.

testAreas.area: Leaving a live session
testAreas.howToReach: In an active live collaboration session, end or stop the collaboration and accept the confirmation prompt; no specific navigation labels were supplied in the context.
testAreas.access: Any live collaborator; no account requirement is indicated.
testAreas.setup: An active shared session containing drawings and at least one inserted image.
checks: Verify that after leaving the session and confirming the prompt, the full drawing including images remains on the canvas and can still be edited and saved normally, without reloading.

testAreas.area: Embedded editor public scene updates and recording
testAreas.howToReach: No navigation path was supplied in context; this surface is any host page that embeds the Excalidraw editor component and updates the scene through its public API.
testAreas.setup: A host page embedding the editor with the public API available for sending scene updates, plus undo available in the editor.
checks: Test a scene update sent by the host that still sets the previously supported yes-or-no flag to force recording; confirm the updated elements still appear on the canvas and that undo can still revert them, since the flag is no longer read and recording now requires one of the new choices.

Verify that scene updates passing each of the three new choices, "capture" to record, "update" to refresh without recording, and "none" to skip, still render their elements on the canvas and that only "capture" updates can be undone.
Confirm that the recording labels now exposed by the editor are the lowercase words "capture", "update", and "none" and that the old all-uppercase words no longer occur.

testAreas.area: Drawing history (undo and redo)
testAreas.howToReach: No navigation path was supplied in context; open the Excalidraw editor canvas as a diagram creator or editor.
testAreas.setup: A blank canvas with a few shapes drawn and text available for binding.
checks: Verify that undo (Ctrl/Cmd+Z or the undo toolbar button) reverses a drawn or moved shape and that redo re-applies it, and that the undo button becomes disabled again once the history is empty.
Confirm that after aligning selected elements, for example align left or center, undo restores their previous positions.
Verify that binding text into a container still works and that undo after binding cleanly removes the binding.

testAreas.area: Scene loading, reset, and startup
testAreas.howToReach: No navigation path was supplied in context; open the editor, load or drop a drawing file, and use the reset-scene flow.
testAreas.setup: A saved drawing file and a second session with content already on the canvas.
checks: Verify that opening or dropping a drawing file renders all of its elements correctly and that undo after loading does not replay changes from before the load.
Verify that resetting the scene clears the canvas and that undo does not resurrect elements cleared by the reset, since clearing now also drops pending scheduled recording work.

report.summary: This release mainly adds a searchable command palette that unifies editor commands with consistent names and icons, alongside smaller fixes to dialogs, canvas editing, and keyboard shortcuts.
keyChanges: The editor introduces a searchable command palette: commands are grouped by category and show icons, labels, and shortcut hints; typing filters the list, arrow keys move the highlight with wrap-around and auto-scroll it into view, Enter or a click runs the command and closes the palette, and the last-used command is highlighted first on the next open with an empty search.

Commands that are unavailable in the current state (for example in view mode, or commands that need a selection such as group and ungroup) render disabled: they cannot be clicked or hover-selected and show a not-available tooltip on hover.

The shortcut lookup now accepts an optional index, so the toast shown when pressing Ctrl+P (without Shift or Alt) can list both palette shortcuts — the primary and an alternative — while existing callers such as the main menu, context menu, help dialog, and welcome screen still receive the first shortcut by default.

Shared dialog behavior was updated: dialogs focus the first focusable control other than the close button on open, keep Tab cycling inside the dialog, restore focus to the previously focused element on close, and show a close button on mobile-sized viewports.

Double-clicking a line or arrow that is already in point-editing mode no longer stops the double-click handler early; the remaining double-click logic now runs, so a second double-click on the same shape may behave differently than before.

Pressing Ctrl+P or Cmd+P without Shift or Alt now shows a toast with the command palette shortcut hints and prevents the browser's default action for that key (previously the print dialog would open), including while typing in a text element because this check runs before the handler skips input fields.

The shared dialog and modal components, the right-click context menu, the icon set, and the main-menu items including the command palette entry were modified; several dialogs in the app (for example share, export, and confirm dialogs) use them, so smoke-test their open, close, Escape, focus, and action flows.
The handler that opens hyperlinks attached to shapes was modified; clicking and tapping element links should still open them on desktop and touch.

A new command palette lets users search and run editor commands: it opens with Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+P or Ctrl/Cmd+/ (deliberately not with Alt held), closes on the same shortcut, Esc, or a click outside, lists commands grouped into categories ordered App, Export, Editor, Tools, Elements, Links, and shows the most recently run command first under Recents.

Palette search strips spaces and the characters <, >, -, _, | from the query and removes accents, so queries containing those characters or accented letters must still find the matching command, and a truly non-matching query shows the no-match message.

Palette entries for changing stroke and background color are gated by the same availability rules as the selection panel, so they should be offered only when the current selection or active tool can actually have those colors, and the clear-canvas entry opens a confirmation dialog before clearing.

The selection panel's stroke-color and background-color conditions were extracted into shared helpers now used by both the desktop panel and the mobile menu; the extracted conditions are logically identical to the previous inline ones, so no visible panel change is expected, but the behavior should be regression-checked on both layouts.

A command palette is now available in the main editor through a new entry in the main application menu. It offers live-collaboration and share commands that open the share dialog, a stop-session command that only appears while a collaboration session is running and stops it, links to GitHub, the project's X profile, and Discord in new tabs, a theme toggle, and an export-to-Excalidraw+ action that exports the current scene.

The Excalidraw+ entries in the palette depend on signed-in status: signed-out users get an Excalidraw+ landing entry (opening a /plus page) plus a sign-up entry, while signed-in users get a single sign-in/go-to-Excalidraw+ entry; all open the Excalidraw+ site in a new tab with campaign parameters.

Element locking commands changed availability and presentation: the lock action is now hidden when nothing is selected (previously it appeared and did nothing), unlock-all is now hidden whenever elements are selected (previously it appeared as long as any element on the canvas was locked), and the action now shows a dynamic label (lock or unlock for one selected shape, lock-all or unlock-all for multiple elements or a selected frame) plus an icon reflecting the next action.
The share dialog now closes automatically as soon as any other dialog opens in the editor.
On the crash-recovery screen, the button that creates a GitHub issue now opens GitHub in a new browser tab without disturbing the error page.

The command palette now lists the canvas and toolbar commands under real names, icons, and search keywords, covering canvas background, clear canvas, zoom in, zoom out, reset zoom, the zoom-to-fit commands, the eraser, and 'Toggle hand tool', which is hidden while view mode is on.

A new 'Toggle theme' palette entry switches the canvas between light and dark, and the theme toggle now shows a moon icon with dark-mode wording while light theme is active and a sun icon with light-mode wording while dark theme is active.

Running a tool command from the palette activates that tool, and the image command inserts the image directly onto the canvas when invoked by keyboard but only selects the image tool when invoked by mouse click.

The link command's wording now follows the selection, showing edit wording when the selected element already has a link and create wording when it does not, with separate variants for embeddable elements, and an empty selection now falls back to the create wording instead of failing, while the command also gained a link icon.
The six align and center commands gained display names and icons, with no change to how alignment moves the elements.

Editor commands — undo, redo, group, ungroup, the frame commands (select all elements in frame, remove all elements from frame, update frame rendering, set frame as active tool) and the line-editor toggle — now carry a standard label and, where newly added, an icon, replacing the former context-menu-only label fields; these labels and icons now surface in the command palette and right-click menu.

Undo and redo are now explicitly disabled in view mode (previously they had no view-mode restriction), so in a view-only drawing the undo and redo shortcuts no longer perform anything; the set-frame-as-active-tool command is likewise now blocked in view mode.

The line-editor toggle's display label moved from a context-menu-only field to the standard label and now tolerates an empty selection (the old logic read an id off a possibly missing selected element), and the command is newly categorized under elements in the command palette.
A new text-normalization routine maps accented and special characters (for example é to e, Æ to E, ß to a single s, Œ to E) to plain letters, intended for search matching and highlighting.
Additive plumbing in this group — a forward-slash key constant, a command-palette dialog type, and a toggle-lock API type — has no standalone runtime behavior change.

The object snap mode toggle changed from being allowed in view mode to being blocked in view mode, so pressing its Alt+S shortcut while view mode is on no longer toggles snapping; in normal editing mode it still toggles snapping and turns off the grid.

Dropdown menus fixed an event-listener cleanup bug: the Escape-key handler is now removed with the same capture option it was registered with, so after a menu closes no stale handler remains that could previously swallow Escape presses meant for other UI.

Editor commands migrated from a context-menu-only label to a shared required label plus icons (paint for copy/paste styles, magnet for object snap, coffee for zen mode, eye for view mode, abacus for stats, layer-order arrows for send backward/bring forward/send to back/bring to front); the right-click context menu and the command palette both read these, and the command palette gains searchable entries with new palette names Toggle stats, Toggle view mode, and Toggle zen mode, plus the embeddable-tool command now being targeted as a tool.

The shortcuts reference gained many entries: command palette Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+P and Ctrl/Cmd+/, zoom reset Ctrl/Cmd+0, zoom out Ctrl/Cmd+-, zoom in Ctrl/Cmd++, zoom to fit Shift+1, zoom to selection in viewport Shift+2, zoom to selection Shift+3, eraser E, hand tool H, frame tool F, toggle shortcuts ?, and save Ctrl/Cmd+S (listed for both save-to-disk and save-to-active-file).

The shared action contract now requires a label and supports icons, keywords, and a new command-palette trigger source; a new internal stable-callback helper was added with no direct user-visible effect.

Core editing commands that previously carried only a context-menu label (copy, paste, cut, delete, duplicate, select all, flip horizontally and vertically, add to library, bind text, unbind text, create container from text) now declare a general label, and several also gained icons; the right-click menu must render exactly the same entry names from the new field, and a consumer still reading the old field would show blank items.

Many actions gain a display name for the first time - distribute horizontally and vertically, project name, export scale, with-background, embed-scene, dark mode, save, save-to-disk, load, the canvas and edit menu toggles, the help/shortcuts entry, go-to-collaborator, and the property actions (stroke, background, fill, stroke width, sloppiness, stroke style, opacity, font size, font family, text alignment, vertical alignment, edge roundness, arrowheads) - so their names can now surface wherever registered actions are listed; save/load entries and the decrease and increase font-size buttons also gained icons.
Copy as SVG, Copy as PNG and Copy text gained the search keywords svg, png, text, clipboard and copy, so command search should now find them by those words.

Five labels are fixed English text rather than translation keys ('Go to a collaborator', 'Change text alignment', 'Change vertical alignment', 'Change edge roundness', 'Change arrowheads'), so they stay English in every language.

The action that finalizes drawing operations (finishing a line, arrow or placed image) received an empty label; normal drawing is unaffected, but it could render as a blank row wherever every action is listed.
qaChecks: Verify pressing Ctrl+P (without Shift or Alt) shows a toast listing the palette's two shortcuts — the primary one and an alternative — and that neither entry is blank or a repeat of the other.
Verify typing in the palette search box filters the commands and clearing it restores all commands grouped by category with their icons and labels.

Verify arrow keys move the highlight, wrap around from last to first and back, and keep the highlighted item scrolled into view when the list is longer than the visible area; Enter runs the highlighted command and closes the palette (for example a theme or save command takes effect).
Verify after running a command, reopening the palette with an empty search highlights that last-used command first, and pressing Escape closes the palette and clears any typed search.
Verify commands that are not available in view mode appear disabled: they cannot be clicked or hover-selected, hovering shows a not-available tooltip, and available commands still run normally.
Verify commands that require a selection (for example group and ungroup) are not runnable when nothing is selected and become runnable once elements are selected.

Verify opening a dialog focuses the first focusable control other than the close button, Tab and Shift+Tab keep focus cycling inside the dialog, and closing it returns focus to the control that opened it.
Verify on a mobile-sized viewport dialogs show a close button and tapping it closes the dialog.

Verify shortcut hints in the Help dialog, main-menu items, context menu, and welcome-screen load option still display the primary shortcut for each action, with multi-key shortcuts split into separate keys (for example modifier and key shown as distinct chips) and no blank or merged hints.
Verify double-clicking a line or arrow on the canvas enters point-editing mode as before.

Verify double-clicking that same line or arrow again while it is already in point-editing mode does not trigger unexpected behavior (for example starting text editing, creating an element, or resetting the editor), since the previous early-exit for this case was removed.
Verify double-tapping a selected line or arrow on a touch device still enters point-editing mode.
Verify pressing Ctrl+P (Cmd+P on Mac) with the canvas focused shows a toast with the command palette shortcut hints and the browser print dialog does not open.
Verify pressing Ctrl+P or Cmd+P while typing in a text element also shows the hint toast instead of opening the browser print dialog.
Verify holding Shift or Alt with P (for example Ctrl+Shift+P) does not show the hint toast, and the shortcuts named in the toast still open the command palette.
Verify the help dialog opens via the ? shortcut and closes with Escape, the close button, and clicking outside, with Escape not triggering other Escape shortcuts underneath.
Verify several dialogs that share the same dialog components (for example image export, share, and confirm dialogs) still open and close normally.
Verify the right-click context menu on the canvas still lists the expected items and each item performs its action.
Verify clicking a linked shape's link icon opens the link, with external links in a new tab and local links in the same tab.
Verify tapping a linked shape on a touch device still opens the link and that dragging the canvas over a linked shape does not open it.
Verify the command palette entry in the main menu opens the command palette and shows its shortcut label.
Verify the palette opens with Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+P and with Ctrl/Cmd+/, closes when the same shortcut is pressed again, does not open when Alt is held with either shortcut, and also closes on Esc.

Test search input the old behavior did not have to handle: type queries containing spaces, hyphens, <, >, _, or |, and a query with accented characters, and confirm the matching command is still found in each case, while a truly non-matching query shows the no-match message.
Verify a command executed from the palette (for example copy or zoom) takes effect on the canvas, and that reopening the palette with no search text shows that command first under Recents.

Confirm running the clear-canvas command from the palette opens a confirmation dialog and clears the canvas only after confirming, and check that arrow keys move the highlighted command and Enter runs it.
Verify the stroke color and background color controls appear when a rectangle is selected on both the desktop selection panel and the mobile menu.
Check that the stroke color control is hidden when only an image or only a frame is selected, and that the background color control is hidden for element types that cannot have a background.

Confirm the palette offers the change stroke and change background color commands for a selected colorable element and omits them when an image is selected, matching what the panel shows, and that running one opens the corresponding color popup.
Verify that with nothing selected no lock action is offered in the context menu or command palette; this exact situation previously showed the action even though it did nothing.

Test with at least one locked element on the canvas and an active selection of an unlocked element: the unlock-all command should not be offered; clear the selection, confirm it reappears (named Unlock all elements), and confirm running it unlocks every locked element on the canvas.

Confirm that with exactly one unlocked shape selected the action reads as locking that shape, with one locked shape selected it reads as unlocking it, and with multiple elements or a selected frame it reads as the lock-all or unlock-all variant; the icon should match the action that will run.

Verify the palette lists the app commands: a live-collaboration command that opens the collaboration sharing dialog, a share command that opens the share dialog, a theme toggle, an export-to-Excalidraw+ command that exports the current scene, and links that open GitHub, the project's X profile, and Discord each in a new tab.
Test start-then-stop: begin a live collaboration session, confirm a stop-session command appears, run it, and confirm collaboration stops and the share dialog closes.

Confirm a signed-out user sees both the Excalidraw+ landing entry (opening the /plus page) and a sign-up entry (opening the plus app URL), while a signed-in user instead sees a single sign-in/go-to-Excalidraw+ entry; all should open in a new browser tab.
Verify that with the share dialog open, opening any other dialog in the editor immediately closes the share dialog, and that afterwards the share dialog still opens and closes normally on its own.
Verify the button for creating a GitHub issue on the error screen opens GitHub in a new browser tab while the error screen stays in place.

Test the image command from the palette two ways: highlight it and press Enter, and image placement should begin directly on the canvas; then click the command with the mouse, and only the image tool should become active until you choose where to place it.
Verify switching to a regular shape tool from the palette activates that tool so you can draw with it immediately.
Verify the palette finds 'Toggle theme' when searching dark, light, mode, theme, or toggle, and running it switches the canvas between light and dark and back again.
Confirm the theme entry shows a moon icon and dark-mode wording while light theme is active, and a sun icon and light-mode wording while dark theme is active.

Verify searching the palette surfaces 'Change canvas background color', 'Clear canvas', the zoom in, zoom out, reset zoom, and zoom-to-fit commands, and the eraser, each with an icon, and that running each performs its normal action.
Ensure 'Toggle hand tool' is not offered while view mode is on and is offered again once view mode is off.
Verify with an element that has no link selected, the link command reads with create-link wording and shows a link icon, and after a link is added to that element it reads with edit-link wording.
Check that an embeddable element uses its own embed-specific create and edit wording.
Ensure the context menu still opens normally with nothing selected, with the link wording falling back to the create variant instead of an error.

Verify with two or more elements selected the six align and center commands appear with their new names and icons and still align the selection as before, and that they stay hidden when fewer than two elements are selected.
Verify Ctrl/Cmd+Z undoes the last edit and Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+Z (or Ctrl+Y on Windows) redoes it exactly as before.
Test the same shortcuts in a view-mode drawing: pressing undo or redo should change nothing on the canvas and raise no error, since both are now disabled in view mode.
Confirm the undo and redo entries in the command palette show their labels and icons and still trigger the same history step.
Check that right-clicking a multi-element selection offers the group command, grouping works, and ungroup then splits the elements back into individuals.
Ensure a single selected element still cannot be grouped (grouping requires at least two elements).

Verify that with a frame selected the menu still shows the select-all-elements-in-frame and remove-all-elements-from-frame items with readable labels, and both behave as before (selecting the frame's contents, and moving the contents out of the frame).
Test the frame-as-active-tool command with a frame selected: the frame tool should become active on the normal canvas, and in view mode the command should be unavailable or do nothing.

Test opening the command palette with nothing selected on the canvas: the command list must render without errors, and the line-editor entry (if listed) shows a readable label rather than a blank or a crash.
Verify that with a line selected the entry shows the edit-line wording and toggles into point-editing mode, and while editing it shows the exit wording and returns to normal editing.
Confirm the line-editor command appears under the elements category, and that undo, redo, group, ungroup and the frame commands show proper labels and icons in the list.
Test searching 'cafe' — the 'café' text should be found and highlighted at the accented positions, since accents are now stripped for matching.
Confirm ß is treated as a single letter s: searching 'strase' matches 'Straße', while the conventional expansion 'strass' will not.

Verify that with view mode enabled, pressing Alt+S no longer toggles object snapping (before this change it did), while the grid toggle still works in view mode; then exit view mode and confirm Alt+S toggles object snapping on and off again and that enabling it clears the grid.
Verify that opening a dropdown menu and pressing Escape closes the menu immediately.

Test the cleanup fix: open a dropdown, close it by clicking outside, then open the command palette with Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+P and press Escape; the palette must close and Escape must not be swallowed by the previously closed menu.

Verify that selecting an element, using copy styles from the context menu (now shown with a paint-brush icon) shows a styles-copied confirmation, and then using paste styles on a second element applies the copied styles.

Confirm that the four layer-order commands (send backward, bring forward, send to back, bring to front) still appear in the context menu with their layer-order icons and correctly reorder the selected element, and that the grid mode entry still shows its label and toggles the grid.

Verify that Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+P (or Ctrl/Cmd+/) opens the command palette and that searching finds the stats, view mode, and zen mode toggles under the names Toggle stats, Toggle view mode, and Toggle zen mode with their icons, and that running each one toggles its mode.
Confirm that searching the palette for the embeddable (iframe) tool finds it and running it makes the embed tool the active tool.

Verify the shortcuts dialog (toggle with ?) now lists the new entries: command palette Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+P and Ctrl/Cmd+/, zoom reset Ctrl/Cmd+0, zoom out Ctrl/Cmd+-, zoom in Ctrl/Cmd++, zoom to fit Shift+1, zoom to selection in viewport Shift+2, zoom to selection Shift+3, eraser E, hand tool H, frame tool F, and save Ctrl/Cmd+S.
Test that pressing Ctrl/Cmd+S still saves the drawing, since two save variants (save to disk and save to the active file) share that shortcut.

Verify right-clicking a selected element still lists every editing entry with its correct name - Copy, Paste, Cut, Delete, Duplicate, Select all, Flip horizontal, Flip vertical, Copy as SVG, Copy as PNG, Copy text, Add to library, Unbind text, Bind text, Create container from text - with no blank, missing or duplicated entries.

Verify the renamed entries still perform their actions: Delete removes the selection, Duplicate copies it, Copy followed by Paste recreates it, Flip horizontal mirrors it, and Copy as PNG puts a PNG image on the clipboard.
Verify Add to library still shows the added-to-library confirmation toast, and Unbind text and Bind text still detach and re-attach a text inside its shape.

Verify the image export dialog still shows the scale choices, the with-background and embed-scene options and the dark-mode option with correct names, and that toggling background or dark mode still changes the exported image.
Verify the save-to-disk and load entries still open the file save and file open dialogs and render their new icons wherever icons are displayed.
Verify the overwrite confirmation still offers save-to-disk and export-to-image with correct names and that both complete successfully.
Verify the panel still shows its usual options with correct names - Stroke, Change background, Fill, Stroke width, Sloppiness, Stroke style, Opacity, Font size and Font family.
Verify the decrease and increase font-size buttons show their icons and still shrink and grow the selected text.

Verify text alignment, vertical alignment, edge roundness and arrowheads still apply to the selection; their names are now the fixed English strings Change text alignment, Change vertical alignment, Change edge roundness and Change arrowheads.
Verify the help/shortcuts entry in the main menu, the footer and the welcome screen still opens the shortcuts dialog and shows its new icon and label without layout problems.
Verify the canvas menu and edit menu toggles still open and close their menus.

Verify that with a non-English language the renamed entries (Copy, Paste, Cut, Delete, Duplicate, Select all, Flip horizontal, Flip vertical, Add to library and the property options) still show translated names rather than raw translation keys or blanks.

Verify Go to a collaborator, Change text alignment, Change vertical alignment, Change edge roundness and Change arrowheads display as English text (they are not translated) and remain clickable and functional.
uncertainty: Before/after diffs were supplied only for the shortcut lookup and the palette item rendering; the remaining palette internals and the shared dialog and icon components came with current code only, so the expected prior behavior is unknown — treat the listed checks as verification of intended behavior rather than regression comparisons against a documented old behavior.

The exact before-and-after behavior for the shared dialog, context-menu, icon, and main-menu changes was not provided in the diff evidence, so coverage for those is limited to smoke testing the visible flows; if release notes specify intended changes there, test those specifically.

The extracted color visibility conditions compare as logically identical to the previous inline logic, so no specific input was found where old and new code differ, and no navigation surfaces were supplied for any of these areas, so the highest regression risk sits with the entirely new palette feature.

How the app determines Excalidraw+ signed-in status is not established by the supplied evidence, so exercise the palette's Excalidraw+ entries in both signed-in and signed-out states; the specific other dialogs that trigger the share dialog's auto-close were also not enumerated, so use whichever second dialog is available.

Several new command names and the theme wording are translation lookups rather than literal text, and the change does not prove every language has translations for them, so spot-check a non-English language to make sure no command shows untranslated placeholder text.

The new normalization intentionally substitutes single letters (Æ to E, ß to s, Œ to E), so conventional expansions such as 'ae' or 'ss' will not match; also, no consumer of this routine is proven within this group's dependency graph, so confirm the search feature actually uses it before sign-off.

The shared action definition now requires a general label and removed the old context-menu-only label property; any editor command updated in other parts of this release that missed its new label could render as a blank entry in the right-click menu or command palette, so spot-check a few context-menu entries beyond the ones covered here.

Any surface that lists or searches all registered actions (which would reveal the newly added labels, icons, search keywords and the one empty label) was not identified in the supplied context, so those additions can only be spot-checked where labels already appear.

testAreas.area: Command palette search, navigation, and execution
testAreas.howToReach: Open the drawing editor (no navigation path was supplied in the release context), then open the palette with Ctrl+Shift+P or Ctrl+/ or via the main menu's command palette entry.
testAreas.access: Any user working in the editor.
testAreas.setup: A drawing with a few elements so command availability differs between having elements selected and none selected.
checks: Verify pressing Ctrl+P (without Shift or Alt) shows a toast listing the palette's two shortcuts — the primary one and an alternative — and that neither entry is blank or a repeat of the other.
Verify typing in the palette search box filters the commands and clearing it restores all commands grouped by category with their icons and labels.

Verify arrow keys move the highlight, wrap around from last to first and back, and keep the highlighted item scrolled into view when the list is longer than the visible area; Enter runs the highlighted command and closes the palette (for example a theme or save command takes effect).
Verify after running a command, reopening the palette with an empty search highlights that last-used command first, and pressing Escape closes the palette and clears any typed search.

testAreas.area: Command palette availability states
testAreas.howToReach: Open the editor in view mode (a read-only drawing or link) and open the command palette as above; no navigation path was supplied in the release context.
testAreas.setup: A read-only/view-mode drawing, then an editable drawing for comparison.
checks: Verify commands that are not available in view mode appear disabled: they cannot be clicked or hover-selected, hovering shows a not-available tooltip, and available commands still run normally.
Verify commands that require a selection (for example group and ungroup) are not runnable when nothing is selected and become runnable once elements are selected.

testAreas.area: Dialog focus and close behavior
testAreas.howToReach: In the editor, open any dialog — for example the Help dialog (press ?) or the export and share dialogs from the editor UI; no navigation path was supplied in the release context.
testAreas.setup: A drawing open; for the mobile check, a narrow viewport or mobile device.
checks: Verify opening a dialog focuses the first focusable control other than the close button, Tab and Shift+Tab keep focus cycling inside the dialog, and closing it returns focus to the control that opened it.

report.summary: This release overhauls how the drawing editor records and applies undo and redo, making whether edits are correctly reversed and reapplied the main thing to test.
keyChanges: Editor actions that modify elements (bind/unbind/wrap text, copy and cut, delete, font family and size, text and vertical alignment, paste styles) now signal history capture through a new store flag; the old record/don't-record intent is preserved everywhere except one case: deleting the last remaining point of a line while editing its points was previously not committed to history and is now captured, so the resulting removal of the whole line should be undoable as its own step.

The element-binding internals were rebuilt: cleanup after deletions, arrow endpoint updates while shapes move, resize, rotate or flip, and rebinding during undo/redo now run through new helpers that always read the latest element state; the intended behavior is unchanged, but this is the highest regression risk for arrows staying attached to shapes and text staying inside shapes.

When text bound to a shape is redrawn (editing text, font family or size changes, alignment changes, pasting styles, undo/redo), the text now takes on the container's rotation angle, which the old code left untouched; rotated containers should keep their text rotated after such edits.

Committing the text editor (adding or editing text and then finishing, for example by clicking elsewhere) now records the change through the new store capture instead of the old history resume; text edits should still undo as a single step.

Undo and redo were rebuilt: instead of restoring saved snapshots of the whole scene, they now apply inverse change records to the current drawing, automatically skip recorded steps that produce no visible change, and a new history-changed signal now drives undo/redo availability.

Recorded changes that touch only app state, such as renaming the drawing, no longer wipe the redo stack; only changes to drawing elements clear redo, so an undone element change can now be redone even after such a change, which was not the case before.

Group and ungroup now report a persistent-store capture instead of a history commit, and the reordered element list for grouping is now taken directly from the index-sync step; the no-op cases (fewer than 2 selected elements, or everything already in one group) record nothing.
Scenes loaded when the page URL changes are now captured through the persistent store rather than pushed as an undo-history step, so such loads should no longer appear as an undo step.

During undo and redo, history entries are refreshed with the latest collaborator changes before being pushed back, replacing the old version-keyed snapshot cache that could fail on remotely updated elements.

Undo and redo were rebuilt: the toolbar actions now run the history engine against the current scene elements and the editor's stored scene snapshot, apply entries until one produces a visible change, and re-file inverted entries onto the opposite stack refreshed with the latest element state; the element-delta engine that computes, inverts, and prunes these changes was reworked alongside.

The undo and redo toolbar buttons now disable themselves when their respective stack is empty, driven by a new history-changed event that reports both stack-empty flags to the buttons through a hook; previously the buttons stayed clickable and silently did nothing.

Binding repair during undo/redo was reworked: connected arrows and bound text are unbound and rebound against the snapshot baseline, and refreshed history entries keep their recorded connection changes while taking all other property values from the current element.
The shared toolbar button component now renders a disabled state (including marking the icon as aria-disabled for screen readers), which affects every toolbar button in the editor.

Undo and redo now rebuild both the drawing and the editor state from before/after change deltas: previously selected elements and groups are merged back, and multi-point line/arrow editing is restored only when that element still exists, otherwise the stale reference is cleared.

Selections and group references pointing at elements deleted since a step are filtered out during undo/redo, and group lookups defensively skip deleted elements and elements without group assignments.

After an undo/redo step the app recomputes size and position of text bound inside shapes, adjusts arrows attached to changed shapes, and re-sorts element stacking order; in the packaged build a failure while applying a step logs an error and returns the previous drawing, so a failure appears as a no-op step rather than a crash.

Change recording was rebuilt around scene snapshots that watch the drawing name, canvas background color, selection, groups and line editing; loading a drawing (open, drag-and-drop onto the canvas, or a shared link) re-baselines the snapshot, and live collaboration applies remote changes through the same apply path.

Undo and redo now record changes as increments through a new internal store rather than whole-scene snapshots, so every editing interaction (drawing, dragging, resizing, erasing, pasting elements or plain text, line-point editing, and color picking) must still produce exactly one undo step that redo can reapply.

Selection-only behavior changed: selecting all elements inside a frame and double-clicking into a group are now recorded as undoable steps (select-all-in-frame previously was not), and a click that only changes the selection no longer wipes the redo stack.
Stray clicks that create invisibly small elements are now discarded through a snapshot update so they do not pollute undo history.

Opening or dropping a saved scene file now repairs element stacking order, refreshes the store snapshot, and records a single undo step, while the very first scene load and a scene reset clear the store so that initial or cleared content is not undoable.

For developers embedding the editor, scene updates pushed through the public scene-update API are no longer undoable unless the host opts into a new commit flag replacing the removed undo flag, which is an explicitly flagged breaking change, and remote collaborator changes are captured as snapshots rather than undoable entries.

Live collaboration no longer clears the local undo stack when remote updates arrive, and the initially synced scene is no longer recorded as an undo step; previously any message from another participant erased the whole undo history.

Starting a collaboration room no longer clears history or records the initial scene as an undo step, while leaving a session now records the final scene update as an undo step (previously it explicitly did not), so Undo right after leaving a session behaves differently.

Scene loading (share links and local restores) now flags the loaded data as not committed to the store instead of not committed to history, a rename whose user-visible effect QA should confirm via undo after opening a scene.
Zoom-in and zoom-out buttons now become disabled at the maximum and minimum zoom limits respectively, and zoom-to-fit clamps zoom using the shared min/max zoom constants.

All canvas actions (background color, clear canvas, hand/eraser tools, zoom), element property actions (stroke color, background, fill style, opacity, width, style, roundness, sloppiness, arrowheads), and save/export actions switched from a history-commit flag to a store capture flag with the same true/false mapping, so behavior should be unchanged but undo/redo across all of them is the main regression risk.

Across the canvas actions in this group, the old history flag became a three-way store action: 'none' for actions that must not touch history (add to library, copy text, paste-failure paths, copy styles, follow collaborator, and the zen mode, grid mode, object snap mode, stats and view mode toggles), 'capture' for actions that commit a snapshot (finalize a drawing, toggle the line editor, open the hyperlink editor, select all), and 'update' for undo/redo.

Undo/redo is the most behavior-sensitive change: restoring a state now updates the store snapshot without adding a new history entry, so each undo/redo must step exactly one step, redo must stay available, and the undo/redo buttons must disable when their stacks are empty (button state is driven by a history-changed event).

Mode toggles explicitly report no history effect, so toggling zen mode, grid mode, object snap mode, stats or view mode must not create an undo step; grid mode and object snap mode also switch each other off when enabled.
Snapshot-committing actions keep their previous behavior: finishing a shape, exiting line editing, opening the link editor, and select all capture a snapshot, so those moments remain undoable.

Supporting internals changed alongside (the action result type, app state types, scene and selection internals, and a shared list-to-map helper used when computing element diffs for history); these have no direct UI but feed the history and undo paths above.

All canvas edit actions in this group — align (top, bottom, left, right, horizontal/vertical center), distribute horizontally/vertically, flip horizontally/vertically, lock/unlock selection, unlock all, and the four layer-order changes — now report history capture through a new store action instead of the old commit-to-history flag; behavior should stay the same: each edit creates exactly one undo step.

Duplicating elements now recalculates fractional ordering indices using only the new copies, whereas before the change both the originals and the copies were passed to the ordering fix, and the result of the fix is now used as the final element list; this is the one real logic change and could affect the stacking order of duplicates relative to originals.
Opening or closing the canvas menu, the edit menu, and the shortcuts dialog now explicitly signals no history capture, so these UI toggles must not create undo entries.

Internal store plumbing was added (snapshot getter/setter, an emptiness check on snapshots, flags marking that an increment capture or snapshot update is in progress, and a filter that drops not-yet-committed elements when comparing element states); these have no direct user control but underpin the undo/snapshot behavior above.
qaChecks: Verify deleting a shape that has an attached arrow and bound text removes the shape, and one undo restores the shape with the text back inside it and the arrow reattached; redo should delete them again cleanly.
Verify moving and resizing a shape with arrows attached keeps every arrow endpoint snapped to the shape edges with the same gap behavior as before, including a shape that also contains bound text.
Verify undoing and redoing a move of connected shapes leaves each arrow attached to the correct shapes at both ends.

Verify entering point-editing mode on a line or arrow with exactly two points and deleting one of them (leaving a single point, which removes the whole line) makes the line disappear, and one undo restores the complete line, because this deletion is now recorded in history where it previously was not.

Confirm editing the bound text of a rotated container (typing new text, or changing its font size or alignment) leaves the text rotated together with the container instead of snapping back to horizontal, and undo after the edit restores the previous text and rotation.
Verify adding text on the canvas, finishing the edit by clicking elsewhere, and pressing undo once removes the whole text addition in a single step.
Verify double-clicking a shape to add text inside it, committing the text, and undoing once removes the text and restores the shape's original size.

Verify copy then paste duplicates the selection, cut removes it and one undo restores it, copy as PNG and copy as SVG still place content on the clipboard, and paste styles applies the copied look and undoes in one step.
Verify changing font family, font size, text alignment, and vertical alignment on both standalone text and text bound to a shape resizes the container to fit the text and undoes cleanly.

Check: draw several elements, then press undo repeatedly until the canvas is empty and redo repeatedly until everything returns - each press must visibly change the canvas (no dead steps), restore the exact prior appearance, and the undo/redo controls must show as unavailable when their history is empty.

Test: start drawing a multi-point arrow, press undo while still drawing before committing the last point, then finish or release - the previous build excluded unfinished arrows and uncommitted last points from history, so confirm no stray one-point arrow or dangling last point reappears.
Ensure: draw a shape, undo it, rename the scene, then press redo - the undone shape should reappear because non-element changes no longer clear the redo stack (previously they did).

Verify: select elements at different stack depths and group them - the group should sit at the stack position of the topmost selected element with internal order preserved - then undo and redo to confirm grouping, stacking order, and ungrouping all revert and reapply exactly.

Check: run the group command with only one element selected, and separately with a set that already forms a single group - nothing visible should change and pressing undo afterwards must revert the previous real change, not a no-op step.

Verify: while a collaborator moves or edits elements, perform undo and redo locally - the scene must stay consistent (no duplicated, missing, or ghost elements) and arrows attached to moved shapes must stay bound.
Confirm: undo one of your own local changes after the collaborator has made further edits - the revert should respect the collaborator's latest positions rather than restoring a stale snapshot.
Validate: after the URL change, the new scene loads completely (all elements present, arrow-to-shape bindings still connected) and the loading indicator clears.

Check: press undo right after the load - the load is now captured through the persistent store rather than undo history, so undo must not rewind the canvas into a partially loaded or previous-scene state; compare against the previous build where the load was recorded as an undo step.
Ensure: after opening the other scene, undo is unavailable and pressing it does not resurrect elements from the previous scene.
Verify that on a brand-new empty drawing both the undo and redo buttons are disabled (grayed and not clickable), and that undo becomes enabled after the first edit.

Verify that with three shapes drawn, undo pressed three times empties the canvas and redo pressed three times restores all three shapes, with each button disabling exactly when its own stack empties and re-enabling without a page reload.

Verify that undo/redo cycles keep history depth stable: undo one of the three shapes, confirm redo is enabled and restores it, then undo again — the shape disappears exactly as before, with no extra steps and no unexpectedly wiped redo stack.

Verify that pressing undo once after selection-only changes (select a shape, deselect, select another) reverts the last visible edit in a single press, since undo now skips steps that produce no visible change, and that the keyboard shortcuts Ctrl+Z, Ctrl+Shift+Z, and Ctrl+Y on Windows still work, including when the corresponding button is disabled.
Verify that moving a shape an arrow is connected to, then undoing and redoing the move, keeps the arrow attached to the shape at both ends throughout.
Verify that deleting the shape detaches the arrow, and undoing the deletion re-attaches the arrow to the restored shape.
Verify that resizing a container with bound text, then undoing and redoing the resize, leaves the text bound and correctly positioned and sized inside the container.
Verify that drawing a rectangle, moving it, and changing its color, then undoing twice and redoing twice, restores the exact position and color with no stale or missing values.
Verify that after changing a shape's color and then its font size, a single undo reverts only the font size and keeps the color.
Verify that one participant's undo/redo only reverts their own edits and does not remove or alter elements drawn by the other participant.
Verify that undo/redo after the other participant moved a connected shape leaves the arrow attached to the shape's current position.
Verify that the shape tools, the hand tool, and the export dialog buttons still respond to clicks and none of them appear unexpectedly disabled during normal use.

Verify: Select several elements including a group, delete them, then undo — the elements return and the selection and group state are either restored or cleanly cleared, never stuck referencing missing elements, and redo deletes them again exactly.
Check: Enter point-editing mode on a multi-point arrow or line, then undo — editing mode must exit or restore cleanly without an error, and the arrow returns to its previous shape.

Ensure: Undo all the way back through many small actions (draw, move, deselect) until history is exhausted — no step should visibly do nothing and block further undo, and redo must walk the whole stack forward again.

Confirm: Undo the deletion of a shape that has text inside it and an arrow attached — the text reappears correctly sized and positioned inside the shape and the arrow endpoints stay attached, and redo removes everything again without leftovers.
Validate: With two overlapping shapes, undo and redo a deletion and a layering change between them — the front-to-back order after each step must match what was on screen before the action.

Check: While user A has an element selected, have user B delete that same element remotely — A's stale selection must be cleared or no longer reference a missing element, and A's next undo must still apply (a single empty undo step is a known possible outcome, see uncertainty).

Verify: After receiving remote changes, user A undoes their own last local action — only A's own change should revert and reapply on redo, and other participants' elements should remain intact without stacking corruption.
Test: Change the canvas background color and rename the drawing, then undo each — both return to their previous values and redo reapplies them.

Verify: Drag a saved drawing file onto the canvas of an existing scene, then undo — the pre-load scene is restored, and redo returns the loaded drawing with no duplicated or visibly out-of-order elements.

Verify each of these produces exactly one undo step that fully reverts it, with redo reapplying it: drawing a shape, dragging it, resizing it, erasing with the eraser, pasting elements, and pasting multiline plain text.
Verify that after undoing a change, one click on empty canvas to unselect does not clear the redo history, so redo still reapplies the undone change (previously such a click wiped redo).
Verify a single click with a shape tool without dragging (which creates an invisibly small discarded element) adds no phantom undo step, so the next undo reverts the previous real change.

Verify adding a point by clicking while editing a line records one undo step that removes the point, and double-clicking into a group to edit a single member records one undo step that restores the outer selection.
Verify opening or dropping the saved file shows all elements with their original stacking order, so overlapping shapes keep their layer order.
Verify one undo after opening returns the canvas to its pre-open state and redo reapplies the opened scene.
Verify right after the editor's first scene load, and after a scene reset, the undo stack is empty so initial or cleared content cannot be restored with undo.

Verify a scene update pushed by the host is not undoable in the editor unless the host opts into the new commit flag, since the old undo flag was removed (a flagged breaking change for existing integrations).
Verify in a live collaboration session that another participant's changes are not undoable on your side and your own edits undo without reverting their remote changes.

Verify the command that selects all elements inside a frame now records an undo step, so undo restores the previous selection and redo reapplies the frame selection (this selection was previously not recorded).
Verify removing all elements from a frame is undoable, with undo returning the elements into the frame.
Verify choosing the frame tool and toggling frame rendering add no undo step, so the next undo reverts the previous real change.

Verify picking a color with the eyedropper while shapes are selected applies the color and is one undo step that restores the previous colors, and picking with nothing selected still records the default-color change as an undo step.

Verify that after the other participant adds or moves an element, pressing Undo in your window undoes your own last local change instead of doing nothing, since remote updates no longer erase the undo stack.
Verify that with existing elements on canvas, deleting an element and then creating a collaboration room keeps the deleted element invisible to the joining participant.
Verify that after leaving the session and confirming the prompt to take over the remote scene, Undo does not clear the canvas or restore unexpected remote content beyond reverting the last change.

Verify that zooming in repeatedly until the zoom stops leaves the zoom-in button disabled, and zooming out to the minimum leaves the zoom-out button disabled, while keyboard shortcuts still stop at the same limits.
Verify that zoom-to-fit on a very tiny or very large selection keeps the resulting zoom between 10% and 3000% and centers the content.
Verify that changing stroke color, background color, stroke width, stroke style, fill style, opacity, sloppiness, roundness, and arrowheads each reverts correctly with Undo after the change.

Verify that changing a selected element's stroke or background color and immediately pressing Undo restores the exact previous color, covering the cases where an empty color value previously skipped history.
Verify that changing the canvas background color and pressing Undo restores the previous background.
Verify that clearing the canvas via the menu and pressing Undo restores all cleared elements and the previous background.
Verify that after loading a .excalidraw file over existing content, pressing Undo reverts to the previous scene rather than doing nothing or clearing the canvas.
Verify that saving to disk shows the file-saved confirmation and that toggling export options (scale, background, dark mode) still applies to the exported image.

Verify each undo/redo moves exactly one step: draw a rectangle, draw a second shape, undo twice (both shapes gone, earlier state restored), redo twice (both shapes back), then make a new change and undo again — that second undo must revert only the new change, not an older state.
Check the undo button becomes disabled when history is empty (fresh canvas or after undoing everything) and re-enables after the next change, and the redo button likewise after redoing everything.
Confirm undo/redo does not itself add history entries: undo, then redo, then undo again should return to the same state without skipping or duplicating steps.
Validate undo restores grouped elements as a unit and keeps bound text attached to its shape.
Verify toggling zen mode, grid mode, object snap mode, stats, or view mode does not create an undo step: toggle one, then press Ctrl+Z — the last element change must be reverted, not the toggle.
Confirm grid mode and object snap mode are mutually exclusive: enabling one clears the other (turn on grid mode, then object snap mode — grid must be off, and vice versa).
Check add-to-library on a supported selected element shows the added-to-library toast and creates no undo step, and copy styles shows the copy-styles toast and also creates no undo step.
Test following a collaborator: click a collaborator's avatar to follow them and click again (or your own avatar) to stop — the view follows and unfollows without creating an undo step.

Verify finishing a multi-point line or arrow creates one undoable step: undo right after removes the whole shape, not only its last point, and a finished shape that ends up invisibly small is discarded rather than added.
Confirm entering and exiting line editing mode on a selected line captures a snapshot: undo after exiting restores the prior state without skipping steps.
Check pressing Ctrl+K on a selected element opens the link editor and does not corrupt the next undo step (undo afterwards still reverts the last real element change).
Validate Ctrl+A selects all unlocked elements while excluding text inside shapes, locked elements, and elements inside frames, and undo afterwards restores the previous selection.
Verify normal paste of copied elements still inserts them, and pasting does not add a history entry of its own (undo after a paste reverts the last real change).
Check pasting unparseable content (plain text copied from another app) shows a paste-failed error message and creates no undo step.
Confirm copy-as-text still copies the selected elements' text, and if the system clipboard write fails an error message appears with no undo step created.

Verify that duplicating a mixed selection (a group plus elements inside a frame plus a bound-text shape) places the copies offset below-right of the originals with the copies' stacking order matching the originals, and that the originals' own stacking order is unchanged — this is the input where old and new code differ, because ordering was previously corrected across both originals and copies and now only across the copies.
Confirm that pressing undo once after a duplicate removes exactly the duplicated copies and leaves the originals untouched.
Check that duplicating selected points while editing a multi-point line still adds the midpoint points and one undo reverts it.

Verify that each of align, distribute, flip, each layer-order change, and lock/unlock produces exactly one undo entry that fully reverts that single action, and that none of them silently skips recording history.
Confirm that opening and closing the canvas menu, the edit menu, and the shortcuts dialog adds no undo entry, so the next undo after a real edit still targets that edit.
Verify that locking a selection prevents moving the locked elements, that unlock all releases every locked element and selects them, and that undo after unlock all restores the previous locked state.
uncertainty: The binding rework is intended to be behavior-preserving, but most of its impact paths are inferred rather than proven and no documented rules were supplied to confirm the old binding behavior; treat any unexpected difference in arrow attachment or bound-text position after delete, move, resize, rotate, flip, or undo/redo as a release blocker.

The expected undo behavior for scenes loaded through a URL change is not established by the supplied evidence: previously the load created an undo step and it is now captured via the store instead, so compare undo availability and behavior after such loads against the previous build rather than against a documented rule.

The old redo action explicitly opted out of having its result recorded as a new history entry (the undo action appeared to do the same), and the new code no longer carries that opt-out; if undo/redo results are now recorded, history depth could drift with extra entries or an unexpectedly wiped redo stack. The history-depth stability check in the undo/redo toolbar area covers this risk.

The evidence presents these functions as newly added or relocated code with no prior implementation, so the exact input the old code handled differently cannot be proven; additionally, the code documents that stale references to remotely deleted elements are cleaned only during history and not during remote collaboration updates, so a single empty undo step right after a remote deletion may be expected behavior rather than a defect.

Existing host integrations may still pass the removed undo flag when pushing scene updates, which would make those updates impossible to undo; confirm with integration owners whether shipped embedders must opt into the new commit flag, since this cannot be verified from this repository alone.

The exact semantics of the new store capture flag versus the old history-commit flag were not supplied, and the scene-load flag was renamed entirely, so if any action's undo behaves unexpectedly, retest that same action after a page reload before assuming data loss.

The supplied evidence included the new code but not the previous code for several supporting files (the selection-grouping logic, the history-changed UI hook, and a shared helper that converts element lists into keyed maps used when computing element diffs for history), so exact before/after could not be compared there; if undo/redo misbehaves for grouped elements or bound text, or the undo/redo buttons' disabled state lags, those internals are the likely cause.

No affected areas, pages, routes, or flows were supplied for any change in this group, so navigation had to be described generically from the editor canvas; the new store snapshot internals (the uncommitted-element filter and the capture/snapshot flags) have no mapped callers or user-facing surface in the evidence, and their effect could only surface indirectly through undo behavior or collaboration sync, which could not be verified from the supplied context. The history-flag rename across the align, distribute, flip, lock, layer-order, and menu actions reads as mechanical with no differing input path identified beyond the duplicate ordering change.
