testAreas.howToReach: No navigation steps were supplied; reach this through a host application that embeds the editor and drives it with the public scene-update API.
testAreas.setup: A host page embedding the editor that can push elements to the scene via the public API, and a second client joined to the same live session for the collaboration check.
checks: Verify a scene update pushed by the host is not undoable in the editor unless the host opts into the new commit flag, since the old undo flag was removed (a flagged breaking change for existing integrations).
Verify in a live collaboration session that another participant's changes are not undoable on your side and your own edits undo without reverting their remote changes.

testAreas.area: Frame selection and rendering commands
testAreas.howToReach: No navigation steps were supplied; reach this by drawing a frame with elements inside it and using the frame-related commands.
testAreas.setup: A frame containing several elements and separate elements outside it.
checks: Verify the command that selects all elements inside a frame now records an undo step, so undo restores the previous selection and redo reapplies the frame selection (this selection was previously not recorded).
Verify removing all elements from a frame is undoable, with undo returning the elements into the frame.
Verify choosing the frame tool and toggling frame rendering add no undo step, so the next undo reverts the previous real change.

testAreas.area: Color picking with the eyedropper
testAreas.howToReach: No navigation steps were supplied; reach this by selecting shapes and using the eyedropper color picker.
testAreas.setup: Two shapes with known different colors, plus a note of the current default stroke and background colors.
checks: Verify picking a color with the eyedropper while shapes are selected applies the color and is one undo step that restores the previous colors, and picking with nothing selected still records the default-color change as an undo step.

testAreas.area: Live collaboration undo and session lifecycle
testAreas.howToReach: Open the editor, start live collaboration from the sharing/live collaboration entry, and open the room link in a second browser window as a second participant.
testAreas.setup: Two browser windows with a shared room containing a few elements
checks: Verify that after the other participant adds or moves an element, pressing Undo in your window undoes your own last local change instead of doing nothing, since remote updates no longer erase the undo stack.
Verify that with existing elements on canvas, deleting an element and then creating a collaboration room keeps the deleted element invisible to the joining participant.
Verify that after leaving the session and confirming the prompt to take over the remote scene, Undo does not clear the canvas or restore unexpected remote content beyond reverting the last change.

testAreas.area: Zoom controls and zoom limits
testAreas.howToReach: Open the editor canvas and use the zoom in and zoom out buttons in the toolbar, plus zoom-to-fit on a selection.
testAreas.setup: A drawing with at least one very large and one very small element
checks: Verify that zooming in repeatedly until the zoom stops leaves the zoom-in button disabled, and zooming out to the minimum leaves the zoom-out button disabled, while keyboard shortcuts still stop at the same limits.
Verify that zoom-to-fit on a very tiny or very large selection keeps the resulting zoom between 10% and 3000% and centers the content.

testAreas.area: Element property panel undo
testAreas.howToReach: Open the editor, select an element, and use the property controls in the left panel.
testAreas.setup: A canvas with a shape, an arrow, and a text element
checks: Verify that changing stroke color, background color, stroke width, stroke style, fill style, opacity, sloppiness, roundness, and arrowheads each reverts correctly with Undo after the change.

Verify that changing a selected element's stroke or background color and immediately pressing Undo restores the exact previous color, covering the cases where an empty color value previously skipped history.

testAreas.area: Canvas background and clear canvas
testAreas.howToReach: Open the editor, change the canvas background from the background color picker, and clear the canvas from the main menu, confirming the clear-canvas dialog.
testAreas.setup: A canvas with a few elements and a custom background color
checks: Verify that changing the canvas background color and pressing Undo restores the previous background.
Verify that clearing the canvas via the menu and pressing Undo restores all cleared elements and the previous background.

testAreas.area: Load, save, and export flows
testAreas.howToReach: Open the editor, use the main menu items for loading a drawing, saving to disk, and image export, or the load action on the welcome screen.
testAreas.setup: A saved .excalidraw file and a canvas with prior content
checks: Verify that after loading a .excalidraw file over existing content, pressing Undo reverts to the previous scene rather than doing nothing or clearing the canvas.
Verify that saving to disk shows the file-saved confirmation and that toggling export options (scale, background, dark mode) still applies to the exported image.

testAreas.area: Undo and redo history on the drawing canvas
testAreas.howToReach: No navigation steps were supplied in the application context; open the drawing canvas and use the undo/redo controls or Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Shift+Z.
testAreas.access: All users with edit access to the canvas.
testAreas.setup: A canvas with several distinct elements, ideally including a grouped pair and a shape with text bound to it.
checks: Verify each undo/redo moves exactly one step: draw a rectangle, draw a second shape, undo twice (both shapes gone, earlier state restored), redo twice (both shapes back), then make a new change and undo again — that second undo must revert only the new change, not an older state.
Check the undo button becomes disabled when history is empty (fresh canvas or after undoing everything) and re-enables after the next change, and the redo button likewise after redoing everything.
Confirm undo/redo does not itself add history entries: undo, then redo, then undo again should return to the same state without skipping or duplicating steps.
Validate undo restores grouped elements as a unit and keeps bound text attached to its shape.

testAreas.area: Mode toggles and other non-history actions
testAreas.howToReach: No navigation steps were supplied; on the drawing canvas use the shortcuts these actions define: Alt+Z (zen mode), Ctrl+' (grid mode), Alt+S (object snap mode), Alt+/ (stats), Alt+R (view mode), Ctrl+Alt+C (copy styles) on a selected element, and the collaborator avatars in the user list.
testAreas.access: All users with edit access; the stats and view mode toggles also work in view-only sessions.
testAreas.setup: A canvas with at least one element change to undo, one style worth copying, and — for the follow check — a live collaboration session with another participant.
checks: Verify toggling zen mode, grid mode, object snap mode, stats, or view mode does not create an undo step: toggle one, then press Ctrl+Z — the last element change must be reverted, not the toggle.
Confirm grid mode and object snap mode are mutually exclusive: enabling one clears the other (turn on grid mode, then object snap mode — grid must be off, and vice versa).
Check add-to-library on a supported selected element shows the added-to-library toast and creates no undo step, and copy styles shows the copy-styles toast and also creates no undo step.
Test following a collaborator: click a collaborator's avatar to follow them and click again (or your own avatar) to stop — the view follows and unfollows without creating an undo step.

testAreas.area: Finalizing drawings and other snapshot-committing actions
testAreas.howToReach: No navigation steps were supplied; on the drawing canvas, finish a multi-point shape, select a line and toggle its line editor, press Ctrl+K on a selected element for the link editor, and press Ctrl+A to select all.
testAreas.access: All users with edit access to the canvas.
testAreas.setup: A canvas with at least one line or arrow, one shape, and several elements to select.
checks: Verify finishing a multi-point line or arrow creates one undoable step: undo right after removes the whole shape, not only its last point, and a finished shape that ends up invisibly small is discarded rather than added.
Confirm entering and exiting line editing mode on a selected line captures a snapshot: undo after exiting restores the prior state without skipping steps.
Check pressing Ctrl+K on a selected element opens the link editor and does not corrupt the next undo step (undo afterwards still reverts the last real element change).
Validate Ctrl+A selects all unlocked elements while excluding text inside shapes, locked elements, and elements inside frames, and undo afterwards restores the previous selection.

testAreas.area: Clipboard copy and paste
testAreas.howToReach: No navigation steps were supplied; on the drawing canvas, copy elements (including the copy-as-text action) and paste with the system paste.
testAreas.access: All users with edit access to the canvas.
testAreas.setup: Clipboard content: copied elements, and separately plain text copied from another application that the app cannot turn into elements.
checks: Verify normal paste of copied elements still inserts them, and pasting does not add a history entry of its own (undo after a paste reverts the last real change).
Check pasting unparseable content (plain text copied from another app) shows a paste-failed error message and creates no undo step.
Confirm copy-as-text still copies the selected elements' text, and if the system clipboard write fails an error message appears with no undo step created.

testAreas.area: Duplicate selection and stacking order on the drawing canvas
testAreas.howToReach: Open the Excalidraw editor canvas, draw a few elements, select them, and duplicate via the selection context menu or the duplicate keyboard shortcut; no page or route navigation was found in the supplied context.
testAreas.access: Diagram creator or editor (any user of the editor canvas)
testAreas.setup: A drawing containing a multi-element group, a shape with text bound to it, and at least one element placed inside a frame, with some elements deliberately stacked on top of each other
checks: Verify that duplicating a mixed selection (a group plus elements inside a frame plus a bound-text shape) places the copies offset below-right of the originals with the copies' stacking order matching the originals, and that the originals' own stacking order is unchanged — this is the input where old and new code differ, because ordering was previously corrected across both originals and copies and now only across the copies.
Confirm that pressing undo once after a duplicate removes exactly the duplicated copies and leaves the originals untouched.
Check that duplicating selected points while editing a multi-point line still adds the midpoint points and one undo reverts it.

testAreas.area: Undo history for align, distribute, flip, layer order, and lock actions
testAreas.howToReach: On the editor canvas, select two or more elements and use the align and distribute controls, flip shortcuts, the send backward/bring forward/send to back/bring to front layer actions, and the lock action; no page or route navigation was found in the supplied context.
testAreas.setup: A drawing with several overlapping elements, including one locked element and one element inside a frame
checks: Verify that each of align, distribute, flip, each layer-order change, and lock/unlock produces exactly one undo entry that fully reverts that single action, and that none of them silently skips recording history.
Confirm that opening and closing the canvas menu, the edit menu, and the shortcuts dialog adds no undo entry, so the next undo after a real edit still targets that edit.

testAreas.area: Element locking and unlock-all behavior
testAreas.howToReach: On the editor canvas, select one or more elements and toggle lock from the selection controls, then use unlock all; no page or route navigation was found in the supplied context.
testAreas.setup: A drawing with a mix of locked and unlocked elements, including a locked element inside a frame
checks: Verify that locking a selection prevents moving the locked elements, that unlock all releases every locked element and selects them, and that undo after unlock all restores the previous locked state.

report.summary: The release overhauls arrows by adding a new self-routing bent-arrow type that stays correctly connected to shapes through every kind of editing action.
keyChanges: A new elbow-arrow pipeline decides which side of a shape a connector attaches to (including diamonds and rotated shapes), snaps dragged endpoints toward the nearest side midpoint with a tolerance clamped between 5 and 80 pixels, and routes the connector with an A* grid search that penalizes extra bends and avoids crossing other shapes.

Every action that moves or changes shapes reroutes bound elbow arrows through this pipeline — drawing and dragging connectors, editing arrow points, changing the arrow type in the properties panel, deleting, cutting, duplicating, flipping, resizing, rotating, pasting, Mermaid text-to-diagram conversion, and text edits that grow a shape — so any wrongly attached, dangling, or tangled connector in those flows traces back to this group.

Elbow arrow endpoints dragged near a shape now bind when hovering anywhere inside the shape rather than only near its border, and endpoints near a rectangle's corners snap to a fixed 5-pixel offset from the corner, including on rotated shapes.

Elbow arrows are now drawn through a dedicated rounded-corner path with a bend radius of 16 instead of the generic line rendering, changing their on-canvas appearance and the outline used for clicking and export.

The internal plumbing that keeps arrows attached when shapes move, resize, or flip was reworked, so arrow-follows-shape behavior and binding cleanup after delete, cut, duplicate, flip, and undo/redo need re-verification.

Rotating a selection containing elbow arrows now re-derives their anchor points instead of treating them like ordinary rotated elements, so connected elbow arrows should stay attached and keep their routed shape.

Shared math helpers now drive attachment-side decisions, including triangle-based side detection for diamonds and aiming the arrow at a shape's center when its endpoint is outside the binding distance.

Undo and redo now pass the current drawing into the history engine, and applying a history entry redraws arrows bound to the affected shapes with that drawing, so connectors attached to moved, resized, or deleted shapes should re-route instead of staying stale after undo or redo.

A new arrow type setting with the options sharp, round, and elbow was added to the editor defaults and starts at round; it is saved in browser storage but stripped from exported files and server saves, so it behaves as a per-browser preference.

Elbow arrows gain a new routing engine that searches a grid built from element outlines to bend around obstacles, penalizes extra bends, and forbids segments that double back; routes now recalculate when connected shapes are dragged, resized, rotated, flipped, duplicated, deleted, or when an arrow's type is switched.

A new arrow type, the elbow arrow that routes with bends, is introduced together with three new style icons; the selection properties panel now shows an arrow type control when arrows are selected (it was not rendered there before), and pressing the arrow tool shortcut A while the arrow tool is already active cycles the type sharp, round, elbow and back to sharp.

Elbow arrows bound to shapes are movement-locked: pressing arrow keys gives them a zero step, so a selection mixing a shape and a bound elbow arrow does not move at all; dragging a single bound elbow arrow does nothing, in a multi-selection drag an elbow arrow bound at both ends stays put while the rest moves, a bound elbow arrow cannot be resized, and rotating a selection reroutes it instead of rotating it.

Elbow arrows bind to the whole shape rather than only its outline, and a new routing routine recalculates their bends whenever bound shapes move, resize, or rotate; elbow arrows are excluded from the line point editor (no entry via Enter or the panel action, no box-selecting or grid-snapped dragging of their points).

For every bound arrow, the connection update now passes the size the shape had at resize start instead of its new size and moves arrow endpoints through the shared point-move engine, a broad internal change that can shift how arrow ends track shapes during drag, resize, flip, and rotate.

Arrows no longer count as roundness-capable, so the roundness control disappears when only arrows are selected, and the arrow tool now shows its own hint mentioning the A shortcut instead of the generic line-tool tip.

Elbow (bent) connector arrows are now treated as non-transformable: selecting one shows no resize or rotation handles and no bounding box, an elbow arrow bound on one or both ends shows no selection outline (including collaborator colors in live sessions), and in point-edit mode only the two endpoints render with no highlight when hovering interior points.

Arrow bindings now keep a fixed attachment point: resizing a shape bound by an elbow arrow preserves that attachment (the binding used to be rebuilt without it), moving, rotating or resizing the bound shape recomputes the arrow endpoint from that attachment point even when the shape is rotated, and duplicating or copying now carries the attachment into the duplicate instead of dropping it.

Elbow arrow endpoints now snap to the outline of rectangle-like shapes (rectangles, diamonds, images, frames, standalone text) while steering away from their corners, so arrow ends settle onto edges rather than corners.

The translucent highlight shown on a shape while an arrow can bind to it now uses a constant 10-unit-thick outline that follows the shape's corner rounding, instead of a thickness derived from the binding distance.

Angle-to-degrees conversion now normalises negative angles into the 0-360 range; this feeds resize-handle detection and shape hit testing, where results should stay equivalent but negatively rotated elements are the sensitive input.

In the Stats panel, the Angle field is now hidden and rotation is skipped when a single elbow arrow is selected; angle edits for other elements still work and now refresh arrow connections using the full scene.

Position and size edits in the Stats panel, for one element, several elements, and groups, now pass the full scene and the element's previous size, so arrows bound to moved or resized shapes recompute their attachment points; notably, group resizing now reports the old size to connection updates where it previously reported the new size.

Reopening or importing scenes now repairs arrow connections by type: elbow arrows missing a stored anchor get the default [0, 0], regular arrows get any stored anchor cleared, and the elbow routing flag is explicitly preserved.

Skeleton-to-element conversion, used by pasting and the Mermaid text-to-diagram flow, now builds arrows with the dedicated arrow constructor instead of the generic linear-element one, so pasted and generated arrows carry arrow-specific properties.
The remaining edits are internal refactors with no expected behavior change: reordered type fields and props, an exported distance helper, and a new helper computing an arrow's anchor point.

A new arrow-type control in the element properties switches selected arrows between sharp, round, and elbow (auto-routing) styles: converting to elbow keeps only the arrow's two endpoints, discarding any middle points of a multi-point arrow, can bind the ends to shapes they touch, and closes the point editor, while converting back to sharp or round clears the stored elbow attachment points.

Elbow arrows are gated out of manual editing: the line/arrow editor cannot be opened for them, dragging their segment does not create midpoints, and the body of a bound elbow arrow no longer shows the move cursor so it cannot be dragged as a whole.

Arrow bindings now record a fixed attachment point for elbow arrows (none for other arrows), and every re-binding path, including finishing a drawing, flipping, resizing, rotating, undo/redo, pasting, and Mermaid-to-canvas conversion, was reworked to pass the full scene and element list, so attachment behavior should stay the same for existing arrows.
The stats/properties panel's position, size, and angle edits were re-threaded through the new binding signature; if a path was missed, elements edited there would stop keeping their attached arrows.
The Edges (round/sharp) control no longer applies to arrows, whose rounding now comes from the arrow-type control, and elbow arrows ignore Edges entirely.

Deleting or cutting a selected shape now clears any elbow (bent) arrow attachment to that shape and reroutes the arrow, where previously the arrow kept a stale binding to the deleted shape; cut reuses the same delete routine.

Elbow arrows are now created by a dedicated arrow constructor carrying an elbow flag: clicking to add more than the two endpoints finishes the arrow instead of adding bend points, its points ignore grid snapping even without Ctrl held, dragging reroutes the bends live, and connection hints pause while dragging a lone elbow arrow.
Ctrl/Cmd plus double-click no longer opens point editing for an elbow arrow, and with only an elbow arrow selected the pointer no longer starts resize handles.

Undo and redo replay now run with the live scene so arrows attached to changed shapes are redrawn and rerouted, and the same scene/element-list threading was applied to text edits, point editing, and pointer-release binding lookups.
Plain lines can no longer be created with arrowheads (arrows keep theirs via the new constructor), so pasted spreadsheet charts, which always drew arrowhead-free lines, should render unchanged.
qaChecks: Verify that drawing a new elbow arrow by dragging from one shape's edge to another binds it to both shapes on release, with all segments staying horizontal or vertical.

Check that dragging an existing elbow arrow endpoint onto a nearby rectangle pulls the endpoint toward the middle of the rectangle's nearest side (a band of roughly 5 to 80 pixels) instead of following the cursor exactly, and that the binding holds after release.
Test an elbow arrow drawn between two shapes with a third shape between them: the route must bend around the intervening shape instead of crossing through it, while keeping bends minimal.
Ensure that dragging a midpoint of a selected elbow arrow keeps every segment axis-aligned and leaves both endpoint bindings on their shapes.
Verify that switching a bound elbow arrow to another connector type in the properties panel and back preserves both shape bindings and restores the elbow route.
Check that for an elbow arrow with one free end, switching its type and back keeps the bound end attached and does not snap the free end onto an unintended shape.
Verify that deleting a shape removes or cleanly unbinds the arrows that pointed at it, leaving no dangling connectors, while arrows between the surviving shapes stay attached and re-route.
Ensure that cutting a selection of shapes with bound elbow arrows and pasting it back recreates the same attached connectors.
Confirm that duplicating shapes with bound elbow arrows gives copies whose arrows are attached to the copied shapes rather than the originals.
Ensure that flipping a connected shape horizontally and then vertically keeps its elbow arrows attached on the mirrored sides.
Validate that resizing a connected shape with the resize handles re-routes its bound arrows, and that entering new width and height values in the stats panel produces the same re-route.
Check that rotating a connected shape by dragging the rotate handle or entering an angle in the stats panel re-attaches arrows on the correct sides of the rotated shape.
Verify that editing the text inside a connected shape so it grows re-routes the bound elbow arrow and keeps it attached.
Ensure that pasting copied shapes with bound elbow arrows produces pasted arrows bound to the pasted shapes at the same sides.
Confirm that converting a Mermaid snippet with arrows between nodes (for example, A --> B) creates arrows bound to the generated node shapes rather than loose, unbound connectors.
Test dragging an existing elbow arrow endpoint into the middle of a large rectangle: it should attach to the rectangle while the cursor is inside it, not only when close to its border.
Verify dragging an elbow arrow endpoint next to a rectangle's corner attaches it about 5 pixels away from the corner instead of at the exact corner, and repeat the same drag on a rotated rectangle.
Confirm dragging the arrow by its shaft or an inner joint keeps its bindings while both ends stay near their shapes, and breaks a binding when that end is dragged far away.
Verify moving and resizing a shape that has arrows attached, including resizing via the element properties panel: every attached arrow should follow the shape and stay connected with a sensible gap.

Check that selecting a shape with a connected elbow arrow together with another element and rotating the selection keeps the elbow arrow attached to the same sides and preserves its routed shape rather than spinning or detaching.
Confirm deleting and cutting shapes that have arrows attached, then undoing and redoing, unbinds arrows cleanly and restores correct bindings, and flipping the shapes keeps connections intact.
Test drawing an elbow arrow with multiple bends and one very short middle segment: corners should render as smooth rounded bends with no gaps or glitches on the canvas.
Ensure exporting the drawing as SVG and as PNG produces the same rounded elbow routing as shown on the canvas.
Verify dragging an elbow arrow endpoint around a diamond: it should attach to the side nearest the cursor as it crosses the diamond's diagonal zones.

Check approaching the horizontal or vertical middle of a wide rectangle: the endpoint should snap to the middle of that edge within the snap band, and aim toward the shape's center when farther outside its binding distance.
Verify an elbow arrow between two shapes routes around a third shape sitting directly between them, keeping both endpoints attached and never cutting through the middle shape.
Confirm two shapes aligned exactly on the same row or column are joined by a straight elbow connector with no unnecessary bends, including when one shape sits at or beyond the other's position.
Test dragging, resizing, rotating, and flipping a shape that has elbow arrows attached, and confirm each arrow re-routes smoothly and its endpoints stay attached throughout.

Test switching an existing arrow's type to elbow and back to another type via the arrow properties, and confirm the route is recalculated cleanly each time with no leftover points from the previous shape.
Test undoing a move of a shape that has elbow arrows bound to it, and confirm the shape and every connected arrow return to their exact previous positions and routes.
Test redoing the same change, then confirm the undo and redo buttons are disabled when their history is empty and enabled again after a new edit.
Test undoing and redoing a deletion of a shape that has arrows bound to it, and confirm the shape and its arrows are restored together with no arrow left dangling.
Test opening a drawing saved before this release that lacks the arrow-type setting, and confirm it loads without errors and new arrows are drawn with the default round type.
Test changing the arrow type, reloading the page, and confirm the chosen type is remembered; then clear the canvas or start a new drawing and confirm the type returns to the default round.
Test deleting or cutting a shape that has arrows bound to it, and confirm the bound arrows are removed or cleanly detached rather than left hanging mid-canvas.
Test duplicating a selection that contains shapes joined by elbow arrows, and confirm the duplicated arrows stay attached to the duplicated shapes with sensible routes.

Verify you can draw an elbow arrow from one rectangle to the other by dragging its end onto the middle of the second rectangle: it should attach and route with bends, and after moving and resizing each rectangle it should stay attached at the same sides and reroute cleanly.

Check that with a bound elbow arrow selected the arrow keys do not shift it, and that selecting a rectangle together with its bound elbow arrow makes the arrow keys move nothing while the connection stays intact.
Test dragging a single bound elbow arrow and then grabbing a corner resize handle on it: the arrow should stay in place and its size should not change.

Confirm that rotating a multi-selection containing a bound elbow arrow leaves the elbow arrow unrotated but rerouted with both ends on their shapes, while an ordinary arrow in the same selection still rotates normally.
Verify that selecting an arrow shows a new arrow type control with three distinct style options and icons, and switching between sharp, round, and elbow changes the selected arrow's style.
Test pressing the A shortcut repeatedly while the arrow tool is active: the arrow type should cycle sharp, round, elbow, sharp, and the next arrow you draw uses the currently selected type.

Ensure that with only an arrow selected the roundness control is no longer offered (it was before this change) while a rectangle still offers it, and that older arrows saved with roundness enabled still render the same as before.
Verify that dragging a shape with a bound ordinary arrow keeps the arrow's attached end following the shape with its gap preserved, without detaching or jumping.
Test resizing a connected shape from corner and edge handles and flipping it: bound arrows should stay attached with sensible endpoints.
Confirm that moving a loose arrow with the arrow keys until its end overlaps a shape and releasing the key attaches the arrow to that shape.
Verify that the point editor still works on an ordinary line or arrow: adding, dragging, and box-selecting points behave as before, including grid snapping while dragging with snap enabled.
Check that an elbow arrow offers no point-editor entry in the panel and that pressing Enter with it selected does not open point editing.
Verify that selecting the arrow tool shows an arrow-specific tip that mentions the A shortcut, and that switching to the line tool shows the original line tip again.
Verify selecting an elbow arrow bound on only one end (and on both ends) shows no selection outline or color, including no collaborator color for a remote participant who selects it.
Verify a selected elbow arrow shows no resize or rotation handles and no bounding box, while a normal arrow and a shape still show handles, bounding box and selection outline.
Verify entering point-edit mode on an elbow arrow shows handles only at its two endpoints and hovering the middle of the arrow shows no point highlight.
Ensure resizing a shape bound by an elbow arrow keeps the arrow pinned at the same relative attachment point, with no detach or jump.
Ensure rotating a bound shape makes the elbow arrow endpoint follow the rotated attachment point on the shape.
Confirm a shape connected by a normal (non-elbow) arrow still reattaches and keeps its usual gap when moved or resized, so classic binding is intact.

Verify duplicating (and copy-pasting) a shape bound by an elbow arrow produces a duplicate whose arrow attaches at the same relative point on the duplicated shape rather than falling back to a default position.

Ensure that with the arrow tool hovered near a bindable shape the highlight is a thin constant-thickness outline that follows the shape's rounded corners (rounded rectangles show a rounded highlight), not the previous wider gap-based band.

Validate that a rectangle rotated to a negative angle (dragged slightly counter-clockwise past level) can still be clicked and selected, that its bound text hit area still responds, and that dragging a side resize handle still grabs the correct side as before.
Verify a drawing saved with elbow arrows connected to shapes reopens with every arrow still attached to the same shapes and keeping its bend routing.
Verify an older file containing plain arrows bound to shapes opens with arrowheads on both ends and the connections intact after import.

Test a collaboration room that contains connected elbow arrows: a participant joining the room should see the arrows attached to their shapes and be able to continue editing without the connections detaching.
Verify entering a new X and then a new Y, first for a single shape and then with several elements selected, moves them while the bound elbow arrow's endpoints stay attached.
Verify typing a new width and a new height for a shape with a bound elbow arrow keeps the arrow endpoints on the shape outline at the matching positions.

Verify selecting several grouped shapes and entering one width value resizes them together while the bound arrow stays attached, since group resizing previously reported the new size to connection updates instead of the old size.
Confirm the Angle field appears for a normal arrow and is absent when a single elbow arrow is selected, and that rotating a shape through the Angle field keeps its bound arrow attached.
Verify pasting copied scene content that includes arrows renders the arrows with their arrowheads and keeps them bound to the pasted shapes.
Verify generating a diagram from Mermaid text inserts arrows that connect the generated nodes as before, with no stray or headless connectors.

Verify a multi-point arrow with at least two middle bends, when switched to the elbow style, collapses to just its two endpoints and reroutes with bends, and that switching it back to sharp leaves a straight two-point arrow while undo restores the original arrow with all its points.

Verify converting an arrow whose ends rest on shapes to elbow binds those ends to the shapes so the arrow follows when a shape is later moved, and that converting an arrow while it is open in the line editor closes the editor.
Verify the sharp, round, and elbow options reflect the selected arrow's current style and that choosing round versus sharp visibly rounds or sharpens a simple two-point arrow.
Test a selection of shapes with bound arrows: flip it horizontally and vertically, then resize and rotate it, and confirm every arrow stays attached to the same shapes and keeps following them.
Verify undo and then redo of a move that repositions a bound shape leaves each arrow attached at the same point on the shape.

Test drawing a new arrow by dragging from one shape toward another and confirm the hovered shape still highlights as a binding suggestion and the arrow snaps to it on release, and that pasting a copied shape-arrow pair preserves the connection.

Confirm the line/arrow editor cannot be opened for an elbow arrow, and pressing and dragging on the middle of one of its segments does not add a midpoint, while the same drag on a normal arrow still splits the segment.

Verify hovering the body of a selected elbow arrow that is bound to shapes does not show the move cursor and dragging the body does not move the arrow, while an unbound elbow arrow still shows the move cursor and drags normally.

Ensure ordinary point editing on a normal non-elbow line or arrow still works: alt-click adds a point, duplicating a selected point inserts a copy, and deleting points keeps the remaining line intact and connected.
Verify changing a shape's position, width, height, and angle in the stats panel keeps its bound arrows attached and moving with it, including an elbow arrow.
Confirm with an arrow selected the Edges round/sharp control no longer changes the arrow and its rounding must be set through the arrow-type control instead.
Verify in a multi-selection of a rectangle with an elbow arrow that changing Edges updates only the rectangle and leaves the elbow arrow unchanged.

Verify deleting one of two shapes connected by an elbow arrow leaves the arrow in the drawing, clears only its attachment to the deleted shape, keeps the attachment to the remaining shape, and reroutes the arrow so it does not jump or disappear.
Verify cutting a shape that has an elbow arrow attached behaves the same as deleting: the arrow survives, unbinds from the cut shape, and reroutes.
Verify that after drawing the first segment of an elbow arrow, clicking a third location finishes the arrow at the second point instead of adding another bend.
Verify elbow arrow points do not snap to the canvas grid while drawing or dragging (they previously snapped unless Ctrl was held), while plain lines and shapes drawn the same way still snap.
Verify dragging a completed elbow arrow reroutes its bends, and that with only that elbow arrow selected, dragging a corner does not start a resize.
Verify moving a shape with an attached elbow arrow reroutes the arrow, undo returns shape and arrow to the previous routing, and redo restores the moved state with the arrow rerouted again.
Verify undoing a deletion of a shape that had an attached elbow arrow restores the shape and leaves the arrow attached and routed to it.
Verify editing the text inside a shape keeps an attached elbow arrow rerouted as the shape's size changes.
Verify the same move/undo/redo sequence with a plain (non-elbow) arrow keeps it attached as before.
Verify pasting spreadsheet content and inserting it as a bar chart and as a line chart renders plain lines without arrowheads, matching the previous chart appearance.
Verify arrows produced from pasted or Mermaid text-to-diagram content keep their arrowheads and connector styles as before.
Verify Ctrl/Cmd plus double-click opens point editing for a normal line or straight arrow but does not open it for an elbow arrow.
Verify duplicating a selected point while editing a line adds the extra point as before, and closing the point editor exits cleanly.
Verify dragging a line endpoint in point-editing mode onto another shape and releasing attaches the endpoint to that shape as before.
uncertainty: Every diff in this group only adds lines (the heading utilities are a new file and the binding, routing, and math helpers appear as additions beside existing code), so no input that the previous code handled differently can be named from the evidence; treat any unexpected change in how elbow arrows snap, attach, or route as a release finding rather than expected behaviour.

The evidence does not establish which shape binds when an elbow arrow endpoint is dragged over several overlapping shapes under the new whole-shape rule, so verify that binding is predictable in that case.

The elbow-arrow routing engine and the arrow-type setting are entirely new with no documented previous behavior, so there is no baseline to compare route quality against, and no navigation details were supplied; the highest-risk unknown is whether undo and redo now restore bound-arrow routes identically to the pre-change behavior.

When a selection mixes shapes with a bound elbow arrow, pressing arrow keys moves nothing at all because the bound elbow arrow forces a zero movement step; the evidence does not state whether this full stop is intended or whether the unbound shapes should still move, so confirm the expected behavior before sign-off.

The new guard on elbow arrows removes all transform handles (resize as well as rotation), while its comment mentions only rotation, so resizing elbow arrows via handles is fully disabled; confirm with the team whether that scope is intended.

Whether drawings saved before this change reopen with elbow arrows attached at exactly the same points: connections that lacked a stored anchor now default to [0, 0] and regular-arrow anchors are cleared, and no supplied documentation confirms the anchor values in older files, so compare a pre-change file side by side before and after this release.

The Edges round/sharp control no longer treats arrows as eligible even though the underlying action can still change non-elbow arrows through other entry points such as keyboard shortcuts, so arrow rounding may be reachable one way but not the other; verify both paths behave consistently.

The line constructor no longer accepts arrowhead options, so any import, restore, or paste path that previously produced lines carrying arrowheads would now silently render them without arrowheads; the supplied evidence does not establish whether such paths exist, so spot-check opening older saved files whose line elements define arrowheads.

report.summary: The release introduces a freehand lasso selection tool that touches nearly every part of the drawing editor, changing how selections are made, remembered, saved, and restored, along with minor visual cleanups.
keyChanges: Element outlines used for selection and frame fitting are now built from the actual drawn shape: curved lines and arrows are sampled along the curve, ellipses use a 90-segment outline instead of the previous 8 straight lines, and rounded rectangles, frames, images, and diamonds now include their rounded corners, so selection and frame boundaries follow curved edges.

The new lasso selection rule selects an element when the lasso crosses its outline (with a 1px tolerance) or when any part of its outline lies inside the lasso path, so touching a shape now selects it rather than requiring full enclosure.

Applying a lasso selection now replaces selected bound text with its container shape, removes frame children from the selection when a frame is selected, keeps previously selected elements when extending the selection, and switches to point-editing when exactly one line or arrow is selected.
A new accessor for the animated lasso trail supports the lasso flow; it has no standalone behavior beyond enabling the live trail during selection.

The lasso tool now draws a purple trail that follows the pointer, with a dashed stroke animating in a 0.3-second loop; the rendered trail is trimmed at its start and is wiped as soon as the gesture ends.

Trail history is now cleared on every new point and on every path start or end, so laser-pointer trails, including collaborators' trails in live sessions, disappear the moment a stroke is released instead of lingering and fading out gradually.

Dragging a selection rectangle while holding the resize-from-center modifier no longer grows the rectangle from its center; it now always grows from the initial press point (the change is scoped to the selection rectangle drawn with the selection tool).

Switching to the lasso tool clears the current selection like other tools, but can now be invoked in a way that preserves it, and the editor's default state gains a new tool flag (false by default) that flows through app start, scene restore, and image/SVG export paths.

The lasso is now a fully working selection tool on the drawing canvas: pressing the canvas starts a visible lasso trail that selects elements live as you drag, with touched or fully enclosed shapes selected.

The lasso selection now survives releasing the pointer and the lasso tool stays active afterwards instead of auto-resetting like one-shot shape tools, and starting a lasso clears the previous selection unless Shift is held so Shift plus lasso extends an existing selection.

With the lasso tool active, dragging over already-selected elements no longer moves them but draws a lasso path instead, while dragging a rectangle marquee with the selection tool can be converted to a lasso by holding Alt and back to a rectangle by releasing Alt mid-drag.

The editor now remembers whether the lasso was entered from the rectangle selection so it resets to that tool when the drag ends, and this memory is reset on every tool switch and whenever drawings are loaded from files or links.

The tool types recognized when drawings and settings are restored now include lasso, so a drawing saved with the lasso tool active keeps that tool on reopen or import instead of the setting being dropped; the active tool can also now carry a flag marking that it was switched on temporarily from the selection tool.

The shared geometry helper that finds where one line segment crosses another, which underpins arrow binding to shapes, shape hit-testing, and lasso selection, now accepts an optional tolerance passed to its on-segment checks; every current caller still omits it, so the default precision applies and results should be identical to before.

The selection of state properties used by the canvas that renders existing drawing elements was restructured but returns exactly the same properties, so no visible rendering or redraw change is expected.

A new lasso tool is added to the editor: it appears as a "Lasso" entry in the extra-tools dropdown on the desktop top toolbar and the mobile toolbar, the extra-tools button shows the new lasso icon and highlights while lasso is active, and the editor initializes a lasso trail so dragging draws a visible trail.
Pressing the selection tool button while it is already active now toggles to the lasso tool and back; before this change, pressing it did nothing.

While the lasso tool is active and nothing is selected, the shape editing panel and the Edit button that opens it are now hidden, matching selection-tool behavior; they reappear once elements are selected.
The command palette gains a lasso tool command in its tools list, and the lasso menu label uses a new translation key, so a missing translation would render a blank label.

The canvas hint bar now renders hints as a joined list, with the canvas-panning and deep-box-select tips going through the new formatting (trailing punctuation may differ), and the embed tool icon is drawn with a slightly heavier stroke.

A new lasso tool is registered for the editor toolbar with a lasso icon and toolbar tracking, and 'lasso' was added to the shared tool-type constants and the action-name list; activating it switches the active tool to lasso with a crosshair cursor and clears the current selection, activating it again returns to the selection tool, and neither toggle is recorded as an undo step.
New lasso selection logic selects an element when the drawn path fully encloses it or merely crosses it, shown as an animated trail on the canvas.

Seven existing actions ('Change canvas background color', 'Clear canvas', 'Toggle hand tool', 'Unlock all elements', 'Toggle stats', 'Toggle view mode', 'Toggle zen mode') no longer declare custom palette names, so only their standard labels remain.

uncertainty: The supplied context documents no intended lasso rule, and the new code selects elements the lasso merely touches (outline crossed or any outline point inside the path) rather than only fully enclosed shapes; confirm touch-to-select is the intended behavior before release.

Trail history is now cleared unconditionally for every animated trail, so the laser pointer's previous gradual fade-out is gone and trails vanish instantly on release; the checks assume this instant clear is intended, and if the fade-out was deliberate design it needs a product decision before release.

Touch and pen input handling now treats the lasso like the selection tool, but the pre-change touch behavior for lasso is not documented in the supplied evidence, so verify on a touch device that starting a lasso does not conflict with panning or other touch gestures.

The geometry helper's new optional tolerance is not passed by any current caller, so no input is handled differently and no regression is expected from it in this group; if another part of this release starts passing a tolerance, borderline cases such as a lasso trail or arrow line just missing a shape edge could change which elements are selected or bound, and should be retested once those callers are known.

The new press-to-toggle on the selection button runs alongside the button's normal click handling, which re-selects the selection tool; if repeated presses never land on lasso or snap straight back to selection, that override is the likely regression to report, since the expected behavior is a clean alternation between the two tools.

No supplied screen or menu shows where the removed custom palette names appeared, so the visible effect of their removal is unverified; if any command-list style palette presents actions by name, confirm those seven entries still appear under their standard labels and still run.

report.summary: The release makes the drawing editor's default selection tool configurable and device-dependent, so touch devices now start with the lasso tool while desktops keep the classic selection tool.
keyChanges: On phones and tablets (touch input with a coarse pointer), the lasso tool is now the default active tool, and after pasting, inserting or dropping library items, placing text, or finishing a drawn shape the active tool resets to lasso instead of rectangular selection; desktop keeps rectangular selection as before.

With the lasso tool active, pressing on an already-selected element, its shared selection bounding box, or a resize handle now moves or resizes the selection instead of starting a lasso trail; on touch devices, tapping a not-yet-selected element selects it immediately with the normal selection rules for frames and groups, and shows the info popup for elements with links or embeddable content.

On desktop, lassoing from empty canvas now blocks dragging the selection until the next press, and dragging selected elements with the lasso tool clears the leftover lasso trail; this prevents elements being displaced while a lasso is in progress.

On desktop, holding Ctrl or Cmd plus Alt while pressing the canvas with elements selected now switches to the lasso tool and starts the lasso trail immediately, first closing any open element-link selection dialog.

The touch long-press context menu and double-tap gestures now fire when the active tool is the default selection tool (lasso on touch devices) rather than only rectangular selection, so on touch devices these gestures no longer work when rectangular selection is chosen manually.

The shape toolbar is now built from a tool list that depends on the app's default selection tool: when lasso is the default, the toolbar's first button becomes the lasso tool (using the selection-style icon, activated by V or 1) and the separate lasso entry is removed from the extra tools dropdown; when selection is the default, the dropdown keeps the lasso entry with a selected highlight when lasso is active, and clicking the selection button while selection is already active now switches to lasso instead of staying on selection.

Returning to the default tool after locking and unlocking a drawing tool, turning the laser tool off with K, and finishing a paste now uses the app's default selection tool, so with lasso configured users land back in lasso instead of selection.
Pasting on a mobile or tablet device now places pasted elements centered in the viewport instead of at the last pointer position; desktop pasting still places content at the pointer.
On an empty canvas, the welcome screen now stays visible while the lasso tool is active when lasso is the default selection tool (it previously required the selection tool).

With the lasso tool active and nothing selected, hovering elements no longer shows the move cursor; the move cursor returns once elements are selected, including when hovering a selected line or arrow.

When a scene loads or is restored, the active tool is now normalized to the device default: lasso on mobile/tablet, selection on desktop, instead of always selection; this applies only when the stored tool is the image, lasso, or selection tool, while scenes saved with other shape tools keep their stored tool.

As a result, a fresh editor session or a saved drawing with the selection tool now opens with lasso active on mobile/tablet (previously selection), and a drawing saved with the lasso tool now opens with selection on desktop (previously it reopened in lasso).

Canceling or failing an image insertion, such as closing the image file picker without choosing a file, now returns the active tool to the device default (lasso on mobile/tablet, selection on desktop) instead of always switching to selection; successful image insertion is unchanged.
Existing automated lasso and tool-selection tests cover this workflow, which is coverage evidence rather than user-facing impact.

After deleting or cutting a selection, toggling the eraser off, clearing the canvas while the image tool is active, or finishing a drawing gesture, the editor now reverts to the configured default selection tool instead of always the classic selection tool; with the shipped default configuration nothing visibly changes, but an integration configured with lasso as the default now returns to lasso in all these situations.
When lasso is the configured default selection tool, the separate lasso toggle action is no longer offered, since lasso is already the default.

Snap and gap guides, previously always disabled while the lasso tool was active, now appear when lasso-selected elements are being dragged (with object snap mode on, or with Ctrl or Cmd held when it is off), but stay off while drawing the lasso selection itself.

A new mobile-device detection flag was added and iOS detection became case-insensitive, so devices newly classified as mobile (for example Android) may now receive the mobile set of resize and rotation handles for selected elements.

report.summary: This release rebuilds the AI text-to-diagram dialog into a full chat-style experience with saved conversations and clearer streaming and error handling, so chat and preview behavior needs end-to-end regression testing.
keyChanges: The shared action button now honors a caller-supplied disabled state in addition to its automatic loading/success disabling; the existing share, image-export, shareable-link, and overwrite-confirm dialogs do not pass it, so their buttons should behave exactly as before.

The text-to-diagram chat input was rebuilt: Enter sends the trimmed prompt and clears the field, Shift+Enter inserts a line break, prompts of 3 or fewer characters after trimming cannot be sent, and the input locks while a diagram is generating or the message limit is exhausted.

While generation runs, the send button turns into a stop control that aborts and the chat history menu is disabled; a remaining-message counter appears in the panel header with warning styling when fewer than 5 remain, and a view-as-Mermaid link appears once a response exists.

Chat messages gained per-message actions: insert to canvas, view as Mermaid, delete (hidden for network errors), and retry for network errors on the last message, which stays unavailable for about 5 seconds after the most recent attempt; parse errors add fix-in-Mermaid and AI-repair links, with AI repair disabled at zero remaining messages.

A new preview panel renders the generated diagram with an insert action plus loading and error states, and limit-exceeded warnings now include an upgrade button that opens the Excalidraw+ page in a new tab.

The diagram preview error state is redesigned: instead of an 'Error!' line showing the raw message with the canvas dimmed to 15% opacity, errors now show a warning icon, a translated error title, and either the underlying error text or, where details are hidden, a generic invalid-syntax message, with the preview canvas hidden entirely.

The dialog panel's footer now renders multiple actions in three styles (regular button, link-style button, and a non-clickable rate-limit text), supports configurable alignment, shows the submit shortcut hint whenever generation is not in progress (previously it was also hidden when the action was disabled), and hides the action row on panels without actions.

New saved-chat history for the text-to-diagram chat persists to browser storage automatically: only the 10 most recent chats are kept, saving is skipped when there is no user message with content, only user and assistant messages are stored, and unreadable storage falls back to an empty history.

Chat titles come from the first user message and are kept in full up to 50 characters, otherwise truncated to the first 47 characters followed by '...'; a chat's recency timestamp only updates when its messages actually change, so re-saving an unchanged chat keeps its position.
Starting a new chat or restoring a saved chat saves the current chat first, and deleting a chat removes it from both the list and storage.

Chat menu actions in the Text-to-diagram dialog now run through a single hook: starting a new chat clears the conversation, the prompt box, and any shown error, and restoring a saved chat reloads its messages, empties the prompt box, closes the menu, and re-shows the assistant's error only if that chat's last assistant reply ended in one.

Deleting a saved chat that is not the open one leaves the open conversation untouched, while deleting the open chat switches to the most recent remaining saved chat or, when none are left, to a fresh empty chat.

Conversations auto-save once a response finishes generating or the message list changes, are titled from the first user prompt, and only the 10 most recent are kept; empty conversations and ones whose first user message has no text are never saved.

While the AI response is still streaming, the diagram preview updates on an adaptive throttle that holds back incomplete Mermaid syntax and renders the final pending content when generation completes; switching between saved chats re-renders the last diagram, and a chat with no assistant replies clears the preview.

Text-to-diagram generation now calls the streaming chat endpoint /v1/ai/text-to-diagram/chat-streaming through a shared streaming helper instead of the previous one-shot /v1/ai/text-to-diagram/generate JSON request: the prompt is sent as chat messages, the diagram preview is built from streamed chunks as they arrive, and the request carries an abort signal.

Failure handling changed: a 429 rate-limit response now reports 'Rate limit exceeded' (previously 'Too many requests today, please try again tomorrow!'), other failures now surface the backend's response text or 'Generation failed...' instead of the previous generic 'Request failed', and the X-Ratelimit-Limit and X-Ratelimit-Remaining headers are read when the backend sends them.

The dialog's public contract changed: its text-submit callback now receives a streaming options object (chat messages, per-chunk callback, stream-created callback, abort signal) instead of a plain prompt string, a new optional warning prop was added, and the dialog shell's internal prompt-change handler and generate routine were removed, so prompt input and generation are now driven by the dialog's text-to-diagram content; this is a breaking change for integrators using the old string signature.

The Mermaid syntax validator used to gate the preview changed: text with unbalanced brackets, braces, or parentheses, or a last line ending in an incomplete token such as '-->', ':', or '|', is treated as incomplete and the preview withholds rendering until the syntax is finished.

The package entry point was updated alongside the new streaming helper and error classes, and the Next.js example wrapper is a downstream consumer of the package, so the embeddable package should still load and render the editor unchanged.

Mermaid conversion in the text-to-diagram dialog now reports success or failure as a return value that callers display, instead of throwing, so invalid definitions, empty text, and render failures surface as in-dialog errors rather than uncaught exceptions.
Dark-mode Mermaid previews now follow the editor theme passed to conversion instead of reading a CSS class from the page, so theme mismatch in the preview is a new risk.
Conversion no longer runs the canvas-size check that showed the canvas-too-big message, so extremely large diagrams no longer get that specific error.

The shared modal shell behind every dialog (share, help, image and JSON export, confirmations, errors, library publishing, paste chart, text-to-diagram, overwrite confirm) no longer carries the marker that told outside-click handling to ignore clicks inside the modal.

The command palette's clock glyph was renamed to the history command icon with identical artwork, the font code icon was redrawn as a different angle-bracket glyph, new retry, stack, and history icons were added, the button component gained a disabled prop (type-level only), and text-to-diagram state and its preview panel moved into new modules with no intended behavior change.

Prompts in the text-to-diagram chat must be 3 to 10,000 characters: shorter or longer input is rejected before any request with a too-short or too-long error, and when the remaining rate limit is 0, generation is blocked before anything is sent.

Each generate appends the user's prompt plus an empty 'generating' reply that fills in as the response streams; only the last 3 prior messages are sent as context, and starting a new generation or aborting cancels the in-flight stream silently, leaving any partial reply in place but stopped.

A rate-limited rejection (HTTP 429) removes the failed reply and shows a warning instead — the message-limit variant when no requests remain, otherwise the rate-limit variant; other failures with 0 remaining also add the message-limit warning on top of the error on the reply.

Error text is now human-readable: nested-JSON backend errors display only their inner messages (plain-text errors pass through unchanged), a generated diagram that fails Mermaid parsing shows a parse error on the reply, and retrying after a network failure reuses the same reply bubble rather than adding a new one.
In the app build, the Mermaid conversion library is now bundled as its own named chunk and the service-worker precache size limit was raised to 2.3MB per file.

Typing a prompt in the new text-to-diagram chat appends the user message plus an empty assistant placeholder, each given a fresh id and timestamp, and the generated description streams into that assistant reply as it arrives.

The chat history menu lets users start a new chat, restore a saved chat with its messages reloaded, and delete a chat, where deleting the active chat switches to the newest remaining chat or an empty session.

The latest assistant reply shows retry after a five-second cooldown since the last attempt, alongside insert-to-canvas, Mermaid view, AI repair, and delete actions, with errors displayed on the message.

The Mermaid preview renders the latest assistant reply with throttled rendering that starts fast at 300 ms, slows to 3000 ms after slow renders, and pauses 100 ms after parse failures, updating as streamed content changes.
Follow-up generation requests now include only non-empty user and assistant messages as conversation context, so empty streaming placeholders are left out of what is sent.

The text-to-diagram tab is now a chat: prompts and replies persist as a conversation with retry, AI repair, abort, per-message insert and delete, saved-chat restore, and a toggleable preview panel, replacing the old single prompt-and-preview layout that blocked generation past 1000 characters and showed 'N requests left today' rate limits.

The Mermaid tab renders its preview only while that tab is active, re-renders when the app's light/dark theme changes, clears the preview when the input is emptied, and now shows a parse error in the preview panel when Mermaid text is invalid; previously a failed parse could leave the stale preview with no error.

Inserting a chat message converts that message's Mermaid text and adds the diagram to the canvas only when conversion succeeds, and viewing a response as Mermaid saves it and reopens the dialog on the Mermaid tab preloaded with that content.

Hardcoded dialog strings (the 'Write Mermaid diagram defintion here...' placeholder, the Mermaid tab label, the 'AI Beta' badge) became translation keys that render blank in production if missing, the dialog widened from 1200 to 1520, and its section labels were replaced by a standard button action.

Check a prompt that yields invalid Mermaid: the reply ends with a parse error rather than succeeding silently.

Verify while a response is streaming, the send control becomes a stop action and clicking it aborts generation without leaving the message stuck in a generating state.
Verify a failed reply shows its error and a retry control that becomes available once five seconds have passed since the last attempt, so consecutive retries are blocked until the cooldown ends.

Verify that sending a short prompt adds your message and an assistant reply to the conversation, and that inserting the resulting preview adds the diagram to the canvas and closes the dialog.

The evidence does not establish which dialog surfaces hide the underlying error details behind the generic invalid-syntax message, so the expected message wording per surface should be confirmed during testing; regardless of variant, a blank error title or message (possible where a language lacks the new error texts) is a defect.

Every changed function in this group shows only added code, meaning the logic appears newly extracted into hooks, so no input could be identified that the previous code handled differently; the checks above verify boundary cases of the current behavior, and exact navigation steps and on-screen labels for the Text-to-diagram dialog were not supplied, so QA must locate them in the UI.

Generation now depends on a backend that serves the streaming chat endpoint as an event stream — the previous one-shot endpoint is no longer called — so if that backend change is not deployed the workflow fails with an unchanged UI; the supplied diffs also cover only the app-side switch and the dialog contract, so the checks for the streaming helper's internals, Mermaid validation, and the error classes verify current behavior rather than confirmed regressions.

The consumer of the removed modal click-guard marker is not in the supplied evidence, so the real effect on inside-click handling is unproven; watch for nested menus or popovers inside dialogs closing or failing to close differently than before.

No navigation path, screen names, or on-screen wording for this dialog was supplied (the context lists no affected areas), so the tester must locate the text-to-diagram dialog themselves and the checks above assert behavior rather than exact text; because these dialog files arrive as new or moved code with no prior version in this diff, the sharp boundaries (exactly 3 and 10,000 characters) are the most important regression probes.

Exact visible labels for the retry cooldown, remaining message count, and message action controls are not supplied in the application context, so testers should locate them by icon and tooltip within the dialog rather than expected wording.

Deleting a reply is expected to remove that reply plus the prompt before it, but the cut is located by matching the reply's identifier; if the delete control ever targets a prompt or an unknown message, the conversation would instead lose its last two messages, so confirm delete is only offered on assistant replies.
