report.summary: This release improves how keyboard-created flowchart shapes are placed so they avoid overlapping and stack neatly, while reorganizing the underlying flowchart handling behind the scenes with all existing keyboard behavior, including undo and redo, expected to work exactly as before.
keyChanges: Creating connected shapes with Ctrl or Cmd plus arrow keys, navigating between connected shapes with Alt plus arrow keys, cancelling with Escape, and committing pending shapes when a modifier is released all moved from the main editor into a new flowchart controller; the relocated logic reads as like-for-like, so the risk is subtle regressions rather than intended changes.

The automatic pan that brings a new or newly selected node into view (about a 300 ms animated pan, only when the node is fully outside the visible canvas) was reimplemented as one shared helper now used by creation, commit, and navigation alike — the most fragile part of the move.

Keyboard events now route through the flowchart controller first and reach other shortcuts only when it reports the key as not handled, so untouched shortcuts such as unmodified arrow-key nudging, Escape closing the shape type-conversion popup, and Enter starting image cropping must still fall through correctly.

Two internal helpers for inserting elements into the drawing and forcing a canvas re-render were made callable from the new controller; no behavior change is intended, and the same insertion path also serves pasting, drag-and-drop, image insertion, and existing automated suites for selection, lasso, laser, and tool flows.

Creating a linked flowchart node by holding Ctrl/Cmd and pressing an arrow key no longer stacks new nodes in a fixed, evenly distributed grid that could sit on top of existing shapes: new nodes now steer to the nearest free spot with at least one gap of clearance from shapes connected to the starting shape, while shapes not connected to it are still not avoided.

Repeated presses of the same arrow while holding Ctrl/Cmd grow the cluster by exactly one node per press without moving the earlier previewed nodes, because the cluster's cross-axis anchor is remembered between presses; switching direction, pressing Escape, or releasing Ctrl/Cmd clears that anchor so the next cluster starts centered on the selected shape.

Each new node is cloned from the selected shape's size and style and gets a connecting arrow bound at both ends, and because placement changed, whether created nodes join a frame now depends on the new positions.

The lookup that decides which node Alt+arrow jumps to was rebuilt as new internal helpers; behavior should be identical, but since the old lookup code is not in the supplied diff it needs a smoke test, and note that creation and navigation share the same keyboard handling path.

New flowchart nodes created with arrow keys are now placed as a group a 100 px gap away from the selected node in the pressed direction and slide along the cross axis into the nearest free slot; the entire connected flowchart, not just directly linked neighbors, is treated as obstacles, so new nodes should no longer overlap other parts of the same flowchart (overlap bug #8518; the old behavior alternated positions in a zig-zag around immediate neighbors only).

Growing a pending cluster by repeating the same arrow key now anchors the already-visible pending nodes in place and extends at either end, relocating the whole group only when it no longer fits; previously pending nodes were repositioned every time the count changed.

The built-in fallback direction to the right and the initial right direction were removed, so creation now starts only from an explicit arrow key and no node should silently appear to the right when no arrow key was pressed.

When two free slots are equally near, placement resolves toward the positive side (down or right), and obstacles touching each other are merged so new nodes keep at least one full gap of clearance instead of squeezing between them.

The detection of which neighboring nodes lie in each direction was rewritten together with creation, and keyboard navigation between flowchart nodes shares this logic, so navigation needs a regression pass.

The flowchart feature's internal state handling was moved out of the main editor into a dedicated flowchart controller, replacing the previously separate creation and navigation helpers; this is a restructuring with no intended behavior change.

Undo and redo now read the flowchart-creation-in-progress state through the new controller, so undo/redo must remain suppressed while a flowchart is actively being created and work normally at all other times.

The on-canvas preview of pending, not-yet-committed flowchart nodes is now fed through the new controller, so keyboard-driven flowchart creation, node navigation, and scroll-into-view should look and behave exactly as before.
qaChecks: Verify selecting one shape, holding Ctrl or Cmd, and pressing an arrow key adds a connected shape in that direction and, when the new shape is fully outside the visible canvas, the view pans to it with a short (about 300 ms) animation.

Verify holding Ctrl or Cmd and pressing two arrow keys in sequence (for example down then right) builds a chain of pending connected shapes, and releasing the modifier inserts them all with the first pending shape selected.
Verify pressing Escape while a chain of pending shapes is not yet committed discards it so the drawing stays unchanged.

Verify with exactly one shape selected, holding Alt and pressing an arrow key moves the selection to the connected neighbor in that direction and pans the view to reveal it when it is fully off-screen.
Verify holding Alt and pressing an arrow key where no connected neighbor exists leaves the selection unchanged with no error.
Verify releasing Alt finalizes the navigation session so a later Alt plus arrow sequence starts cleanly from the currently selected shape.
Verify arrow keys without Ctrl, Cmd, or Alt still nudge the selected shapes instead of starting a flowchart chain.
Verify Escape without active flowchart creation still closes the shape type-conversion popup or clears the selection as before.

Verify that when a connected shape already occupies the band beside the selected shape in the pressed direction, the previewed new node lands in the nearest free spot perpendicular to that direction with a visible gap instead of overlapping the existing shape, which is where the old fixed grid placed it.

Confirm that holding Ctrl/Cmd and tapping the same arrow key three times grows the preview to exactly three new nodes with three connecting arrows and that the first two nodes keep their positions while the third is added rather than the whole cluster re-centering.
Ensure the very first press in a direction places its single new node aligned with the selected shape's row (for left/right) or column (for up/down) when the nearby area is free.
Ensure new nodes created from a shape inside a frame still join that frame when every created node fits within or overlaps it.
Verify pressing Escape while preview nodes are showing removes all preview nodes and arrows immediately and creates nothing.

Ensure that after Escape, or after committing by releasing Ctrl/Cmd, the next creation in any direction starts with a single node centered on the selected shape instead of resuming the previous cluster's offset.
Ensure every created node is joined by a connecting arrow that stays attached at both ends and re-routes to follow when either the original or the new node is dragged around the canvas.

Verify holding Alt and pressing an arrow key moves the selection to the connected node in that direction, and that repeating the same key cycles through several connected nodes at the same level instead of getting stuck on the first one.
Ensure navigation works on the arrows produced by the creation feature: from a node created with Ctrl/Cmd plus an arrow key, Alt plus an arrow key selects its connected neighbor.

Verify pressing each arrow key (up, right, down, left) with a flowchart node selected creates exactly one connected node one 100 px gap away in that direction, keeping the selected node's size and style.

Verify with a grandchild node of the same connected flowchart occupying the space to the right of the selected node, pressing the right arrow places the new node in the nearest free slot without overlapping any connected node (the old build overlapped here).
Verify when free slots above and below, or left and right, are equally near, the new node is placed on the positive side (below or to the right).
Verify with two existing connected nodes touching edge-to-edge inside the target band, the new node lands with at least one full gap of clearance rather than inside the seam.

Verify repeating the same arrow key to grow the pending cluster from one to three nodes keeps the first pending node exactly where it appeared while new nodes are added at either end, all one gap apart.
Verify when the grown cluster no longer fits in its anchored slot because an obstacle blocks it, the whole pending group relocates together to the nearest free slot.
Verify starting the flowchart creation flow without pressing an arrow key creates no node (the old default silently placed new nodes to the right).
Confirm pressing Up creates the node above and not to the right, and each arrow key maps to its own direction on the first use of the feature.
Verify arrow-key navigation still moves the selection to the node connected in the pressed direction and never to a node on a different side of the selected node.
Verify navigation works when a node has connected neighbors on multiple sides at once.
Verify that with a shape selected you start keyboard-driven flowchart creation by pressing an arrow key, and that pressing Ctrl/Cmd+Z while creation is still in progress does not undo any step.
Ensure that after finishing or canceling the flowchart creation, Ctrl/Cmd+Z undoes the most recent change and Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+Z or Ctrl/Cmd+Y redoes it.

Check that the toolbar undo and redo buttons perform the same undo and redo as the shortcuts, and that each button is disabled when its history stack is empty, for example redo immediately after opening a drawing with no changes.

Confirm that pressing an arrow key with a node selected shows the connected pending node on the canvas immediately, and that confirming the creation turns it into a normal, selectable element that undo can remove.
Confirm that moving between connected nodes with the keyboard selects the target node and scrolls it into view, including pending nodes that are not yet committed.
Ensure that canceling the creation mid-way clears the pending preview without adding any elements to the drawing.
uncertainty: No specific input was identified that the old and new versions treat differently, as the diff shows the keyboard logic moved essentially unchanged; the residual risk is concentrated in the reimplemented pan-to-reveal helper and in the rare case where Alt navigation and Ctrl or Cmd creation both finalize on the same key release, so exercise both on a connected chain.

The neighbor lookup behind Alt+arrow navigation was replaced with new code whose previous version is not included in the supplied changes, so identical behavior cannot be confirmed from the evidence; treat the navigation checks as a comparison against the previous release and report any difference in which node gets selected rather than assuming it is intentional.

The direction-based neighbor detection used by keyboard navigation was rewritten with no documented rule for its expected behavior, so whether navigation should behave exactly as before is unresolved; if navigation misroutes to a wrong-side neighbor, confirm with the team whether that change is intentional.

The editor previously exposed the flowchart creation helper as a public class property, and that property is now replaced by the single controller in the editor's public property list; any external embedded integration that read or set the old property could break, but the supplied context includes no such integration surface to test against.

report.summary: This release reworks how elements join, stack, and highlight inside drawing frames, so frame behavior on the canvas needs a focused testing pass.
keyChanges: Arrow binding now treats only element types that support background fills as blockers, so dragging an arrow endpoint over a frame can reach the smaller shape underneath and bind to it instead of sticking to the frame.

Clicking, dragging, and erasing from an element's interior now apply only to element types that actually offer a background fill, for example frames with an opaque background no longer respond when you click inside their body and must be grabbed by their border or title instead.
Deselecting and finishing a draw or drag now explicitly clear the highlighted frame, so the frame highlight no longer lingers after pressing Escape, clicking empty canvas, or completing an action.
Older browsers that lack the newer built-in array helper methods now receive built-in fallbacks so the editor keeps working there, while modern browsers are unchanged.

When elements are added to a frame by dragging, dropping, pasting, or wrapping a selection, they are now actively reordered to sit just below the frame or just above its highest existing child, and elements already inside that frame are included in that reorder instead of being skipped; elements that still belong to a different frame are no longer pulled into the target frame.

Scene insertion was consolidated: the explicit insert-at-index and batch-insert helpers were removed and the remaining routine now treats a null index as append-at-end, so all creation flows (drawing shapes and freehand strokes, text, images, embeddables, iframes, new frames) go through one path; inserting at a negative index still raises an error.

Flows that replace a frame's contents, such as resizing a frame or ungrouping elements inside it, now also normalize the frame's children to sit directly before the frame in stacking order, which can subtly change layering inside frames.
While dragging a selection over a frame, the live layering preview no longer reorders the selection when every dragged element already belongs to that frame.

Adding new elements to frames is now decided by what is actually under the cursor: a new shape drawn over an element that covers a frame without belonging to it no longer joins that frame, while shapes drawn over empty frame area or over frame members still join the frame.

While dragging a selection, the frame the selected elements belong to stays highlighted even when the cursor crosses overlapping elements, a selection containing a frame highlights nothing, and switching tools now clears any leftover frame highlight.

Creating shapes, frames, freehand strokes, arrows, and embeddable links now goes through one shared insertion step that also refreshes the frame highlight, so a frame shows highlighted right after you draw something into it.

Text editing changes: text binding inside frames no longer gets blocked by the frame itself, and text bound to a shape only joins a frame when that shape is itself a frame member; the frame for new text is now determined from the text's final position rather than the raw click point.

Inserting or dropping library items that contain frames now keeps the original stacking order of the frame's contents in the copies; duplicating selected elements uses the unchanged in-place path and needs only a regression check.

Text pasted onto the canvas is now inserted frame-aware, so lines pasted over a frame become children of that frame placed right after its existing children instead of being appended on top of the entire scene.

Element insertion from paste, drop, and the library now applies the frame-assignment result to the scene and supports preserving the stacking order of children when duplicating frames, which the library drop path uses.

Frame highlighting on pointer move is now suppressed while an element is being created, dragged, or selected, and otherwise still refreshes on plain hovering even with tools that cannot create frame children.
Dropping a single PNG or SVG file that fails to load as a scene now falls back to inserting it as a regular image, while other load failures still show the invalid-file alert.

When a frame is resized from the Stats panel, the step that recomputes which elements belong to the frame now calls the frame-membership helper with three inputs instead of four, no longer passing the app object; both the single-element and multi-selection resize paths were updated, so elements joining or leaving a frame after a Stats-panel resize must still be recomputed correctly.

Both canvas layers — the one painting the drawing content and the one painting interactive feedback such as selection — now decide whether to repaint by comparing a required string canvas nonce instead of an optional numeric scene nonce; the comparison logic is otherwise unchanged and still also compares the element collections directly, so repaints should still happen even when the nonce value stays the same.

While elements are being dragged over a highlighted frame, they are now visually reordered into that frame's stacking order during the drag itself, before release; when every dragged element already belongs to that same frame, no reorder happens.

An element being newly created inside a frame is now drawn as part of the frame's normal element order on the main canvas instead of on the separate in-progress overlay canvas, which now receives the in-progress element through a dedicated prop; elements created outside frames keep the previous overlay behavior.

The underlying visible-element computation was restructured into cached steps with a new cache key based on scene state plus the in-progress element's version when it belongs to a frame, and editor teardown now clears the renamed cache; existing frame rendering tests cover this path, and any caching mistake would surface as missing, duplicated, or stale elements while panning, zooming, or remounting.

When finishing a drag on the canvas, the frame a selection is dropped onto is now resolved differently: the frame the selected elements already share is excluded as a target, selected elements themselves cannot be treated as the target frame, and the filter deciding which elements join the frame no longer skips elements already assigned to that frame. This changes which frame (if any) receives the selection on pointer release.

Newly created freehand strokes, lines/arrows, embedded iframes, and magic frames are now inserted through a shared insertion path that also updates frame highlighting, so drawing inside a frame can now visibly highlight that frame where it previously did not.

Inserting a library item is changed to preserve the order of frame children when the item is duplicated onto the canvas, so frames inside library items should land with the same child stacking order as saved.
Flowchart nodes committed via keyboard now go through the same shared insertion path instead of a direct scene insert.

An internal helper that computed which elements are visible in the canvas viewport was removed from its old location with no replacement visible in the evidence, so canvas rendering of elements when panning and zooming needs a smoke check.

uncertainty: The exact list of element types counted as supporting a background fill was not supplied, so other stored background colors, such as those kept on arrows by older files, may also change which element is grabbed, erased, or bound.

Moving an element from one frame to another is the highest residual risk: the old logic moved elements into the target frame unless the element and its own frame were both selected, while the new logic never takes elements that still belong to a different frame, so a frame-to-frame move now depends on the original membership being cleared earlier during the drag; if elements stay behind in the original frame, that is the regression to report.

Whether ordinary clipboard copy and paste of frames also preserves the frame's content order like library insertion now does is not established by the evidence; compare paste results against the previous build when testing.

Most changed functions in this group were supplied without before and after code, so the checks verify current behavior; the provable old-versus-new divergences are frame-aware insertion for pasted text and preserved stacking order when duplicating frame children, and other regressions inside these functions may not be directly targeted.

The evidence does not show how the new string canvas nonce is produced or how often it changes compared with the old numeric scene nonce; if an edit no longer updates it, the visible symptom would be a canvas that keeps showing pre-edit content until another interaction, which the first test area targets.
The application context supplied no affected areas or navigation paths for these canvas changes, so all navigation guidance is generic and testers must locate the main editor canvas themselves.

No navigation routes, menus, or surfaces were supplied for any of these areas, so testers must reach them through the general editor canvas and Library panel, and the removal of the viewport visibility helper left no evidence of where that computation now lives, so a rendering regression there cannot be localized further.

report.summary: This release reworks how the server tool launches and how its web API stores, filters, looks up, and identifies records, so everyday startup and data-handling behavior needs retesting.
keyChanges: Starting the tool with a .json data file that does not exist now warns and creates that file pre-filled with built-in sample data before serving it, while a missing .js source still fails as before.

If the data source cannot be turned into the API at startup, for example a .json file with invalid content, the tool now prints the error in red and exits with a failure status instead of crashing with an unhandled stack trace.

Watch mode now uses the runtime's built-in file watcher instead of the previous watching library: data-file changes still restart the server (a .json file only when its contents actually changed, a .js file always), the reload message now names the data file as given on the command line instead of the exact changed file path, and the routes file is watched via its folder with reloads limited to that file.

The remaining edits in this group — the startup banner listing resource URLs, internal detection of .json/.js/URL sources, and how JSON, JavaScript, and remote URL sources are loaded — are internal refactoring with no intended behavior change.

List filtering now skips any item whose filtered field is empty, zero, or false, so filtering by those values that previously returned items now returns nothing, and range and equality comparisons work on text rather than converted native types, so string-stored numbers can rank alphabetically.

Creating and updating items no longer auto-converts submitted values: numeric strings like "10" and "true" are stored exactly as sent, whereas they were previously stored as real numbers and booleans.
Fetching a single item and deleting it now use the raw request ID without conversion, so items whose stored ID is a number must still be found; deleting still also removes dependent child records.

Pagination links are now built with the system URL formatter instead of string concatenation, and the server's command-line entry point now loads the built library instead of the source, so server startup itself must still work.

Request-body parsing (JSON bodies up to 10MB and form-encoded bodies) plus method overriding moved from server-wide default middlewares into the API router itself, keeping the same parser settings; if this wiring is wrong, every create or update request fails, so all write requests need retesting.
New records added to collections whose ids are strings now receive a short generated code instead of a 36-character UUID; collections with numeric ids still get the next consecutive number.
The server now validates the database contents when it loads, so a database file that previously started the server could now stop startup with an error instead of serving malformed data.

The full-database read endpoint (GET /db) was rewritten inline with no intended behavior change, and default middlewares such as compression, logging, CORS, no-cache headers and read-only mode are unchanged apart from no longer carrying body parsing.

Nested child-resource reads and creates no longer convert the parent identifier from the URL into a native value, so an identifier such as 1 now reaches the query string or request body as the text '1' instead of the number 1.
Server startup now rejects a database whose top level is not a plain object or whose property names contain a slash character, failing fast with descriptive error messages.

The route rewriter and the singular-resource router were rewritten in newer declaration syntax with no intended behavior change, and an internal helper that recognized file paths ending in .json was removed with no other dependents found in the code graph.

A brand-new command-line entry point was added whose only job is to immediately start the main command-line routine, so the genuinely new behavior is that the json-server command should launch, show its usage, and parse options as documented.

The main startup module was rewritten with the same declarations in the current language style and now passes the same package-information object to the version-update check in shorthand form, which should not change any observable behavior such as option defaults or the update notification.
No dependents of either change were found and no application areas were supplied, so the QA impact is limited to launching and driving the command-line tool from a terminal.
qaChecks: Verify that starting with a .json filename that does not exist, such as a brand-new name, prints two yellow messages saying the file doesn't seem to exist and is being created with default data, creates that file with sample content, and starts serving the sample resources.

Verify that starting with a .json file containing invalid JSON (for example a file holding only the text not json) prints an indented red error and exits with a failure status instead of a raw crash stack.
Verify that starting with a .js filename that does not exist still fails without creating any file, confirming automatic creation applies only to .json sources.

Verify that editing and saving the data file with changed content — including a save style that replaces the file, as many editors do — logs a reload message naming the data file and the API then returns the updated data.

Confirm that creating or updating data through the API, which makes the tool rewrite the data file itself, does not trigger a reload or stop the server, since the on-disk content matches the in-memory data.
Verify that rapid consecutive saves of the data file still leave the server running the latest content without crashing.
Verify that editing and saving only the routes file, including editor saves that replace the file, logs a reload message and the remapped path follows the new mapping after the restart.
Verify that changing another file in the same folder as the routes file does not trigger a reload.
Verify that each of the three source types starts successfully and prints the startup banner listing resource URLs and the home address, confirming the loading refactor kept all source types working.
Verify filtering the list by a zero value (for example views=0) still returns the item with 0, because this is the input the old filter kept and the new filter silently drops.
Verify filtering by a false boolean (for example published=false) still returns the unpublished items instead of an empty list.
Verify a range filter with zero as the boundary (for example views_gte=0) includes items with 0, and that ordinary filters for positive numbers and text still return the expected items.
Verify that creating an item with values sent as text (for example "10" or "true") stores and echoes them exactly as sent, since the automatic conversion to real numbers and booleans was removed.
Verify that after creating an item whose number was sent as a string, a range filter on that field still ranks it numerically (for example the item still appears for field_gte=9), not alphabetically.
Verify that PATCH and PUT on an item with a numeric stored ID still find and update it, and the response echoes the saved record.
Verify fetching a single item by its numeric ID still returns it, and requested related records are still embedded in or expanded onto the response.
Verify deleting an item by its numeric ID still removes it, and its dependent child records are still cleaned up in the same request.
Verify that paginating returns first, previous, next, and last links that still contain the correct protocol, host, and original query, comparing against the address used for the request.
Verify the server still starts from its command-line entry point and serves the database without a startup error, since the entry now loads built output instead of source.
Verify a POST with a small JSON body to a collection endpoint creates a record whose stored fields match the body, since JSON body parsing now lives inside the API router.
Verify a POST with a form-encoded (urlencoded) body is still parsed and saved the same way as before the reorganization.
Confirm a JSON body just over 10MB is still rejected with the same too-large error as before, proving the preserved size limit still applies from its new position.
Confirm a POST carrying an X-HTTP-Method-Override header (for example overriding to DELETE) still performs the overridden operation.
Test creating a record in the numeric-id collection and confirm the new id is the existing maximum plus one, matching previous behavior.

Test creating a record in the string-id collection and confirm the returned id is now a short generated code (previously a 36-character UUID), then confirm GET, PUT and DELETE using that id in the URL still work.
Validate that a database file that loaded before this change still starts the server and serves its collections normally.

Check startup with loosely structured data (a collection whose entries are not plain objects) and confirm the server either starts as before or fails immediately with a clear validation error rather than serving malformed responses.
Confirm GET /db still returns the complete database state with all collections in the same JSON(P) format as before, since its handler was rewritten.

Verify GET /posts/1/comments still returns exactly the child records that belong to the parent with identifier 1, because the identifier now travels as the text '1' where it used to be converted to the number 1.

Verify POST /posts/1/comments with a JSON body creates a child record whose parent link can still be found by later filtered reads, checking whether that link is now stored as the text '1' instead of the number 1.
Verify GET /posts/true/comments behaves consistently with prior releases, since the word true used to arrive as the boolean true and now arrives as text.
Verify startup with a database file whose top level is an array rather than an object fails fast with the error message stating that data must be an object.
Verify startup with a database property name containing a slash fails fast with the error message that names the offending property.
Verify startup with a normal database file in the standard .json format still loads and serves records, confirming that the removed .json-path recognition did not change how data files are loaded.
Verify a rewritten route with a URL parameter (for example one containing :id) still returns the rewritten target and populates the query string exactly as before the refactor.
Verify a prefix-style rewrite without parameters still rewrites matching requests, including one whose target contains a query string.
Verify reading, creating, and updating the singular resource still store and return the value exactly as before the refactor.
Verify the command launches after a clean install or build by running it against a small sample JSON data file, and confirm the server starts and answers a basic request on the default port 3000.
Check that running the command with no arguments shows the usage text and the options list rather than an unhandled crash, since this exercises the new launcher immediately invoking the main routine.

Check that core option handling is intact in one or two runs: -p 3001 moves the listening port, --read-only allows GET requests but refuses writes such as POST, and a custom config file passed with -c applies its settings instead of the defaults.
uncertainty: The watcher replacement may behave differently by operating system and save style: some platforms report changed-file names unreliably, and the tool's own atomic rewrites of the data file are exactly the events the new watcher must classify, so a missed reload, a duplicate reload, or a crash during watch mode is the most likely regression; report the OS, the editor save style, and the action that preceded it.

Whether items whose stored ID is a number are still matched once the raw text ID from the request is used could not be confirmed from the supplied evidence; the single-item fetch, update, and delete checks above are the ones that would expose it.

The exact rules of the new startup data validation are not part of this evidence, so a database file that previously started could now be rejected at launch; if any new startup failure appears, capture the error message and the data that triggers it.

When stored parent identifiers are numbers, the nested-route lookups now compare text against numbers and may return no results, and the evidence does not reveal every consumer of the removed conversion to confirm the full reach of this change.

No input handled differently before and after was identified because the startup edits are syntax-only and the launcher file is newly added, so the main open risk is whether the installed command is actually wired to the new launcher, which would surface as the command not starting at all.

Verify that starting with a .js filename that does not exist still fails without creating any file, confirming automatic creation applies only to .json sources.

testAreas.howToReach: From a terminal, start the json-server command with a valid .json data file and the watch option enabled; no screens were supplied.

checks: Verify that editing and saving the data file with changed content — including a save style that replaces the file, as many editors do — logs a reload message naming the data file and the API then returns the updated data.

testAreas.area: Nested child-resource API routes
testAreas.howToReach: No navigation steps were found in the application context; send GET and POST requests to a nested route of the form /:resource/:id/:nested, for example /posts/1/comments, on the running server.

testAreas.setup: A running server instance whose database contains a parent resource with nested child records and numeric identifiers.
checks: Verify GET /posts/1/comments still returns exactly the child records that belong to the parent with identifier 1, because the identifier now travels as the text '1' where it used to be converted to the number 1.

Verify GET /posts/true/comments behaves consistently with prior releases, since the word true used to arrive as the boolean true and now arrives as text.

testAreas.area: Server startup and data validation
testAreas.howToReach: No navigation steps were found in the application context; start the server from the command line pointing at a database file.
testAreas.access: Developer or operator starting the server.
testAreas.setup: Three database fixtures: a normal one, one whose top level is an array rather than an object, and one with a property name containing a slash, the kind of key that appears when data is copied from other sources.
checks: Verify startup with a database file whose top level is an array rather than an object fails fast with the error message stating that data must be an object.
Verify startup with a database property name containing a slash fails fast with the error message that names the offending property.
Verify startup with a normal database file in the standard .json format still loads and serves records, confirming that the removed .json-path recognition did not change how data files are loaded.

testAreas.area: Custom route rewriting
testAreas.howToReach: No navigation steps were found in the application context; configure custom rewrite routes when starting the server and request them against the running instance.
testAreas.setup: A server started with rewrite rules covering both a parameterized route and a plain prefix rewrite.
checks: Verify a rewritten route with a URL parameter (for example one containing :id) still returns the rewritten target and populates the query string exactly as before the refactor.
Verify a prefix-style rewrite without parameters still rewrites matching requests, including one whose target contains a query string.

testAreas.area: Singular resource routes
testAreas.howToReach: No navigation steps were found in the application context; send GET, POST, PUT, and PATCH requests to the configured singular resource path on the running server.
testAreas.setup: A database containing a singular resource such as a single profile object.
checks: Verify reading, creating, and updating the singular resource still store and return the value exactly as before the refactor.

testAreas.area: json-server command-line tool
testAreas.howToReach: No navigation steps were supplied for this repository, so reach this feature from a terminal by running the project's command-line executable with a data source file.
testAreas.access: Anyone who can run commands in a terminal, since no user roles were supplied.
testAreas.setup: A small JSON data source file to serve, and optionally a custom config file to pass with the config option.
checks: Verify the command launches after a clean install or build by running it against a small sample JSON data file, and confirm the server starts and answers a basic request on the default port 3000.
Check that running the command with no arguments shows the usage text and the options list rather than an unhandled crash, since this exercises the new launcher immediately invoking the main routine.

Check that core option handling is intact in one or two runs: -p 3001 moves the listening port, --read-only allows GET requests but refuses writes such as POST, and a custom config file passed with -c applies its settings instead of the defaults.
